author: balpha
body:
I created the controller builder so that there's a typesafe, single-source-of-truth way to create Stimulus controllers without error-prone `declare`s and copy&pastes, which is the Stimulus-recommended way of doing things when working with TypeScript.

I was looking around at the many uses of the controller builder in our codebase, and I noticed that the single most often encountered shortfall of the typings is the fact that targets are always typed as `HTMLElement`, so people often had to resort to type assertions like

```ts
(this.myButtonTarget as HTMLButtonElement).disabled = false;
```

This changeset makes it possible to (optionally) specify the element type at definition time, like this:

```ts
.withTargets("myButton")<HTMLButtonElement>()
```

Yes, I agree that this syntax looks slightly weird, and I've debated many different approaches before I settled on this. I think it's intuitively clear from reading it what's happening.

The most obvious solution would have been this:

```ts
.withTargets<HTMLButtonElement>("myButton")
```

but unfortunately this doesn't work, because Typescript does not allow partial type argument inference, and `withTargets` needs to infer the target name types. I didn't want to force the user to duplicate them with something like

```ts
.withTargets<HTMLFormElement, "myForm" | "myOtherForm">("myForm", "myOtherForm")
```

because that is much less readable.

I also considered (and actually originally implemented) a method called `ofTargetElementType` that you could directly chain behind a `withTargets` call. This is very similar to the solution I ultimately went with, but it has the disadvantage that Prettier will move it to the next line:

```ts
... = buildController("something-or-other")
    .withTargets("foo")
    .ofTargetElementType<HTMLCanvasElement>()
    .withClasses("bar")
    ...
```

and that makes it much less obvious to the reader of the code that the two belong tightly together.

Finally, this would also have been possible:

```ts
.withTargets<HTMLButtonElement>()("myButton")
```

but this doesn't feel any more elegant than my chosen solution, and it has the disadvantage that you would either need two different functions (`.withTargets` and `.withTargetsOfType`), or add additional complexity from added overload behavior of `withTargets()`.

That's why I went with what I went with.

I also added a couple of unit tests to verify the runtime behavior of the controller builder. There has always been an extensive "test suite" of the *typings*, and they are clearly the more complex piece of the puzzle. But especially with the added complexity of `.withTargets()`, including additions to the runtime behavior, I felt I should also add some validation that the builder actually builds controller classes as expected.
title: controller builder: allow narrowing the element types of targets

body: ## Summary [**Jira** ](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/jira/software/c/projects/YETI2/boards/411?selectedIssue=YETI2-698) An alternative and simpler implementation of https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23336. This PR adds some new rules around paginating the `/questions` and `/content-feeds/comments` endpoints. The final values for the new site settings will be determined in a separate Jira work item. The rules are: - Users cannot paginate over 10k (site setting) items without creation date filters - If a user enter date parameters, then the date range must not exceed 90 days (site setting). When a valid date range is used, the user may exceed 10k (site setting) items. - "To" parameter must always be accompanied by "From" - "From" does not need the "To" parameter if it's in the past 90 days The tradeoff of this implementation is that the code in this PR can still lead to long running count queries depending on filter values. One way to mitigate that, is that we will now cache the result of the count query for 5 minutes. Because this endpoint does not depend on individual user permissions, we can cache the value for all users. Later on, we'll need to implement a more robust and reusable caching component that can be used throughout the API instead of the one off implementation in this PR. **Note:** Instead of calling these rules "pagination restrictions", I have referred to it as "time-based pagination" in the code. It's not a common term but it does come up on search. ## Tests Unit tests were first generated with Copilot and then reviewed and edited. I added a couple of integration tests to make sure more than 10k items cannot be requested. ## How to Test 1. Enable time-based pagination https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled ### `/questions` #### Pagination without date filters 1. Make a request to page 1 without any filters. You should receive a 200 response. 2. Make a request to the final page without any filters. You should receive a 200 response. 3. Make a request to the final page + 1 without any filters. You should receive a 400 response with a message stating you cannot exceed 10k items. #### Pagination with date filters 1. Make a request with a "from" date in the last 90 days such as "7/22/2025". You should receive a 200 response. 2. Make a request with a "from" date later than 90 days such as "01/01/2024". You should receive a 400 response with a message stating the "to" date is missing and that the range must be 90 days. 3. Make a request with a "to" date and no "from" date. You should receive a 400 response with a message stating the "from" parameter is missing. 4. Make a request with a "to" date and "from" date that is farther than 90 days apart such as "01/01/2024" and "07/01/2024". You should receive a 400 response with a message stating that the date must be within 90 days. 5. Update the total without pagination site setting to something like 150. https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxItemsWithoutDateFilters 6. Make a request with a "to" date and "from" with a range that was high activity such as "01/01/2018" and "03/31/2018". You should be able to go beyond the 150 items. ### `/content-feeds/comments` This endpoint will behave similarly to `/questions` except we are caching the count query for 5 minutes. Only queries without commentIds will have their result cached. #### Pagination without date filters 1. Make a request to page 1 without any filters. You should receive a 200 response. 2. Make a request to the final page without any filters. You should receive a 200 response. 3. Make a request to the final page + 1 without any filters. You should receive a 400 response with a message stating you cannot exceed 10k items. #### Pagination with date filters 1. Make a request with a "from" date in the last 90 days such as "7/22/2025". You should receive a 200 response. 2. Make a request with a "from" date later than 90 days such as "01/01/2024". You should receive a 400 response with a message stating the "to" date is missing and that the range must be 90 days. 3. Make a request with a "to" date and no "from" date. You should receive a 400 response with a message stating the "from" parameter is missing. 4. Make a request with a "to" date and "from" date that is farther than 90 days apart such as "01/01/2024" and "07/01/2024". You should receive a 400 response with a message stating that the date must be within 90 days. 5. Update the total without pagination site setting to something like 150. https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxItemsWithoutDateFilters 6. Make a request with a "to" date and "from" with a range that was high activity such as "01/01/2018" and "03/31/2018". You should be able to go beyond the 150 items. #### Caching count This is difficult to test because we are using site cache which is a two level cache (first level is local and the second level is in Redis). The best way to test this is to add breakpoints on GET and SET. The first call should hit both the GET and SET. Subsequent calls as long as the filter is the same, should not SET the value again until it expires in 5 minutes. To make sure that this is a PER SITE value, you should call `/content-feeds/comments` using both `meta.stackexchange.local` and `literature.stackexchange.local`. They should return different count values. Try the date range `1/1/2018` to `3/30/2018`. The cached entries will also be visible in Redis. For example, to see entries for the Literature site use the following commands in the Redis container terminal: ``` redis-cli -n 668 keys *api* ``` https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/questions/498 - SO Internal article with information on site cache
title: YETI2-698 - Add time based pagination on questions and comment endpoints - Option 2

author: aalear
body:
https://robotics.meta.stackexchange.com/questions/1528/is-it-possible-to-stop-migrated-questions-with-upvoted-answers-from-getting-bump

Back in 2023, we imported ~36k questions from Gazebo and ROS forums into Robotics. We didn't want to grant reputation based on external contributions, however, so none of the votes were migrated and the post metadata (such as the score and the accept status of the answers) were only included in the body of the post. This had the unfortunate side-effect of making it look like every imported post has a score of 0, which makes them eligible for being bumped to the front page by the Community user. This creates a lot of noise on Robotics.

After discussion (see meta post above), we've decided to exclude these posts when choosing one to bump up.

I tested this query via the data explorer: https://dataexplorer-local.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/stackoverflow/query/39211/choose-questions-to-bump-to-the-front-page.
title: CEE-5938 Don't bump posts imported from an external source to the front page

author: KyleMit
body: MOD-173 ## Summary This change will show the signup modal when an anonymous user hits the follow button on a review queue. (And we should expect no change in behavior for a signed in user) ## How to Test 1. As a signed in user make sure you can follow and unfollow a post in a review queue 2. As a anonymous user try to follow a post in a review queue and you should see a signup modal. ## Context So I want to be able to answer a couple questions before writing (or even pasting) new code 1. How does the follow button get wired up for logged in users on the review page? 2. How does the log in modal work normally on the question page for anon 3. How do we differentially load JS. Lots of call stacks to pull on to get an answer to those questions, but a deep dive into how we handle JS bundling ### Differential Loading So the difference between full users / anon is from each of the scripts they load. Here's where we differentially load who gets which script (i.e. `full.en.js` or `full-anon.en.js`) https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/620470e225a3b1eb0ffadf26e33673dcd793b3c4/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/stub.js#L346 `StackExchange.using` determines which file to load based on the key value lookup here https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/620470e225a3b1eb0ffadf26e33673dcd793b3c4/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/stub.js#L493 And those scripts are built into standalone js files here https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/620470e225a3b1eb0ffadf26e33673dcd793b3c4/StackOverflow/webpack.common.ts#L53-L54 The full script barrels up all of these scripts https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/64d3e3119ee6d9bc7e5126a2de22a93f37a52bc3/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/PartialJS/full/index.ts#L1-L7 While full anon barrels up all of these https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/64d3e3119ee6d9bc7e5126a2de22a93f37a52bc3/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/PartialJS/full-anon.ts#L1-L5 ### How follow works for logged in users on review page Review gets initialized via https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/853ae7717e51501cc1742ff2bc071ed219ec6381/StackOverflow/_Scripts/reviews/review.ts#L1584 Which is generated into JS via https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/620470e225a3b1eb0ffadf26e33673dcd793b3c4/StackOverflow/webpack.common.ts#L77 And registered with stub file provider here https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/620470e225a3b1eb0ffadf26e33673dcd793b3c4/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/stub.js#L515 In review queues, voting should get initialized on renderNextItem here https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/853ae7717e51501cc1742ff2bc071ed219ec6381/StackOverflow/_Scripts/reviews/review.ts#L340 For logged in users it's hydrated, but for anonymous users, it's null. For logged in users, that will then call `follow_init` where logged in users get bound to votes https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/853ae7717e51501cc1742ff2bc071ed219ec6381/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/full/vote/index.mod.ts#L39 ### Question Page How does the modal work for anon users from the question page? The method we want to call is really `bindAnonymousVoteDisclaimers` which is in the `full-common` folder that feeds into both full (logged in) and full-anon https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/64d3e3119ee6d9bc7e5126a2de22a93f37a52bc3/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/full-common/11_Question.js#L923 Which is differentially called for anon/logged in here https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/64d3e3119ee6d9bc7e5126a2de22a93f37a52bc3/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/full-common/11_Question.js#L821-L826

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

Apparently we're already sending an event to AEH when a comment is created. Now I'm adding an event that'll be sent when a vote is cast.

There are two reasons why the event is sent only after a successful vote of a certain type:
1. The CommentSubmitEvent that we're supposed to use next to it is only sent if a comment was successfully added. We don't track failures there, so I didn't want to add them here without changing both places.
2. "Voting" on comments is technically voting or flagging and I don't feel like mudding the waters is helpful right now (we don't need to track flags in the experiment). If we do, maybe we should do it through a separate event?

I think it makes sense to track it now, but I don't feel we should wait with merging the first step.

author: chris-doucette-stack
body:
[KRAKEN-2386](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/KRAKEN-2386)
## Summary
This PR attempts to address an issue where the question feedback island stops refreshing after discarding a draft. I was able to replicate the bug consistently using two separate methods. 

The first one is by sending the same title and body to the question assistant twice in a row, the question assistant was holding on to the previous content value after discarding a draft and was therefore not updating its content. 

The second issue is that our conditional in the effect rune that sends out the event makes it very easy to break svelte's state tracking. For this method add a title and body, wait for the feedback island to update then add a tag. Because `sentAutomaticQuestionFeedbackEvent` is first in the conditional, we never access a variable that svelte is tracking and this breaks the effect causing it to never run again.

## How to Test

Issue 1:
1. In a note pad copy a the contents of a question title in body
2. paste both title and body into the form, question feedback should update
3. discard the draft
4. repeat step 2, question feedback should update again.

Issue 2:
1. Copy title and body into the form, wait for question feedback to update
2. Add a tag
3. discard draft and repeat step 1, question feedback should update

This issue was very transient when we first looked into it, another method that seemed successful was to
1. Discard any draft and refresh the page
2. Fill out the question form and go to the review page
3. Discard draft from the review page and fill out the form again
4. Question feedback should update

Sometimes the bug would occur and sometimes it would not, feel free to repeat any of these methods multiple times


[KRAKEN-2386]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/KRAKEN-2386?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

## Summary

*Validation Model is now a class with a `clear` function to remove all validation warnings and messages when a user clicks discard*

What started out as a means to ensure we create event listeners inside of the `onMount` and also have a return function that removes the event listener, turned into a refactor of how we clear validation errors/warnings from components.

Most components no longer care about the discardDraft event, or need to write up a listener. We now call `validationModel.clear()` from the discard draft event handler. This in turn is responsible for clearing all errors/warnings from each of the validationModel sub objects.

5. click the discard draft button.
6. the contents of all fields plus all warnings/errors should also still be cleared.

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
This PR changes the behaviour of the Fragment Proxy where previously the `Accept` header on the request sent to a downstream service would always be set to `text/html` regardless of what the client sent.

This used to work fine because there were no services that used content negotiation but the situation changed and now we need to support this scenario.

When this PR is merged the Fragment Proxy will only set the `Accept` header if none was provided. The value will be set to `tet/html`.
If a `Accept` header was provided, it will be passed on as is.
title: [FRAGMENT PROXY] Pass through Accept header when provided

author: franciscodua
body: FERRET-978 # Summary We're trying to add a new section, to the end of the answer area, with similar questions that the user might answer after they just answered the current question. This means we'll need to know when a user just answered a question, and only in that case, should we fetch suggested questions and show them. For that, I considered 3 different alternatives: 1. Add a query parameter after the user answered a question, so that the query parameter signals that the question view is coming from an answer. `?from-answer=true` 2. Similar, but use the [hash property](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/hash). This is something we already do when we want to add some behavior to the page on the client side, e.g., scrolling down and highlighting the comment section when the URL ends with a #addcomment. I think we used this in the past on client side code, but as far as I know, we don't really use it on the server side (I might be wrong). `#from-answer` 3. Show that new section every time the user visits a question he answered in the last x minutes For this PR, I went with option 1. When a user submits an answer, we'll check if the new site setting is enabled, and if that's the case, we'll add that new query parameter to the returned URL. When the user visits that URL (the browser will take care of that redirect), the query parameter will be there and the server will get it as a parameter, but the user won't see it because there's JS removing the parameter on load (similar to what we do with referrer codes.) ### Fetching questions The second part of this PR is that it's also fetching suggested questions based on the post the user just answered. For this we're using the same question list retriever we used for the tag search page, and we're filtering questions by the same filters and sorts as the `Unanswered` tab, but filtered by the same tags the question that was just answered had. ### Note These changes will later be complemented with this PR https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23442 @bukola-stack is working on. Which should help us test the whole feature end to end # How to test 1. Enable the site setting `SuggestedQuestions.AvailableFor` 2. Select a question to answer 3. Open the network tab on your browser 4. Answer the question 5. You should see something like 👇 on your network tab, and your URL bar shouldn't show any query parameter
title: FERRET-978 Fetch suggested questions after answer

author: animuson
body:
## Summary

Jira: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-14732

Product Support and the SE/CS team have a lot of trouble with trying to explain service keys to Enterprise customers because the term doesn't make any sense with the way it's used. We're not creating a "key" but an "application" which provides all the same components of any other, including a key.

Both teams agree that it would be much easier to explain this to customers if it were correctly named as a "service application" instead. We already have documentation prepared for a change here, and the SE team would be happy to see it changed. It just needs to be updated in the code.

The new wording form has been approved by Loren for better clarity. We also removed an incorrect line about the Domain being required for use with API v3 (was true initially, as v3 was only accessible via access tokens, but it is now accessible with keys also).

Does not change any functionality. Change is entirely to wording.

## How to Test

1. Visit Admin settings then API
2. Ensure the term "service application" is used in all places
3. Click the Register new service application button
4. Ensure the creation form correctly references "service applications"
title: TEAMS-14732: Use "service application" instead of "service key" for clarity

## Summary
MOD-165 

*Your summary.*

Before we were checking if a review queue was full without seeing if the post was locked, this resulted in users with permissions who can bypass review queues getting a weird error message.

The fix in this change is to display an error message if the post is locked as a higher priority then showing the review queue is full.

3. Make sure there is at least one pending suggested edit
4. lock a post as a mod
5. try to edit that post as a non mod
6. After this change you should now see "Post is locked." and not a error about the review queue being full.

author: jbubriski
body:
From [AW-1524]

## Summary

It looks like we're not properly outputting some vars into the HTML to get used by the AEH client-side event code. The current code ends up encoding the quotes around the JSON properties which messes up the HTML. Luckily it doesn't totally break, but it does send the 1 event as 3 separate ones, with the first one being the only "real" event, and missing the other properties.

This change just inlines the vars into the page, and uses `AsJavascriptString()` to ensure that the site name isn't a problem later on.

## How to Test

1. I think you need to enable the [LeftNav.EnableLeftNavItemAehEvents](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=LeftNav.EnableLeftNavItemAehEvents) Site Setting.
2. Inspect the HTML of the Chat link in the sidebar to see that the HTML is busted.
3. Open the Network Tab in Chrome and enable Preserve Log, and clear the log.
4. Click the Chat link to see that it sends 3 events instead of 1. Inspecting them should reveal that the first one is correct, but missing the properties, and the other 2 are the properties that got exploded into the 2nd and 3rd events.
5. Pull/Build/Run the site.
6. Verify that the HTML looks good now.
7. Verify that only 1 event gets sent.

---------------------------------------------------

body: MOD-199 | [Spec](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ALqcns4X5XXEADkjAj6O9jWYgfUySQVij-g-zpVqLk0/edit?tab=t.0) | [Slack Thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C08A82U83JN/p1752154919258059?thread_ts=1752071518.888929&cid=C08A82U83JN) See guidance in [How can I add a moderator-only tag to all meta sites?](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/questions/8677) Prior art in #21014 Better Prior art in #21780 ## Summary We need to fix this two ways 1. For existing sites that won't re-run `Meta Specific DB Creation.scmd` on every deploy, execute a 1 time route to populate the tag 2. For new sites, that don't yet exist during the 1-time route run, make sure they at least get a meta tag on creation (wiki and content TBD) For the one time route, we used to be able to handle this with crazy long URL params But I added a front end in this PR so we can more easily do the data entry with confidence on production ## How to Test 1. Go to [`/developer/tags/add-meta-tag`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/tags/add-meta-tag) 2. Enter the following information and hit "Add new meta tag" * **Tagname** ``` company-update ``` * **Tag Usage Guidance** ``` For posts made by Stack Overflow employees about platform updates, product releases, calls for feedback, etc. ``` * **Tag Wiki** ``` This staff-only tag should be used on all official company announcements, including ones that are not featured. This includes important updates like product releases, platform changes, policy information, community contests, experiment updates, and requests for community feedback. ``` * You can leave Tag summary blank * Check the box for All Meta Sites * Check the box for Mod Only 4. Go to https://meta.stackexchange.local/tags/company-update/info and review tag info 5. Go to https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/company-update And **confirm tag exists** 6. Go to https://literature.meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/company-update And **confirm tag exists** 7. Go to https://literature.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/company-update And **confirm tag doesn't exist** 8. As a mod, you should be able to create a new post or edit that tag into an existing post 9. As a non-mod, you should not be able to insert the tag. ## Notes * If you need to repeat any steps, you can nuke the company-update tag with [`/developer/destroy-tag/company-update`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/destroy-tag/company-update) * If the tag mod only indicator on the tag doesn't show up, [`InitSpecialTags`](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/431529134c2fd7923be49fc0de5db18182b5b44e/StackOverflow.Common/Models/Tag.cs#L301) is only run once on startup and then we cache in memory. If we need to manually clear it, we can run [`/developer/clear-special-tag-cache`](http://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/clear-special-tag-cache), but this should now be addressed in the script. * View other [special tags here](https://dataexplorer-local.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/meta/query/39168/special-tags) * After deployment to prod, should follow instructions in [How do I set up translated special tags?](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/questions/6646) to handle translations

author: connellsharp
body:
We've always had the `not 1234` accountId rule, and the `not ExperimentOptOut` rule. But now, `not` is just a global prefix that can be put on any rule.

This means we can do `not moderators` for example. Also `10%, not rep > 1` or `not 90%, rep < 1`. Which maybe isn't what we want, but we spoke about it recently, and I feel that the idea has come up a few times before, that maybe it's worth doing anyway.

The logic follows that all `not` exclusions are calculated _before_ any inclusions. So a `not` always overrides the other rules.

# How to test

1. Try some PeopleSelectors e.g. `not developers`
2. See if they work
title: [CE-1784] PeopleSelector "not" prefix everywhere

author: CraigTheStacker
body:
MOD-181

**the Problem:** A certain DOM structure was expected for the edit tags button to appear through javascript: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/64d3e3119ee6d9bc7e5126a2de22a93f37a52bc3/StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/inline-tag-editing.js#L140

A div with the class `js-post-tag-list-wrapper` was not being added around the tags in the DOM on the reload.

If you look at this in a debugger it appears that `wrapInList` is true on first render but not true after a live refresh:

https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/431529134c2fd7923be49fc0de5db18182b5b44e/StackOverflow.Common/Models/Tag.cs#L924

this would of added the expected `.js-post-tag-list-wrapper` if set to true.

Thanks to Kyle we know that the initialization of `ShowQuestionParameters`  for this call stack happens in `AjaxMultiLoad.cshtml`

**The Soloution:** Make sure this specific call route sets the wrapInList for tag rendering to be true.

### How To Test

1. Set up and run https://github.com/StackEng/SocketServer
2. turn on the site setting `Realtime.EnableSocket`
3. In two different browser environments: one browser a user who can edit tags on a particular question and second browser with a different user who has permissions to edit the same question.
4. The user on browser 1 should be viewing the question
5. the user on browser 2 should make an edit to that question
6. the user on browser 1 should be able to live refresh the question
7. If the user on browser 1 can see the edit tags button after a live refresh (as well as seeing what user 2 changed) then the test is a success.

author: balpha
body:
ASCN-678

Every time that `scheduled/decay-inferred-tags` runs, which is once a week, we see a whole lot of exceptions like [this](https://opserver.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/exceptions/detail?id=8bb74402-4e49-48bb-a61d-012f16b348f7&log=Q%26A&store=):

```
StackExchange.Redis.RedisTimeoutException: Timeout performing SCAN (5000ms)
```

This scheduled route is marked as failed for pretty much all sites, but for some of them, it's just timed out after 5 minutes, so chances are that they actually succeeded eventually. But a lot of sites failed with that Redis exception, and interestingly, it's the *smaller* sites where that happens. And I think I know why.

For avoidance of confusion: [`StackExchange.Redis`](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/) is our open source Redis library (I say "our", but it's mostly maintained by ex-employees these days). [`StackRedis`](https://github.com/StackEng/StackRedis/) on the other hand is our internal wrapper around `StackExchange.Redis` that also adds things like L1 in-memory cache, key prefixing, and propagation of cache invalidation via Redis messaging channels.

The scheduled route in question here enumerates over all the redis keys that follow a specific pattern. Enumerating over keys is slooooow, which is why you shouldn't usually be doing it, but since this is a background task, I guess it's fine. Note that under the hood, this is *not* using the Redis `KEYS` command (which you absolutly **MUST NOT** use in production because it completely blocks the Redis server until it's complete), but the `SCAN` command.

The `SCAN` command (see the [documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/scan/)) is safe because it uses a cursoring approach. You have to call it multiple times in succession to iterate through the whole keyspace, but each individual call is quick enough.

`SCAN` also takes a pattern as an argument (called `MATCH`), and if given (like in our case), only keys matching said pattern will be returned. A crucial behavior of this argument is described in the [documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/scan/#the-match-option):

> It is important to note that the MATCH filter is applied after elements are retrieved from the collection, just before returning data to the client. This means that if the pattern matches very little elements inside the collection, SCAN will likely return no elements in most iterations.

In our case here, the pattern definitely "matches very little elements". This is especially true now that in GCP, we're using the prefix model. Say for example that the scheduled route is executed on esperanto.meta.stackexchange.com, site ID 663. The `SCAN` command will iterate through all the keys in our giant keyspace (including all the keys for stackoverflow.com, for the global cache, for all the other sites), but it will only match those very few that are prefixed with `s663:viewed-tags-`. That's not a lot of them.

So we're sending a `SCAN` command, getting nothing, sending the next `SCAN` command, getting nothing again, many times over. Only very rarely do we actually get a key matching our pattern.

`StackExchange.Redis` abstracts this cursoring into a class called [`CursorEnumerable`](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/blob/2cb97afe6df2f038430bdccceb55762c2193eedc/src/StackExchange.Redis/CursorEnumerable.cs). That class implements both `IEnumerable` and `IAsyncEnumerable`, so your code can iterate through it synchronously or asynchronously, whichever you prefer.

`StackRedis` prefers sync. It has a [method called `AllKeys`](https://github.com/StackEng/StackRedis/blob/183ee58d782b0d45401f3560c920b9bec424433d/src/StackRedis/Caches.AsyncRedis.cs#L2250), but no `AllKeysAsync`. This method, via `RemoveKeyPrefix`, [synchronously iterates](https://github.com/StackEng/StackRedis/blob/183ee58d782b0d45401f3560c920b9bec424433d/src/StackRedis/Caches.AsyncRedis.cs#L2285) through the `CursorEnumerable`.

Here comes the catch: The synchronous `IEnumerator.MoveNext` implementation for the `CursorEnumerable` simply calls the asynchronous task and `Wait`s for it. And this waiting [uses the same timeout mechanism](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/blob/2cb97afe6df2f038430bdccceb55762c2193eedc/src/StackExchange.Redis/CursorEnumerable.cs#L202) as is used for *actual* Redis timeouts.

So even if the individual Redis `SCAN` calls work just fine and don't actually time out, the task will [keep spinning](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/blob/2cb97afe6df2f038430bdccceb55762c2193eedc/src/StackExchange.Redis/CursorEnumerable.cs#L228) *until one of those calls actually has a result*. This can take a long time especially on small sites, as we pointed out above.

And that's why we're seeing these Redis timeout exceptions. They aren't actually Redis timeouts.

At least I'm pretty sure that's what happens. I would like to confirm that with this very code change, which hacks together some code that does what an `AllKeysAsync` in `StackRedis` would do.

This code isn't meant to exist for long -- either it fixes things and thus confirms my theory, in which case I'll add this new method to `StackRedis`, or it doesn't, in which case I'll back it out again.

---

I have tested locally that his works (as in, it behaves semantically correct by grabbing the correct keys), but of course we need prod volumes to confirm that it actually fixes the problem.
title: Test a fix for "Timeout performing SCAN" Redis exceptions

author: dionrhys
body:
In [SCALE-514](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/SCALE-514) / #23038 we inadvertently broke how Enterprise retrieves its Channels connection string. We relied on Enterprise getting the Channels connection string from the Sites table row for the Channels site (10000) previously, but that PR inadvertently changed it to look for the connection string from `IConfiguration` instead (like it is for other deployment variants).

The initial Enterprise-specific behaviour to get connection string from database instead of `IConfiguration` came from #11607. This was for SOE On-prem, to remove customers' worries about storing passwords in plain text configuration files, so we instead moved those into the Sites table... where it is stored in plain text there instead.

Since we no longer need to worry about SOE on-prem and since we'd like to make our deployment scenarios consistent between variants, this PR doubles down on the change in #23038 and moves SOE connection string retrieval back to `IConfiguration` as it was before 2022. This essentially reverts #11607.

It also essentially reverts the SOE installer change associated with that PR (https://github.com/StackEng/Enterprise-Tools/pull/196) by removing the Channels connection string setting in the Sites table in the SOE CNAB pipeline. Since we migrated SOE to AKS we were already populating the config files with the Channels connection string via the Helm charts, so despite #23038 landing it only broke local and not any of the SOE Hosted instances.

I've verified on the SOE AKS instance that the new PR continues to function with Channels with the connection string removed from the Sites table:

- https://aks.dev.stackenterprise.co/enterprise/teams
- https://aks.dev.stackenterprise.co/c/private-team-1/questions

Since #11607, we added API v3, hence why that project's appsettings.Local.Enterprise.json also has the password added even though #11607 only removed it from the StackOverflow file of the same name.

I've also removed both Sites and Channels connection strings from Channels DB API for Local Enterprise because we don't support that project locally for Enterprise and I'm also keen to remove Channels DB API altogether now because it no longer serves as a security boundary for FBB or SOE since we migrated off app identity Windows Auth.

[SCALE-514]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/SCALE-514?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

This pull request changes the `JwtGenerator` to support this scenario and give us the capability to still send a JWT but one that only contains the relevant data.

- tenant
- user_type
- ip_address
- site_id

## Summary

This PR adds two AEH events: `question_ask.draft_saved` and `question_ask.draft_discarded`. These both mirror the Prizm events of the same name. It is fired in Ask V3 when a draft is saved or discarded.

Prerequisite: [set up your environment for Azure Event Hub](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/questions/27709)

4. Reload the page so that you're able to discard your draft
5. Discard your draft
6. Pull the latest messages in KafkaEsque to see an event for `question_ask.draft_discarded`

## Summary

This PR is changing syntax of Dapper queries in order to use `{=param}` syntax instead of `@param` for constant values. This should end with mere string replacement instead of sql parameter and should help SQL Server choose the better execution plan and/or reuse existing plan.

This started as an attempt to perform replacements on the entire code base, but was eventually limited to `StackOverflow.Common` and `StackOverflow.Common.Api` projects (I did not find anything that needs replacing in V3 project). This is still a large change that covers big part of our codebase. If you see any part of this PR (file, folder) that you think should be excluded, feel free to leave a comment and I will shrink it.

## How to Test

There is no easy way to test this. Assuming build and tests are not failing, the only way to confirm validity of this change is to check it out locally and verify that every parameter with `{=param}` syntax is indeed a constant.

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

We'll be opening commenting to all users. Since we have 1 rep users, a lot of them, this may increase the spam levels. To slightly protect ourselves without being too invasive, we're introducing Turnstile (automated, multi level captcha) for low rep users before their first comment.
After a user passes the check once, we do not verify that user again.

The new modal is implemented on:
- new Razor UI (cause that's the one we have on prod)
- new Svelte UI (cause that's the one we want to have on prod)
- old UI (cause even if we keep the new UI, the old UI will still be there for questions)

Communication between components works through events. The button sends a global event to open the modal, which is handled in the island. After the user is verified, the modal sends either a success or failed event, which is handled in all three places separately (old UI & two new ones). I could make it somewhat more centralized, but then we'd lose the modularity of each implementation. This way each of them works on each own. This leads to some duplication, i.e. data-show-first-commenting param is stored multiple times on UI, but I guess meh.

I'm convinced there are still many ways to improve the code especially on the front end side. I've been sitting at it for a few days now and I think a second opinion would really help me.

## How to Test

### Technical setup
1. Open DevLocalSetup
2. click ~~2,c,1~~ 2,b,1 - this will reconfigure so to run under local.meta.stackexchange.com, which is a valid domain and can be registered in google & cloudflare consoles. This domain is already configured there.
3. Run DB migrations.
4. Impersonate dev and enable turnstile check for as many people as you want ([1](https://local.meta.stackexchange.com/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.ShowFirstTimeCommentingModalFor),[2](https://local.meta.stackexchange.com/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.MaxRepToSeeFirstTimeCommentingModal))
5. Configure Turnstile [site key](https://local.meta.stackexchange.com/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Auth.TurnstileSiteKey) and [secret](https://local.meta.stackexchange.com/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Auth.TurnstileSecret). You can find them on the [cloudflare dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com/f510c13207fc4c7d068e3896525995c9/turnstile/widget/0x4AAAAAAAwfGaA-P7-ratVQ/edit).
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Now testing
1. Make sure you have the new UI without Indiana Jones.
2. Impersonate someone with 1 rep
3. Try commenting, see the modal
4. Don't click ok, close it.
5. Try commenting again.
6. See that it shows up again.
7. Now set the [Turnstile secret](https://local.meta.stackexchange.com/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Auth.TurnstileSecret) to sth incorrect.
8. Try commenting again, this time click ok.
9. See that it failed. There's a toast with an error & all comment & reply buttons are disabled.
10. Enable one of the buttons in dom.
11. Go ahead and comment.
12. See the backend respond with an error.

1. Now set the [Turnstile secret](https://local.meta.stackexchange.com/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Auth.TurnstileSecret) back to the correct value.
2. With the same user, try commenting again.
3. This time, when you click ok, you shouldn't get an error.
4. Comment. This will succeed.
5. Refresh the page.
6. Comment. This time no modal is shown.

1. Impersonate someone with more rep.
2. Try commenting.
3. No modal is shown, you can immediately comment.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Now repeat the steps above for:
- new razor UI
- old razor UI
- new svelte UI
title: [CE-1766] New commenters must pass a captcha check before posting their first comments

author: gabrieltron
body: ## Summary This PR improves parallelization on the playwright tests. You can see not every one of those were related to parallelization, but I was playing around with improvements left them because they're small enough changes. Noticeable changes are: - All tests now may execute in parallel, even if they're in the same class. - This is a big change of paradigm that I'd argue is valuable. It's not uncommon for playwright tests to take 30+ plus seconds. It should be expected that they can run in parallel. - All test methods are called from the same class object - This is the default behavior of NUnit and that was not changed. This is more noticeable now since tests run in parallel. This can cause race conditions with tests that access the same test attribute - Communities related tests were moved to Teams tests instead of public tests - Semantically it makes more sense, and it's also the correct environment to run them. Not as much related to parallelization, but public tests were really slow and my expectation was that this would even workload a little bit more - Only apply site settings once per test class - This saves time applying site settings as settings are defined per class - Do not create an orchestration context before every test - Code before created an orchestration context for every test, and then did nothing with it if one already existed. The changes here remove this extra work. - Many many small changes to reduce flakiness on the playwright tests ## How to Test Playwright integration tests should pass. The [latest commit before the cleanup](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/16180171752/job/45721919768) executed 5 times without flaking, with retry disabled. author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR invalidates `AppCache.cs` used in API v2 when running one of the developer routes used to disable API applications. In addition, this PR:
- Swaps out the SQL queries in the developer routes to call methods in `ApiApplication.cs`, these methods will invalidate the cache
- Move the `app_changed` magic string into a constant variable
- Rename `DeveloperController.ApiV3.cs` to `DeveloperController.Api.cs` since the routes are not only for API v3
- Fixes a UI bug where expired keys do not show as expired in the Stack Apps UI. This is because dates from the DB do not have a specified time zone. When these values are used in JavaScript, the expiration date is parsed in the user's time zone but the time zone should be UTC +0/Zulu. The change here will append a "Z" to the date string so it is parsed as a UTC date by JavaScript and compared against the user's time correctly. 
- Add a new developer route to enable an API application

## How to Test
Configure your startup project to startup both StackOverflow and API v2. 

**Local Setup**
1. Make any call to API v2 (such as `/answers` using the doc site) to subscribe to the PubSub event
2. Use Docker Desktop to open a terminal on the Redis container and enter the following commands `redis-cli` and then `pubsub channels`.
3. If you have subscribed successfully, you'll see the "channel" `local:app_changed`. To listen in on changes, enter `subscribe local:app_changed`.
4. Impersonate a user on Stack Apps that will have their API applications disabled. I [used this user](https://stackapps.local/impersonate/155659 .
5. Create 2 apps and add at least one key per app

**Testing Locally**
1. After completing the setup above, impersonate a developer on Stack Apps
2. Run `https://stackapps.local/developer/api/disable-app-and-keys/{appId}?dryRun=false` to disable a single app. 
    - Verify the app ID is published in the terminal watching the `local:app_changed` subscription. 
    - Verify the app has been disabled and the keys expired by querying the database or using Stack Apps.
3. Run `https://stackapps.local/developer/api/enable-app/{appId}?dryRun=false` to enable a single app. 
   - Verify the app ID is published in the terminal watching the `local:app_changed` subscription. 
   - Verify the app has been enabled querying the database or using Stack Apps.
4. Run `https://stackapps.local/developer/api/disable-account-apps-and-keys/{accountId}?dryRun=false` to disable all apps for a single account. 
   - Verify the app IDs are published in the terminal watching the `local:app_changed` subscription. 
   - Verify the app has been enabled querying the database or using Stack Apps.

```
SELECT * FROM [Local.Sites].dbo.ApiApplications
WHERE Id IN (20585, 20586)

SELECT * FROM [Local.Sites].dbo.ApiApplicationKeys
WHERE ApplicationId IN ()
```
_________________

**Testing with PR Environment**
This is more for Jeff since you can't easily validate that the cache was invalidated without generating API keys and making calls to API v2.
1. [Impersonate user 1 ](https://23294-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/impersonate/1)
2. In a private window, [impersonate user 4](https://23294-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/impersonate/4)
2. As user 1, run `https://23294-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/developer/api/disable-app-and-keys/1?dryRun=false` to disable a single app. 
    - As user 4, verify the app "App No. 1" has been disabled using Stack Stack Apps' `/applications` view. Click into the app to verify that the keys have been invalidated.
3. As user 1, run `https://23294-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/developer/api/enable-app/1?dryRun=false` to enable a single app. 
   - As user 4, verify the app "App No. 1" is enabled using Stack Stack Apps' `/applications` view.
4. As user 1, run `https://23294-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/developer/api/disable-account-apps-and-keys/4?dryRun=false` to disable all apps for a single account. 
   - As user 4, verify that both apps have been disabled using Stack Apps' `/applications` view. Click into the apps to verify that the keys have been invalidated.

author: dionrhys
body: # Summary This PR refactors `ZuoraHelper` to remove its `DEBUG`-only `OverrideClientForTesting(IZuoraClient client)` method and make `IZuoraClient` be passed in from DI instead. This is part of [SCALE-467](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/SCALE-467) work to remove all `DEBUG` conditionals that prevent Integration Tests from running in Release builds. Our usual quick fix here would be to just remove the `DEBUG` conditional and add a `if (Env.IsTestRun) { throw ... }` guard instead, but I wanted to spend some time refactoring one of these cases the "proper" way to learn how this can be done in our static state-heavy codebase and what kind of effort is required. I was pleasantly surprised how little effort was needed here. When I say "proper" way above I mean to avoid usages of `Env.IsTestRun` conditionals, static state, `Current` state, and `AsyncLocal` dependencies. For `ZuoraHelper`, it means no longer keeping the real `ZuoraClient` in a static variable, no longer using `Current.SetContextItem` for stashing a client override for testing, and having the `IZuoraClient` instance passed in from the callers instead of storing it itself. Here's a summary of what's been done: - **`ZuoraHelper` is now just a collection of static helper functions** that get `IZuoraClient` passed in directly as an argument - nb: static functions are great, static state is not - `IZuoraClient` will be coming from DI in all places at run time, and from direct mock/stub instantiation at test time - **A `ZuoraClientFactory` class has been created** that's responsible for managing the real `ZuoraClient` instance at run time (the client that talks to zuora.com over HTTPS) - We need to cache `ZuoraClient` as long as possible to ensure we hold on to its `AuthToken`; if we just instantiated this class every request we needed it, we'd quickly evaporate our Zuora rate limits for fetching this token - We also need to recreate the `ZuoraClient` when the Zuora site settings change since the client caches all its configuration when it's instantiated - While I'm averse to introducing any kind of "factory" (😉), we need something to manage the lifecycle of `ZuoraClient` at run time because of the aforementioned constraints - Crucially what this achieves is moving the `ZuoraClient` from being managed as static state to being managed in an instance's state, which makes it much easier to manage in DI - **A `IServiceCollection.AddZuora()` extension method has been added** that wires up the `ZuoraClientFactory` and `IZuoraClient` services to DI - `ZuoraClientFactory` is registered a singleton at startup - `IZuoraClient` is registered as a transient service that gets its client from calling the singleton `ZuoraClientFactory`'s `GetClient()` method - This same pattern is essentially used by [`IServiceCollection.AddHttpClient()`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/71c30b405516b1fe774a1bfdbc43cd804468568f/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Http/src/DependencyInjection/HttpClientFactoryServiceCollectionExtensions.cs#L26) that uses the[`DefaultHttpRequestFactory` singleton service](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/71c30b405516b1fe774a1bfdbc43cd804468568f/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Http/src/DependencyInjection/HttpClientFactoryServiceCollectionExtensions.cs#L40) under-the-hood to make available [`IHttpClient` as a transient service](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/71c30b405516b1fe774a1bfdbc43cd804468568f/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Http/src/DependencyInjection/HttpClientFactoryServiceCollectionExtensions.cs#L65-L69), reusing a cached client or spinning up a new one # What this means **For run time application code**, it means that any controller action or background service that needs to talk to Zuora at some point will now get the `IZuoraClient` from DI and pass this down to any methods that need it. For controller actions, that just means adding a `[FromServices] IZuoraClient zuoraClient` parameter to the method. **For tests**, it means that you can create a `IZuoraClient` directly (real, mock, stub, etc.) and pass it into whatever Zuora-related methods you want to test. If you're testing a controller action end-to-end with `TestServer`, you can register a custom `IZuoraClient` using the `ConfigureTestServices` method on the server. # Technical details A few quirks of the monolith mean there are some interesting details: ## Responding to site settings changes Site settings changes in the monolith are announced using SO's custom `EventAttribute` and `HandlesEventAttribute`. The event handlers can only be assigned to **static methods**. In order to move the `ZuoraClient` lifetime management to an instance-based class, this means we needed to have a way where the static event handler can notify the factory instance about the event, so that it can refresh the `ZuoraClient`. This was done by adding a plain .NET static `EventHandler _zuoraSiteSettingsChanged` field to `ZuoraClientFactory` and having the factory instance(s) subscribe to this event at construction time and unsubscribe from it at dispose time. Whenever site settings are changed, the static `ZuoraClientFactory.OnGlobalSiteSettingChangedAsync` is called and this ends up calling `_zuoraSiteSettingsChanged?.Invoke(...)` to notify all the factory instances that they should refresh their `ZuoraClient` instances. In reality there should only be one (singleton) factory instance, but the benefit of this system is that it doesn't care if there are more for some reason (e.g. in tests). **This is a pattern that will likely apply to other refactorings where classes are dependent on SO's custom event handling mechanism.** ## Coupling with Zuora in Chargify-only routes I noticed that quite a few routes relating to Chargify also depend on Zuora for various reasons. I've left these alone and not tried to refactor to decouple them because it would likely expand the scope of this work considerably. I'd also like to touch billing / subscriptions code as little as possible because I'm not very familiar with it. # How to Test I've tested this by deploying the PR to stackoverflowteams.dev and doing this: 1. Verifying that [/scheduled/channels/subscriptions/sync-user-quantities](https://scheduler.eastus-dev.teams.int.stackoverflow.net/scheduler/jobs/aHR0cDovL3N0YWNrb3ZlcmZsb3ctY2hhbm5lbHMuc3RhY2tvdmVyZmxvdy9zY2hlZHVsZWQvY2hhbm5lbHMvc3Vic2NyaXB0aW9ucy9zeW5jLXVzZXItcXVhbnRpdGllcw%3D%3D) works ok (that receives an `IZuoraClient` from DI) 2. Verifying that the "Sync with Zuora" button on the [Support Dashboard](https://stackoverflowteams.dev/c/dion-business-test/admin/support/subscriptions/1098) works - Annoyingly, there doesn't appear to be a shared team on stackoverflowteams.dev that can act as the Support Dashboard site so I temporarily changed the dashboard site ID to one of my own teams right now (you should be able to quick join it at https://stackoverflowteams.dev/c/dion-business-test/quick-join) 3. Verifying that `/developer/zuora/describe/test` calls out to Zuora You can do the same or other Zuora test steps if you know of any. I've also verified on Enterprise (https://aks.dev.stackenterprise.co) with this PR that routes requiring a `IZuoraClient` succeed as they did before, e.g. [/scheduled/channels/subscriptions/sync-user-quantities](https://aks.dev.stackenterprise.co/scheduler/jobs/aHR0cDovL3N0YWNrb3ZlcmZsb3ctY2hhbm5lbHMuc3RhY2tvdmVyZmxvdy9zY2hlZHVsZWQvY2hhbm5lbHMvc3Vic2NyaXB0aW9ucy9zeW5jLXVzZXItcXVhbnRpdGllcw%3D%3D). I've verified on PubPlat that trying to access a Zuora route keeps the same behaviour as it did before. Here's what you'll get before and after this PR: [SCALE-467]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/SCALE-467?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
title: SCALE-467 Refactor ZuoraHelper to allow it to be tested in Release builds

This PR attempts to be a little smarter in determining the repository root and thus the target location for generated Type Script files.

author: WouterDeKort
body:
This PR is for [ASCN-669](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/ASCN-669).

# Context

We are seeing a lot of _Invalid non-ASCII or control character in header_ errors in our log. 

The issue is that ASP.NET on Kestrel on Linux does not handle non-ASCII characters in the `Location` header of a redirect request. This was not an issue on IIS.

The fix is to encode the return URL before ASP.NET puts it in the header: https://www.adamrussell.com/asp-net-core-invalid-non-ascii-or-control-character-in-header.

This is a known issue and a GitHub issue has been open for years: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/4919.

This seems to be happening only on bot request on `meta.serverfault.com`. We never generate a URL like this ourselves so it feels like a bot is trying to get to this URL, malicious or not. We want to make sure that this specific code path no longer generates this error.

See [this DataDag notebook](https://us3.datadoghq.com/notebook/179304/error-invalid-non-ascii-or-control-character-in-header) for my research.

# Fix

author: balpha
body:
ASCN-370

The first time we deployed Stack Overflow after moving it to GCP in April, the application struggled to become alive because the pods got overwhelmed with traffic while they were still warming up. Incident 1094 was what happened next.

As a temporary fix, we did three things:

1. change the cluster to run on more powerful nodes
2. increase the startup delay for startup and readiness check to 60 seconds each
3. during deployment, only bring up one new pod at a time

Because of 1), we're currently spending more money on production than we would like. Because of 2) and 3), a deployment of the Q&A application currently takes around 20 minutes, much longer than we would like.

This change here fixes those things by doing the following:

1. Add a readiness health check that ensures that `IActionDescriptorCollectionProvider.ActionDescriptors` is initialized before marking the application as ready. This is part of the MVC routing mechanism, and its initialization is usually only triggered on the first request that makes it to the MVC pipeline (which, crucially, does not include health checks). A thread dump taken at the time of the incident points to this initialization potentially causing deadlocks if too much traffic is thrown at the pod.
2. Add a readiness health check that monitors how many requests are currently in the pipeline, by monitoring AspNet's `http.server.active_requests` metric. If this health check, by some crude-but-working approximation, assumes that the number of inflight requests will exceed 800 (this threshold is configurable if needed) within the next second, it will mark the application as not ready (anymore). That way, the load balancer will stop sending new traffic to the pod until it has worked through its backlog. This should only happen during startup (but is good to prevent request pile-ups for any other reason as well).
3. Set `minReadySeconds` to 10 for the deployment strategy. This waits for a container to remain ready continuously for 10 seconds before terminating a previous pod. This is useful because with 2), the pod might be briefly ready (green), receive some warmup traffic, then unready (orange) again while it actually warms up, and finally ready (green) for the world.
4. Set the health check frequency for readiness checks to 1/s, so that a pod quickly gets a chance for marking itself unready. An interval of 10s is too long to prevent request pileup from reaching critical levels.
5. Set `maxSurge` to 40% on the deployment strategy. This means that up to 4 new pods are created together during a deployment. I picked this number rather arbitrarily, and I'm leaving it up for discussion. At 40%, a full deploy takes about two minutes (excluding container image download). At 100%, it takes about one minute.

I've tested this extensively in `load-test`, which was [scaled down](https://github.com/StackEng/gcp-pubplat/pull/161) back to the hardware level that we would like to use for prod as well.

Once this is merged, I want to give it on more run in `load-test` from `main`, before deploying it to prod.

Scaling down `main-prod` will then be a separate thing that we'll have to coordinate with SRE, and where we'll have to keep an eye on *all* the applications while it's happening.
title: Make application startup more resilient to thundering herd issues

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
Currently, integration tests isolate the current site's caches (Redis and Local) for the test class. This works fine for most tests, where we only use the current site as loaded when the ContextProvider sets it. 

The problem is that the `AsyncLocal`s that are used to override the current site's Redis and Local caches are part of the object (not static), meaning that if we get a different object representing the same site, or another site, the cache wouldn't be isolated in that case. And when we isolate the site cache, we want it isolated for every site that the test uses. 

The way cache isolation works is by using a unique prefix on Redis. So, this PR reuses that concept but instead of isolating the Current site's object redis/local caches, it enables sites (all sites) caches for the test. It does so by setting the prefix in a static async local (`AsyncLocal<string> _cacheOverridePrefix`). Then we it also uses another asynclocal (`_cacheOverrides) `with a dictionary of `<SiteId, (LocalCache, RedisCache)>`, that allows us to have the isolated caches for each site as they are used in the test ambient. 

The way it works is:

- We isolate the site caches for a test by calling: `Site.OverrideRedisAmbientForTesting(uniquePrefix);` (where `uniquePrefix` is the isolation key). This will set the `Site._cacheOverridePrefix` AsyncLocal.
- Then whenever we do `mySite.RedisCache`, the code will:
  - Check if the caches are overriden for the current ambient by checking if `_cacheOverridePrefix.Value` is not null
  - If they are overriden, it checks if we already created the overriden caches for this site in the `Site._cacheOverrides` async local dictionary. If we did, we return it, otherwise we create it with the `Site._cacheOverridePrefix`, store it in the dictionary for future use and return it. 
  - If it's not overriden, just return the regular instance as usual.
title: SCALE-546 Update how ambient Site cache overrides work

author: aalear
body:
## Summary

With the move to GCP, we are no longer deploying debug builds to the main-test environment, which makes user impersonation unavailable since it's conditionally compiled only into debug builds. This is creating problems for product teams trying to test anything in that environment before a production release.

<s>The existing validation checks were updated to include a configuration setting check.</s> 

This PR moves the routes from being conditionally compiled to a controller that only allows requests from internal IP addresses. The IP address checks are a part of the safety net here, but I'm also adding two new configuration parameters:

- `UserImpersonation:AllowRegular` controls impersonation of regular (unregistered, registered, moderator) users
- `UserImpersonation:AllowPrivileged` controls impersonation of employees.

The settings are deliberately not set up as site settings in order to require a PR and a review for any changes.

Last but not least, I'm adding a new parameter to `[StackRoute]` to add an extra tier check and immediately 404 in production. This will mitigate the odds of us accidentally leaking the existence of these routes if IP checks break while still allowing the convenience of `PostToRun`.

## How to Test

1. Impersonate a user locally (should succeed)
2. Change the local configuration to disable impersonation and verify that it then fails
3. Impersonate a user in the pubplat PR environment (should succeed)
4. Impersonate a user in the Enterprise PR environment (should succeed)
5. This PR is currently deployed to `ascn-dev` and can be tested there as well, although impersonation  has worked there this entire time, so it's a bit moot. Still, you can see the restriction on impersonating employees in action there.

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR prevents suspended users in the newer Stack Apps flow from:
- Registering new API applications
- Create/delete/rotate API keys
- Create/delete/rotate client secrets

All of these actions will return a HTTP status code of 403 when a suspended user attempts them.

Users will still be able to edit their app's details or OAuth configuration. However, neither of these functions can be used by a suspended user for mischief (aside from uploading a bad image?). This is because we use the application's disabled state to determine whether to serve a request or complete an OAuth dance. For access tokens that have already been created, both API v2 and v3 check if the application is disabled when a request comes in. 

## How to Test
**Suspended User**
**Note: All errors are generic.**
1. Impersonate a suspended user - https://23245-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/impersonate/4
2. Go to an app that the user created before the suspension - https://23245-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/applications/view/1
3. Verify the user cannot create/rotate/delete API keys - These will all show generic errors, the HTTP response code is 403
4. Verify the user cannot create/rotate/delete client secrets - These will all show generic errors, the HTTP response code is 403
5. Verify the user cannot create a new application - https://23245-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/applications/register
    - The generic error is now a danger toast instead of a modal
    - The HTTP response code is a 403

**Regular user**
1. Impersonate a user that is not suspended -  https://23245-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/impersonate/5
2. Verify the user can create a new application
3. Verify the user can create/rotate/delete API keys
4. Verify the user can create/rotate/delete client secrets

**Replacing generic error modal with a toast**
Caro asked if we could replace the modal with a toast so that the behavior is more in line with the rest of the site.
1. The new toast can be seen on the register page when impersonating a suspended user and attempting to register a new application
2. To see the new toast on the "Edit details" modal, it's easiest to create an empty `.csv` file and try to upload it as an image
3. The new danger toasts should not appear when we know what went wrong with validation such as a missing description

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d7e3252-ccfc-4b2d-aaec-edf55ed49424)

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
This PR parallelizes Channels tests. Right now they are all running sequentially: 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25ec4a39-0728-4741-9740-457246235b8f)

With this PR, they run in parallel, much faster:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6222d42a-eab5-4a4b-8c65-ad709eaf3eb2)

## Important changes
1. This PR isolates the Channels Settings cache for each channel tests, using the `AmbientIsolatableObject` pattern. 

2. Api tests need to run at the end and sequential to the rest because they update the ContextProvider. It was using the `StackOverflow.Tests.Integration.Api.ApiCollection` which disabled parallelization, however XUnit doesn't take into account the `DisableParallelization` attribute if the collection definition is in another assembly. So I had to create `StackOverflow.Tests.Integration.Channels.Api.ChannelsApiCollection`

3. Channels test classses that didn't need a channel instance were extending `BaseTest`, without possible DB isolation. I did some refactoring and now the base channels tests classes are as follows:
  - `BaseTest`
    - `BaseChannelTest`
      - `IsolatedDBChannelsBaseTest` <-- Isolated without an instance 
      -  `BaseChannelInstanceBaseTest`
         - `ChannelInstanceBaseTest`
         - `EmptyChannelInstanceBaseTest` 
         - `IsolatedDBChannelInstanceBaseTest` <-- Isolated with an instance
      
## Results
The `Integration tests (Debug, BlueshiftTest, StackOverflow.Tests.Integration.Channels)` job goes from **5mins to 2.5 mins**. 
The `Integration tests (DebugEnterprise, EnterpriseTest, StackOverflow.Tests.Integration.Channels)` job went from **4mins to 2 mins**

So, we are saving a total of 4 mins per workflow run. Last year there were 21,298 workflow runs, so 21,298 * 4 * 0.064 = **$5,400/year**
title: SCALE-546: Parallelize channels tests

author: troygould-stack
body:
[KRAKEN-2357]

## Summary

*Issue when suggested tags returns a tag that is a synonym*

We used to start showing the synonyms after the first search, and then do another search for the tag suggestion data used in the popups. This was an issue because sometimes the suggestion list contains a tag that is a synonym for another tag. Therefore, when we tried to attach the data from the second fetch call back to the tagName, it would return the "parent" tag, and not the tag that was sent. 

This change results in us just using the tags from the first API call to make the next set of API calls and using whatever tags are returned to decide what to show in the list.

## How to Test

1. You'll need to search your local database for Tag Synonyms and ensure that the child or synonym appears in the body of your question. A good post to copy to see this is: https://meta.stackoverflow.com/questions/432369/non-whitelisted-html-like-text-is-incorrectly-stripped-from-discussions-post-mar
2. Inspect the call to `suggested-tags` and notice the tags that are returned. An example might be:
```
{
  "suggestedTags": [
    "markdown-rendering",
    "data-explorer",
    "data-dump",
    "self-answer"
  ]
}
```
3. The second set of calls to `popup` would search for `markdown-rendering` but return results for `markdown` because `markdown-rendering` is a synonym for `markdown`. This was throwing errors and the popup would not be populated.



[KRAKEN-2357]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/KRAKEN-2357?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
title: fixed suggested tags to handle synonym tags.

author: KyleMit
body:
Follow up to #23004

MOD-146

## Summary
This change makes election update notifications idempotent by re sending the notifications to those who haven't already received the notifications on a scheduled basis, this also will allow people to vote who qualify to vote after the notifications were first sent.

this also adds logging for any notification that throws an exception so the notifications don't stop if one notification throws an exception.

## How to Test

1. You'll want to create an election locally by going to [`/election`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/election)
2. Create an election and get to the nomination and primary phase
3. Check what your current election id by running the following query

    ```sql
    SELECT TOP 1 *
    FROM [Local.StackExchange.Meta].dbo.ModeratorElections
    ORDER BY Id DESC
    ```

4. Before transitioning to the election phase, we want to emulate a scenario in which all election notifications did not go out. To do that, just add `.Take(100)` to the following line of code

    https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/26c8c186025361598dca90e2118c0e3a2ba75384/StackOverflow.Common/Models/ModeratorElection.StateChanges.cs#L252
    
    ```diff
    - foreach (var accountId in accountIds)
    + foreach (var accountId in accountIds.Take(100))
    ```

6. Now you can move the Election into the "Election" phase to trigger the partial set of notifications
  
6. You can test the number of notifications that have gone out on your local DB with the following query
    
    ```sql
    SELECT *
    FROM [Local.Sites].dbo.Inboxes
    WHERE InboxTypeId = 30 -- ElectionBegins
        AND SiteId = 4 -- MSE
        AND ItemId = 1 -- USE YOUR LOCAL ELECTION ID
    ORDER BY Id DESC
    ```

7. You should see a total count of only 100.

8. You can confirm there should be way more eligible voters with the following query

    ```sql
    SELECT AccountId
    FROM [Local.StackExchange.Meta].dbo.Users
    WHERE Reputation >= 150
      and AccountId is not null
    ```

9. Because we use a redis lock to prevent multiple executions, in order to run the same code again, without having to wait an hour, you'll have to kill the redis key that controls the lock by going to the following route

    https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/redis/killglobalkey/election-transition-to-Election-4

    **NOTE**: Make sure to do this every time before you re-try the schedule route or it won't run

10. Now go hit the schedule route

    https://meta.stackexchange.local/scheduled/resend-election-notifications

11. You can re-check the inbox notifications count and now it should be incremented by **100** and at **200 total**

12. Now remove the `.Take(100)`  you added earlier and re compile

13. Hit the scheduled route again after removing the Redis lock and it should run for the rest of the accounts that need to be notified.

14. You can re-check the inbox notifications count and now it should be now contain all notifications.
title: MOD-146 Automatic retry of election notifications

author: gabrieltron
body:
## Summary

We have two new flaky integration tests. Those are the tests and what this PR does to make them not flaky:
- `Helpers.Services.GenericRedisQueue.WhenUsingTheGenericRedisQueue.GivenMessageForSameSiteIsEnqueuedDuringProcessing_AllMessagesAreHandled`
  - The queue stays running for 5 seconds ([here](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/2cee4e9f8166afa4f31f1a8c5c78aff7dde80c0e/tests/StackOverflow.Tests.Integration/Helpers/Services/GenericRedisQueue/WhenUsingTheGenericRedisQueue.cs#L274)). The loop interval was 250 seconds (see changes). Each request took 4*250 to execute ([here](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/2cee4e9f8166afa4f31f1a8c5c78aff7dde80c0e/tests/StackOverflow.Tests.Integration/Helpers/Services/GenericRedisQueue/WhenUsingTheGenericRedisQueue.cs#L194)). We had 5 messages. So the queue runs for 5 seconds, and we take 5 seconds to process all messages. I reduced the `ProcessLoopWaitInterval` time so each request takes 400ms to execute, so we have 5 seconds of queue running to run 5 requests of 400ms (2s)
    - This was consistently failing on my local and is now passing
- `StagingGround.RecentActivityNoticeTests.Recent_reviewer_activity_notice_shows_appropriate_sg_action`
  - We were trying to add a key in a dictionary that already had that key. The dictionary is static and can be accessed by multiple threads. I made it thread safe to avoid multiple inserts of the same key
    - Wasn't able to reproduce the flakiness on local, but I'm pretty sure that's the issue by the stack trace of the failing test

# Testing

I ran the [tests on the latest commit ](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15881351902/job/44789901982?pr=23227)5 times with no flakes
title: Fix flaky tests

author: dionrhys
body:
Slack context: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C033747T0AF/p1746528494605469
Jira context: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/SCALE-481

## Summary

This PR removes the Menubar roles from TopBar actions and fixes a Critical A11Y issue across all pages on Teams and Enterprise due to the menubar having errant `<li>` elements without `role="none"`.

The [Menubar](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/) ARIA role requires special input and focus handling so that you can navigate between the menu items using arrow keys instead of tabbing. This isn't how the TopBar functions, so the role should be removed.

Here's what W3C has to say about [using Menubar for navigation](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/examples/menubar-navigation/):

> [!CAUTION]
> Before considering use of the [Menubar Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/) for site navigation, it is important to understand:
>
> - The menubar pattern requires complex functionality that is unnecessary for typical site navigation that is styled to look like a menubar with expandable sections or "fly outs".
> - A pattern more suited for typical site navigation with expandable groups of links is the [Disclosure Pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/). For an example, see [Example Disclosure Navigation Menu](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/).

I've tested these preliminary changes with the [NVDA](https://www.nvaccess.org/) screen reader and they work fine, although it would be nice if _some_ of these links get `role="button"` and `aria-expanded=...` to indicate they're buttons that open/close trays with more actions ([Disclosure Navigation pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/)). It's tricky because they're also real anchors with hrefs that work as hyperlinks when JavaScript is disabled (to take you to a relevant page instead of opening their trays). I decided against making changes to the JS here to apply roles dynamically on handler registration.

## How to Test

Run the in-app Accessibility Scanner against an Enterprise build (where the violations are detected) before and after this PR.

Before this PR, the top bar actions section should flag up with invalid elements (a `<li>` that doesn't have `role="none"`). After this PR, the top bar actions section should no longer flag up any invalid elements.
title: [A11Y] SCALE-481 Remove role="menubar" from TopBar
