author: aalear
body:
## Summary

Since moving to GCP, we've been throwing the `Invalid non-ASCII or control character in header` exception ([example](https://opserver.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/exceptions/detail?id=0ee2af02-0eb0-41e5-92f9-5b3ddd157d4f&log=Q%26A&store=)). After trying to reproduce it and looking closer into when it was being thrown, I noticed that it's only happening on child meta sites when using the "log in" link from the site switcher and logging in with an email/password combo: 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c680b8a-1ebf-4968-83a7-89337050a8c0)

Turns out that the signup and login links in that popover are `http://` rather than `https://` and that's causing another redirect by Cloudflare because it's enforcing HTTPS for all traffic. Somewhere somehow that lands us with an insufficiently encoded header.

(Why are the links `http`? No idea, but [past me did it](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/commit/b687b5f1212832101caa2988d1ad138986a53295) for a reason that made sense at the time, I'm sure.)

## Testing

This isn't really feasible to test locally due to the setup required. We do have a child meta site locally, so you can at least verify that the links are `https://` now on `https://literature.meta.stackexchange.local`. 

Beyond that, if you have an email/password credential in prod...

To reproduce the bug:
1. Visit `https://meta.stackoverflow.com/users/53897/thorbj%c3%b8rn-ravn-andersen` in incognito (or otherwise logged out) mode
2. Click the SE speech bubble logo next to the "log in" button and click the "log in link" (see screenshot above)
3. Use your email and password
4. Observe the error page

To test the fix:
1. Visit `https://meta.stackoverflow.com/users/53897/thorbj%c3%b8rn-ravn-andersen` in incognito (or otherwise logged out) mode
2. Click the SE speech bubble logo next to the "log in" button and edit the HTML to replace `http://` with `https://`
3. Click the updated link, use your email/password and observe a successful login and redirect back to the user profile page you started from.
title: ASCN-669 Use https "log in" links in the site switcher on child metas

author: qheaden-stack
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a new site setting `Questions.AbandonedQuestionViewCountMultiplier`, and it updates the `ScheduledController.RemoveAbandonedQuestionsAsync()` method to use that setting to control the multiplier used in the calculation to determine if a post has "low view count". By default, this is 1.5 times the age of the post in days. This might need to be adjusted on a site-by-site basis since other SE sites don't get as much traffic as the main Stack Overflow.

The PR also adds tests for `ScheduledController.RemoveAbandonedQuestionsAsync()` to verify existing functionality, verify our changes work as expected, and ensure our changes don't break anything.

## How to Test

- [Impersonate the dev user](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/users/impersonate/1)
- [Create a new question](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/questions/ask)
- Save the URL of the newly created question (and take note of the post ID in the URL)
- Set the question's creation date to less than 365 days old (route `https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/posts/<post ID here>/set-creation-date/2025-01-01`)
- [Run the weekly scheduled route](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/scheduled/weekly)
- Revisit the question you just created and ensure it **isn't** deleted
- [Update the Questions.AbandondedQuestionRemovalDays setting to a low value such as 10](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Questions.AbandonedQuestionRemovalDays)
- [Run the weekly scheduled route again](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/scheduled/weekly)
- Revisit the question you just created and ensure it **is now** deleted by Community Bot
- Click on the "undelete" link below the question to undelete it
- [Reset the Questions.AbandondedQuestionRemovalDays setting back to the default value of 365](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Questions.AbandonedQuestionRemovalDays)
- Set the question's creation date to a little over 365 days old (route `https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/posts/<post ID here>/set-creation-date/2024-06-01)
- Update the question view count to 1000 (route `https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/posts/<post ID here>/set-view-count/1000`)
- [Run the weekly scheduled route again](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/scheduled/weekly)
- Revisit the question and ensure it **isn't** deleted
- [Update the Questions.AbandondedViewCountMultiplier to be 10](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Questions.AbandonedQuestionViewCountMultiplier)
- [Run the weekly scheduled route again](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/scheduled/weekly)
- Revisit the question and ensure it **is now** deleted
- [Reset the Questions.AbandondedViewCountMultiplier back to the default value of 1.5](https://23200.stackoverflow.cloud/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Questions.AbandonedQuestionViewCountMultiplier)
title: [LAUNCH-137] - Add site setting to more finely controll question cleanup process (aka Roomba)

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
With the recent work that Scale did, we isolated the first main site’s database alongside the Sites and ChannelsDB. However, the PublicTest network (or any other used by the integration tests) has more sites than that. For example, Literaturature, Meta Literature, StackApps, etc. 

Some tests switch to these sites with methods defined in `BaseTest`, such as `WithMainSite` or `WithLiteratureSite`. The problem is that when for example the current database is Literature, and the test is using the `IsolatedDatabaseTest` base class, it runs on an isolated SitesDB but in a non isolated ContentDB. 

This PR fixes that by:
- During bootstrapping it takes a backup of all the content database of each site in the testing network (i.e. PublicTest)
- The `IsolatedDatabaseTest` keeps restoring the SitesDB and the network's principal's site content DB (the default used by every test). 
- `IsolatedDatabaseTest` overrides the `With{Site}` methods, by creating an isolated version of that site's content DB and overriding **again** the connectionstring mappings. So now when the test switches to a new site, that site's DB is also isolated and the test hit that DB. We only restore it once per TestClass, same concept as with the principal's site content DB and SitesDB. 

This is how a test that uses `WithMainSite` looked like before. You can see in the items watched at the bottom, that the originalCurrentDB and sitesDB point to an isolated test (have a guid at the end), while the currentDB doesnt:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dca8688a-a0c0-4c57-ae3b-abce3a40b958)

With the changes of this PR, this is how it looks like. The 3 databases are isolated:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb283148-4e3b-4982-a810-f0106a365e9c)
title: Isolate all databased for integration tests

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
>Lloyds has found that you can create an Access Token for an API Key and use it for all methods, GET, POST, etc. 2.3 Methods: After you delete the Key on SO, you can still call the API successfully. It seems that, when we do a lookup for what app is connected, we cache that result (seemingly permanently) in the application. When looking it up, we find it in the cache and don't see the changes to the application.
I was able to recreate this using an Access Token created from this key, calling any 2.3 API, deleting the key, and then using the API again. After being deleted, it worked in my terminal and in the SO doc environment.
It stops being usable after a restart or if I attempt to use the same access token in V3(which gives the proper error) and then go back to V2.3.
This potentially leaves a gap when an API is exposed to a deprecated key.

The problem is with the `AppCache.TokenCache`, which holds references to applications. When an application is disabled it's not properly invalidated in that cache. 

After reviewing with Yaritza we found this cache to be very problematic and decided to remove it. We tested it together in my SOE local and could replicate the issue before adding the fix, and then that it's rejecting request with "`key` has been disabled" after the fix.
title: INCIDENT-1161 Fix SOE access tokens keep working after api application was disabled

author: dionrhys
body:
# Background

In [#incident-1154-stack-overflow-and-stack-exchange-sites-are-down](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C090R1SJNTY), stackoverflow.com went down because a release of the code was deployed to Prod running on the latest ASP.NET Core 8.0.17 update and that contained a breaking change to the `ForwardedHeadersMiddleware` that broke our app's `X-Forwarded-Proto` header handling:

- Release notes: https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/9930
- Microsoft's apology for not mentioning this breaking change initially in the release notes: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/61622#issuecomment-2968115960
- Original issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/61449

The fix that Microsoft backported as a security patch was necessary because the middleware before was not respecting the `KnownNetworks` or `KnownProxies` configuration, meaning that `X-Forwarded-Proto` would always be respected if the configuration also hadn't been set up to respect `X-Forwarded-For`.

Our app relied on this incorrect behaviour - it expected `X-Forwarded-Proto` to always be respected regardless of the remote endpoint, despite the default `KnownNetworks` and `KnownProxies` defaulting to localhost only. Since this doesn't happen in ASP.NET Core 8.0.17+, the app considers all requests to be non-HTTPS since they come over HTTP from the edge, which lead to an infinite redirect situation with the app trying to redirect the user to HTTPS.

# Summary

This PR fixes the issue by **allowing `X-Forwarded-Proto` to be respected always**, by clearing `KnownNetworks` and `KnownProxies` in the configuration, meaning all remote endpoints are allowed to set this header. This matches the logic for most of our other web applications, including [StackMail](https://github.com/StackEng/StackMail/blob/b47fa3bc608e18ebfb8e6114fb6f8ddc9cce7c8d/StackMail.AspNetCore/Program.cs#L99-L103), [Scheduler](https://github.com/StackEng/Scheduler/blob/6e550c38de5ef7ca4f670fc1156f4607f5b5c148/src/Scheduler.Host/Startup.cs#L93-L97), [SocketServer](https://github.com/StackEng/SocketServer/blob/c6a23d6b8059b8bc247c091fa77c2d0337709e61/SocketServer/Program.cs#L130-L132), [StackSnippets](https://github.com/StackEng/StackSnippets/blob/d22c6e3eeb50adf01479199ed8d2f8105310b24e/src/StackSnippets/Startup.cs#L28-L32) and more. This was how the `X-Forwarded-Proto` header was being dealt with in ASP.NET Core 8.0.16 and below in this repo.

We are **trusting that our edge CDNs / Proxies will clear these `X-Forwarded-` headers** and set them according to the remote endpoints they're talking to. See here for details on how this should happen: https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/a/28907/629.

Additionally, a big change in this PR is that I'm **removing the `TrustedHeadersMiddleware`** in favour of the standard logic in `ForwardedHeadersMiddleware`. This is to reduce the complexity of how we're handling these `X-Forwarded-` headers and remove custom logic that's already handled by ASP.NET Core's built-in middleware. This means that **the `X-Forwarded-For` header containing the user's real IP is now _also_ allowed to be set by any remote endpoint**, and we're trusting the edge CDNs / Proxies to handle sanitization appropriately as mentioned above.

Finally, this PR also upgrades the codebase to the latest ASP.NET Core (currently 8.0.17) by reverting #23093.

# Technical Details

The call to `services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(...)` has been moved into `StartupExtensions.AddStackOverflowCommonAspNet` for all apps that make use of this helper. ChannelsDbApi doesn't use this helper so it still calls this directly and doesn't bother with the `X-Forwarded-Host` support required by the other apps for GitHub Codespaces.

`ControllerBaseTest.GetRemoteIPTest()` tested some cases of remote IP address handling that no longer applies with this change. In particular, `ForwardedHeadersMiddleware` no longer rejects `X-Forwarded-For` being set to IP addresses we consider internal. This was a failsafe that `TrustedHeadersMiddleware` / `StackExchangeNetwork.GetRemoteIP` had to guard against requests coming via the CDNs and somehow reporting as internal. This failsafe no longer exists - we rely on the CDN to report the remote IP correctly.

I've instead created a new `RequestUtilTests` class to test `RequestUtil.GetRemoteIP()` and verify its logic directly without also involving middleware in the process. I still need to create tests that verify IP address handling in reality now, likely using `TestServer` or something like that to spin up the app as prod-like as I can get it but ideally not depending on SQL / Elastic / Redis.

I've also introduced a new test class and test called `StartupExtensionsTests.UseStackHeaders_RespectsXForwardedHeaders` that verifies the middleware behaviour when you call `services.AddStackOverflowCommonAspNet()` and `app.UseStackHeaders()`. This test method is quite meaty because it spins up a `TestServer` and doesn't make use of the existing `TestServerFixture` to try to keep things simple (that fixture loads _a lot_ of stuff) and allow the test to run parallel with all other tests.

## How to Test

In addition to the new unit tests, you can test this locally by sending HTTP requests directly to the app (e.g. at `http://meta.stackexchange.local`) and fiddling with various `X-Forwarded-` request headers. You should see that the app should always accept your `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-For` header values, which you can test using `/developer/headers`.

This can also be tested by deploying the PR release to a Dev environment for the various product variants. Here's a checklist of the ones tested so far:

- [x] SOE - https://aks.dev.stackenterprise.co/
  - Requires this PR to be deployed across the customer base: https://github.com/StackEng/teams-kubernetes/pull/101
- [x] FBB - https://stackoverflowteams.dev/
- [x] Pubplat - https://load-test.stackoverflow.dev/
- [x] PR Env SOE - https://23169-enterprise.stackoverflow.cloud/
- [x] PR Env Teams - https://23169-blueshift.stackoverflow.cloud/
- [x] PR Env Pubplat - https://23169.stackoverflow.cloud/
title: SCALE-530 Fix X-Forwarded-Proto header not being respected in ASP.NET Core 8.0.17+

Aggregator tests currently stop the aggregator thread and waits until the thread completes. This is because the aggregator thread could consume the aggregator queue and affect the aggregator tests that call the aggregator methods directly. 

However, we are now isolating the Redis cache for the threads, so although the aggregator is running in the background, it's not using the same Redis caches (queues) than these tests, so we no longer need to stop it. 

The aggregator has a some locks with timeouts of up to a minute, that's why we are seeing the aggregator tests taking over a min even though there are only 2 aggregator tests and they seem pretty straight forward.

ApiV3 implements multiple rate limiters and each adds a set of headers to the request, which allows the callers to know when to back off and pace the requests. 

These headers works well in FBB, however in SOE we are not returning it back to the client. The reason for this is that in SOE, ApiV3 is proxied, and the proxy only relays a few headers back to the user, which don't include the rate limiting ones.

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary

**This change will effect PubPlat, Teams and Enterprise.**

Application `Role` is used in a handful of places including as a tag in Datadog metrics. API v2 and v3 projects use the same `Role` on startup which causes both API versions to be tagged as `apiv2`. This makes it impossible to tell whether the metrics are derived from API v2 or API v3.

This PR:
- Adds the tag `service` which will allow us to differentiate API v2 from API v3. 
    - The value of this tag comes from the environment variable `DD_SERVICE`.
       - Locally, this is configured in the project's web.config for use by IIS (Windows only)
       - In production, this value is defined in the Helm variable files
           - API v2 - https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/319874307b4f79725880fbe1168305cb5671eb3b/charts/apiv2/values.yaml#L51
           - API v3 -   https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/319874307b4f79725880fbe1168305cb5671eb3b/charts/apiv3/values.yaml#L49
- Renames the API role tag from `apiv2` to `api`. 

**Expected Outcome:**
- Datadog metrics from API v2 and v3 should have their `role` tag value set to `api` . 
- Datadog metrics from API v2 and v3 will have their `service` tag value set to the environment variable `DD_SERVICE`
- Datadog costs will increase since we are adding a new tag with a handful of different values set in Helm variable files.
- After this PR is merged, Datadog metric queries should follow a pattern like: `role:api , service:api-v2, instance:ascn-dev, product:pubplat `.

A [preview of the new tags can be seen in the `ascn-dev` environment](https://us3.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?fromUser=false&start=1750266863464&end=1750268663464&paused=false#-wogKiuWRZSwK0hqRheGyYoRcyRKLyVRqJMaqxeBDYnzmnjgUCcRiCWw02I+CEJQwWpOmOlmeypK1p+PpeyZxzglSm5xwl2ut3uj15Gje+AFfwBEVFMQlAFZpdCMnK4XlFcUkiqQGrbZqVtqmHA9VkDUaTWYzRbPtbKXbyU6IMt4us6TsPYcvadfWzA1yQy8w-). (You may need to change the time frame to see data)

**Code showing the same `Role` in different API projects**
https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/dc022652bf677f5ad0101e5ed14555233db3e1a8/StackOverflow.Api.V2/Startup.cs#L68-L75

https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/dc022652bf677f5ad0101e5ed14555233db3e1a8/StackOverflow.Api.V3/Startup.cs#L101-L108

## How to Test
**Datadog Metrics**
[Clone the Dog Stats Monitor repo](https://github.com/StackEng/DogStatsMonitor) and then run the following two commands so that we can print only the `dotnet.kestrel.requests.current"` metric.

```
cd C:\code\DogStatsMonitor
dotnet run --project .\src\DogStatsMonitor\DogStatsMonitor.csproj -- metrics --metric "dotnet.kestrel.requests.current"
```

1. Run the Datadog Stats monitor tool
2. Start up API v3
3. Make a request to any endpoint and note that the `service` tag in the Dog Stats Monitor contains the value `api-v3`, the `role` tag should be set to `api`
4. Repeat step 3 but with the API v2 project, the `service` tag value should be `api-v2` and the `role` tag to `api`
title: YETI2-555 Add Datadog service tag

author: aalear
body:
We have chosen to go ahead with `main-test` as our primary test/dev environment for merged PRs. `main-stg` helped us migrate apps to GCP by being the environment where we ran apps in hybrid mode, e.g. app in GCP and databases in NY. Now that the data centers are being actively shut down, the `main-stg` environment is starting to break.

This PR makes two changes:

2. removes a few conditionals in the step that deploys to `main-test`. That step only runs on merged PRs, so it doesn't make sense to have `ascn-dev` as a fallback anyway and by the time that's removed, we may as well just specify the targets directly rather than through variables.

author: gcasar
body:
A continuation of https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.ProductEvents/pull/18 

In short - we were exposing `StackOverflow.Observability` from `ProductEvents` due to how things came to be which lead to 3 competing ways to get `IMonitoringEvents`:

1. Using the original, but abstract `MonitoringEvents` from the monolith
2. Using the later exported, but _should have been internal_ version from `StackOverflow.ProductEvents`
3. Using the latest library `StackOverflow.Observability` -> this is likely the north star

With the PR from @threefjefff we now remove the option no2.

**What are the differences between 1 and 3?**

Yea, ideally we should reconcile those. However, in practice -> if you're not in the Monolith -> use `StackOverflow.Observability`. That one provides OTEL library to use through its abstraction.
If you are in the monolith -> Continue to use `MonitoringEvents` or `ModuleMonitoringEvents`. This is implemented using a DataDog backed implementation directly and we are not likely to switch to using another indirection (OTEL) for the monolith.

**Follow ups**

Likely followups that would make sense:
- Replace `MonitoringEventsProxy` with `ModuleMonitoringEvents` -> medium priority
- Move `ITraceContext` to `StackOverflow.Observability` -> low priority
- Have `MonitoringEvents` implement `IMonitoringEvents` -> we're basically at feature pairity at this point.

---

**Testing**
This is not a big change so I don't expect explosions at runtime. I will definitely monitor my own Gauges after this is merged and extra scrutny should be made for metrics steming from `StackOverflow.Module.Events`. I'm also relying on our FAT tests to click through some happy paths.

I'll give a shout in #engineering

Historic context can be found [here](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C05U6196PCN/p1746695736786339)

## Summary

Jira: TEAMS-14654

**What is in this PR**:
- Add 2 new settings: `Tags.TagSubscriptionDailyBatchSize` (default 1000) and `Tags.TagSubscriptionPostsCount` (default 10) to limit the number of subscriptions processed each time and the number of posts shown in an email.
- Make the scheduled route scheduled/tag-digest-daily to run every 30 minutes until finishing all daily tag subscriptions.
- Only display 10 posts in each email, sorting by highest score, then oldest posts.
- Add more logs to capture exceptions at the email generation steps
- Add try/catch when processing each email batch so that if an error happens, it can continue with other emails
- Calculate the cutoff time based on the `LastSendDate` field (table: `TagSetRows`) in the database for each user's subscriptions instead of from cache.


## How to Test
- Update value of 2 new site settings to make it small so that we can test it (Ex:  1 for [Tags.TagSubscriptionDailyBatchSize](https://stackenterprise.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Tags.TagSubscriptionDailyBatchSize) and 2 for [Tags.TagSubscriptionPostsCount](https://stackenterprise.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Tags.TagSubscriptionPostsCount))
- Have at least 3 different users for testing. Subscribing 2 users for the daily tag digest and 1 user for the 15-minute tag digest. For testing purposes, if you already have these subscriptions in the database, update the `TagSetRows` to set the `LastSendDate` fields to null
```
 UPDATE [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].dbo.TagSetRows
 SET LastSendDate = null
 WHERE TagSetTypeId = 1 and NotificationFrequencyTypeId in (1, 2)
```
- Create 4 or 5 questions with tags that the above 3 users follow
- Run the [daily scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily).
- Check that only 1 email is sent to 1 user who subscribes to the daily tag digest. Use the below query to check the email.
```
SELECT *
FROM [Local.Enterprise.Sites.Teams].[dbo].[EmailMessages]
ORDER BY CreationDate desc
```
- Copy the content of the `BodyHtmlTemplate` field to a blank HTML file and verify that only 2 ([Tags.TagSubscriptionPostsCount](https://stackenterprise.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Tags.TagSubscriptionPostsCount)) posts display in the email.
- Check the `LastSendDate` field is updated for the above user, but still null for the remaining users.
```
SELECT *
FROM [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].dbo.TagSetRows
WHERE TagSetTypeId = 1 NotificationFrequencyTypeId in (1, 2)
```
- Run the [daily scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) again and verify everything is correct for the last user who subscribes to the daily tag digest.
- Run the [daily scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) again and verify no email will be sent
- Run the [15-minute scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/tag-digest-fifteen-minutes) and verify email sent and LastSendDate updated for the user who subscribes to the 15-minute tag digest.
- For testing purposes, Update the LastSendDate to 2 days before the current UTC date.
```
 UPDATE [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].dbo.TagSetRows
 SET LastSendDate = DATEADD(day, -2, GETUTCDATE())
 where TagSetTypeId = 1 and NotificationFrequencyTypeId in (1,2)
```
- Run the [daily scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) and Run the [15-minute scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/tag-digest-fifteen-minutes) again then verify you receive 3 emails and the LastSendDate updated to the current UTC time.

body: # Summary This PR adds logic to save integration test db's into the github action cache after bootstrapping the test network. Thus allowing us to re-use these backups on subsequent test runs as long as there haven't been any Migration changes. The behavior will be such that: * `main` branch commits will cache the baked db's so subsequent main branch runs and PR's can re-use them. * If a feature branch has migration changes: it will create and cache its own db's on the first run and re-use the cached db's on subsequent commits to the feature branch. It's worth noting that feature branches can use main branch caches and caches from the feature branch itself. But main branch runs can only access caches created on the main branch. ## Contained Users It's worth mentioning that it turns out our integration tests don't use contained database users like we do in production. I updated our test networks to use contained users now which is what allows us to re-use pre-baked channels schema db's. # How to Test Changes can be confirmed on this very PR: * Here's the first run where there are no pre-baked db's: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15640626802?pr=23121 * That run created the following cache entry: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/caches?query=key%3Atestdbs-cache- * And here's a subsequent run I triggered where the workflow re-uses the cached db's: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15640626802/job/44069157385?pr=23121 * The cache usage, aka "Fast Path" in the bootstrapper, can be confirmed by looking at the bootstrapper logs: Here are the test runtimes before and after (I highlighted the longest running tests only): ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f991aa6-ade1-4952-897e-b7d80deec64f)

author: ProductiveRage
body:
We're going to change the question list preferences for all users whose current question list preferences were not configured through the Filters dialog. So if you are on "Active" because that's the tab you clicked last, you will be in our sights.

The `ExplicitlySetSortOrder` property on the [UserQuestionList](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/7dc412cb75cfba7fc1b71560474e59781bc272bb/StackOverflow.Common/Models/DataContexts/DBContext.Tables.cs#L410) is set if the Filters dialog was used, and this will be captured in the serialised preferences data in the `Users` table's `PreferencesRaw` values. If it ends with `;1` then the Filters dialog was used - eg.

```
[224|True][160|;MostVotes;;;1][10|50]
```

^ _(It's the section with the `160` identifier that relates to question list preferences)_

Values that do no have the `;1` suffix did not get set through the Filters dialog - eg.

```
[222|False][160|;RecentActivity;]
```

This PR is only part of it (I've been struggling to get this far, so I'm going to try to get this much approved, then move on to the next bit!) -

1. It adds a developer route for us to update `User` records that have `NULL` values for `PreferencesRaw`, to add a preference for "Unanswered" question list
2. It adds a developer route for us to update `User` records that have non-`NULL` values for `PreferencesRaw`, but where those preferences don't include anything about the question list

(People _do_ exist that visit tag search pages but without having preferences for it - I think that they're only saved against the `User` record when they are set, whether by clicking a tab or using the Filters dialog)

The "part two" PR will need to add a developer route that updates `User` records that have non-`NULL` values for `PreferencesRaw` which _do_ include question list preferences - we need to change those values if they do not correspond with `ExplicitlySetSortOrder` being `true`, and leave them untouched where that flag _would_ be set.

We also need to take a backup of the current preferences, but I suspect that it will be easiest / most effective / reliable to do that through Snowflake (download a CSV of a snapshot of the data, before hitting any dev routes in prod).

author: TheSpivack
body:
## Summary

After turning on the UserSignedUp events for Braze, we started seeing duplicate users in Braze - in each case, one of the users in Braze is an unidentified user (email only without external_id), and the other is the user created by the UserSignedUp message handler.

We determined that the duplicates are a result of a race condition between users being tracked in Braze from 2 different ways. The user without the external_id is created when the user is first synced to OneTrust, while the user with the external_id is created from the user sign up event handler in the monolith.  If the OneTrust sync occurs before or around the same time the user verified their email (which fires the UserSignedUp event), this results in the duplicate Braze records.

This PR updates the UserSignedUp event handler code so that the [Braze Identify Users endpoint](https://www.braze.com/docs/api/endpoints/user_data/post_user_identify) is called.  By doing this, after the user with the external_id is created in Braze from the monolith, any other Braze accounts with the same email address will be merged into the newly created user account.

## How to Test

1. See testing steps in #22820 
2. Note the `web.customer_engagement.braze.users_identified.count` metric is being published
title: [BLAZE-26] Call Identify User to Resolve Duplicates in Braze

body:
## Summary
[YETI2-527](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-527)
This PR adds a new AEH event (`left_nav.click`) and attaches a new Stimulus Controller to our front end to fire the event when left nav item links are clicked. This behavior has a site setting that can toggle it on per site.

A Stimulus controller was used so that the event can be wired up to other left nav elements in the future. Currently it is only attached to LeftNavItem.cshtml elements on the left nav but can be easily added anywhere else we want to track navigation on the left nav.

A bit of extra data has been added to facilitate AW-1406

## How to Test

### Configuration

Make sure these site settings have been enabled by impersonating a user that has access to site settings
- Stack events on the StackApps site (/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Site.EnableStackEvents) because it is a per site setting
- Left nav link from any network site (/developer/site-settings/edit?name=StackApps.EnableYourAppsInLeftNav) because it is a global value
- AEH events on left nav for the site you are working with (/developer/site-settings/edit?name=LeftNav.EnableLeftNavItemAehEvents)

### Test

Front end validation
1. Visit Stack Apps.
2. Open your browser network tab (CTRL+Shift+i => network) and look for a 'stackevent' call.
3. Validate that is shows a location and destination and that it shows that the POST response was 200.

Back end validation
There are two options for Backend validation. You can hook up Kafka tools to look at AEH events by following [this](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/articles/25015) set of instructions, or you can add a breakpoint to StackEventController.cs line 22 and follow the event through its backend life cycle and validate that the user is attached

# Summary

SCIM might be a good feature set to be extracted into a module but I'm a bit dubious on the benefit of doing that with all the wrapper classes modules need to get things done. It would make SCALE-260 work to implement site importer integration a lot more difficult (as we found out implementing Connectivity to the site importer - we had to hack that in). Going to leave that out of scope for this PR.

# Testing

There shouldn't be any functional changes in this PR. Existing automated tests hopefully cover everything here.

That said, I've added PR environments to double check that the SCIM admin settings and SCIM API endpoints still work correctly.

// forcefully run the aggregator on a background thread

author: daleksiuk
body:
TEAMS-14637

## Summary

Previous to this PR, we would construct a list of deactivated accounts (Lloyd's has over 6200) and do an `IN` clausein SQL to make sure that the current name being checked isn't in that list. From the stack trace it looks like that is the line that is failing.

### Performance 

I artificially added in 6500 deactivated IDs into the code and 250 account IDs to check against them. Because the check against the deactivated ID hashset is a "not" check it has to hit each one. Locally on my machine there was no visible difference when doing the fake check when I looked at the profiler numbers for the entire submission process.

However - in production we loop over each each name in the list and do the entire check for each name. The deactivation check has to run for each name. We could optimize this but I liked keeping this fix within the condition where it only runs for Enterprise.

### Implementation Notes

- This PR selects the deactivated accounts into a variable and then filters out any users whose accounts are in that list.
- The deactivated account IDs are a HashSet so the lookup should be very fast
- The original implementation made sure that user groups are always included and this is still true.
- I think this code could be made even more efficient but I like that it is kept within a conditional that is Enterprise-only (`Account.AllowDeactivation`)

## How to Test

The only way this code path gets hit is if deactivation of accounts is allowed (always true on Enterprise, and only true on Enterprise) and if there is at least one deactivated account in the system.

### Part A - deactivated users should not be saved
1. Make sure you're on Enterprise
2. Deactivate a user that isn't your current admin user. I updated the DB directly: `update [Local.Enterprise.Sites.Teams].dbo.Accounts set IsDeactivated = 1 where Id = <id of user>;`
3. As an admin, navigate to the [tags page](https://stackenterprise.local/tags)
4. Click the link in the table under the "SMEs" header to add or remove SMEs from the tag
5. Add your deactivated user to the list and save - they should not be saved. Note that this code path runs whether or not the deactivated user is added to the SME list.

### Part B - user groups
There is specific code to ensure that user groups are always included. The points below are to ensure that user groups still save properly
1. Make sure you're on Enterprise
2. If you haven't deactivated a user from the steps above, do so now (see point 2 above for instructions)
3. As an admin, navigate to the [tags page](https://stackenterprise.local/tags)
4. Click the link in the table under the "SMEs" header to add or remove SMEs from the tag
5. Add your user group and save.

### Other testing
Removing SMEs and saving without changes should still work as before. Note that if there is a user in the SME list and they are then deactivated, they will still be in the list until it is saved again.

author: animuson
body:
## Summary

Jira: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-14634

The current schema definitions available in the Swagger UI for API v3 are very generic and don't provide important information. Particularly, the `body` variable is provided in HTML for questions, answers, and articles but that is not clear because bodyMarkdown is only returned if you query for an individual post - it is not returned in lists of those posts. This has already caused confusion for some clients who thought it would be returned as Markdown.

This change makes it explicit for each post type (as well as comments, which return body as Markdown for some reason) which format is being returned for each of them. It also makes the descriptions of these variables more consistent across post types.

While I was testing, I noticed that the schema definition for IsAnswered was also wrong. It claimed that it could be true if there was an accepted answer. This is not correct. The database column which API v3 pulls from is strictly for having an upvoted answer only and does not pay attention to accepted state at all.

This does not change any functionality. It only changes the textual descriptions for the request and response models.

## How to Test

Ensure that each post type shows the correct line in its related schema. The schema can be accessed via the grey boxes at the bottom of the Swagger UI, or by clicking the Schema button in the example response of the relevant endpoint.
title: TEAMS-14634: Update schema definition of body variables to specify HTML vs Markdown

author: ProductiveRage
body:
## The history
In PR #22971, I had changed a line in the `static StagingGroundPrefs Get(int userId)` method following this call:

```
var json = cn.DB.QuerySingleOrDefault<string>("Select StagingGroundPrefs From UserMetadata Where UserId = @Id", new { Id = userId });
```

When I was writing unit tests for the `QuestionsController`, `cn.DB.QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` was returning null and I presumed that it must have been a behaviour of `QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` that I had misunderstood, and that its concept of `null` for a `string` was a default blank string value. As such, I changed the `??` null coalesce check into `string.IsNullOrEmpty(..)` and my test code worked, and all other tests did, and I went about my day.

In that PR, there was [a comment](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/22971#discussion_r2131851337) from @gcasar  -

> This bit I do feel strongly about - its tackling a totally unrelated bug to the code and I'd like us to move it to a separate PR in the future. That way its easier to revert/review on its own.

## The confusion
Although it didn't block that PR, it weighed on me, and I dug into it again.

It turns out that an `NSubstitute`-instantiated `IDBContext` reference will return a blank value (rather than `null`) from any method that returns a `string` that hasn't had a behaviour explicitly specified. So it was only _my test code_ that was affected.

## The controversy
I could have specified a behaviour on the `NSubstitute`-provided `IDBContext`, such `QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` calls would return null (overriding the `NSubstitute` blank-string default). And maybe I should have done! (This PR is a draft, and a discussion, and so I may backtrack, if you think that what I did instead is terrible).

Overriding `IDBContext` methods is such a coarse way of mocking things out in our unit tests, and so it always gets my shackles up. Plus, I felt like this was a really weird, surprising decision on the part of `NSubstitute` (is everyone else aware of it??)

As such, I did some Googling, and found a way to add some code (by reading [GitHub issues, like this one](https://github.com/nsubstitute/NSubstitute/pull/705#issuecomment-1285460860) to the `StackOverflowUnitTestFramework`* so that every test that uses that class will get `null` strings by default from `string`-returning methods of mocks that have not had explicit behaviour assigned.

\* _(Currently, the projects `StackOverflow.Tests.Unit` and `StackOverflow.Tests.Unit.Common` and `StackOverflow.Tests.Unit.RazorViews` all use `StackOverflowUnitTestFramework` but there are unit test projects for modules that do not - I have avoided meddling with them too much, though it may be worth thinking about in the near future; how consistent they should be with our "main" unit test projects)_

## The ask
I could genuinely go either way on this. If a review strongly suggests that I change the code that changes the `NSubstitute` default behaviour (particularly if you, or others, find it logical and/or non-surprising) then I'll remove the "magic" and stub out the `cn.DB.QuerySingleOrDefault<string>(..)` in my test code.

But I wanted to get an opinion about whether this was going to _reduce_ confusion in the future.

**Observation from me:** If it _does_ reduce confusion in the future, it will probably be more so the case for this style of "fat unit test", that targets a large surface area (like a controller), and smaller-scoped tests will be less likely to have to worry about how many things may be attempted during an operation under test.

---------------------------------------------------

- [x] I've added instructions on how to test this PR.
- [x] I've added unit and integration tests as appropriate, or justified their absence.
- [x] This PR can be reviewed in a few hours at most. (Please consider splitting it up otherwise.)
- [x] If this is a work in progress, I've marked this as a draft PR.

MOD-136 | Meta: [Change semicolon to a comma in "To put other Markdown blocks in a list; just indent four spaces for each nesting level"](https://meta.stackexchange.com/q/410549/209031) ## Summary ### Issue 1 The following text is not grammatically correct > To put other Markdown blocks in a list; just indent four spaces for each nesting level A semicolon can only join two independent clauses, and "To put other Markdown blocks in a list" is an [introductory infinitive phrase](https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/general_writing/punctuation/commas/commas_after_introductions.html). Can be fixed by replacing `;` with a `,` ### Issue 2 The following html is not valid ``` 

Hi

``` Paragraphs can only contain "phrasing content" (text, inline elements, etc). The browsers parser will automatically close the opening paragraph tag, essentially turning it into ``` 

Hi

``` Where the last tag is unclosed. We can just wrap in a div instead. > [!NOTE] > Sometimes changing the DOM structure can do funky things with assumptions we've made in CSS/JS, so we should just test that valid version looks and works the same, but this is a pretty trivial change, so not expecting a lot of chaos here. Actually, looks like we were relying on the paragraph terminating before the `
` block in order to provide spacing in between, so I'll just close early, rather than wrap in a div

## How to Test

1. Check [`/editing-help`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/editing-help)

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
The Fragment Proxy allows you to register a service prefix such as `/my-service` in the monolith for which all requests will be proxied to another service to provide UI pages and components inside the monolith.

However, the registration of service prefixes happens after the monolith routes have been registered which means that if there is a service prefix that overlaps with an existing route, the existing route will not be handled.

For example:

- Given the monolith route `/feature-x/list`
- Given the service prefix `/feature-x` in `fragment-proxies.*.json`

Calling `https://stackoverflow.com/feature-x/list` is now proxied to the service rather than being handled by the monolith.

As the Fragment Proxy also registers a wild card route there is no straightforward way to decide which one should "win".
Therefore, this PR introduces a check that when service prefixes are registered it will look for overlaps and refuse to start the application.

The error is logged and looks like this:

```
System.InvalidOperationException: The service prefix for Fragment Proxy must be unique.
Found conflicting routes for service prefix: /feature-x:
- feature-x/list
```
title: [FRAGMENT PROXY] Refuse to start if a service prefix overlaps

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
This PR Isolates all the DBs used by channels in IsolatedDBChannelInstanceBaseTest:
- Sites DB
- Channels DB
- Channels schemas DB
- Parent site content DB

As for the `IsolatedDatabaseTest`, the backups are taken by the bootstrapper before tests start running (they are the same backups!). The main difference is that we are claiming a channel **before** taking the backups, this way, when we restore the databases for a test class, everything is ready to be used (the channel and the admin). 

As the boostraper lives in the `StackOverflow.Tests.Integration` project, in order to be able to claim a channel before taking the backups, I had to move some channel specific test helpers from `StackOverflow.Tests.Integration.Channels` to `StackOverflow.Tests.Integration`.

Addtionally, I isolated for ambient the channels snapshot. This snapshot is reloaded every time that a channel is claimed and this cache is used in multiple places. As we can potentially have multiple ChannelsDBs running at the same time, we have to isolate this cache to avoid flakiness. I did it using `AmbientIsolatableObject`. 

The rest is mostly using the same concepts as I used for isolating DBS for `IsolatedDatabaseTest`, using asynclocals for the connectionstrings mappings.

Finally, there is a targeted but impactful change in connection string localization. In this PR I encountered a few more times the problem of replacing a substring and then having it to replace it back. I did that those times, which was getting ugly but _it worked_. However, I hit a problem with a specific scenario where the ChannelsSnapshot loaded an already localized version of the connectionstring and we tried to localize it again, which failed. So, after having so much pain with this, I bit the bullet and introduced escaping of the `\;` and `\=`. As we were having problems with suffixes, I only used the `\;`, but both are supported. 

The escaping implementation is quite simple. I replaced `\;` and `\=` with 2 different GUIDs (to ensure that I'm not picking an extra char that could be used in the connectionstring), then do the regular splitting by `;` and then by `=`, to finally revert the GUIDs for `;` and `=`. 


## Testing
In a `IsolatedDBChannelInstanceBaseTest` I added watches for the name of all the databases:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86a2c095-e2d5-4c65-91d8-9bcc188243e3)

This is what I got:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66910a39-1d23-45fd-8c93-a1e21280b3f0)
title: SCALE-514 IsolatedDBChannelInstanceBaseTest Improvements

body:
[KRAKEN-2320](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/KRAKEN-2320)
## Summary
This PR expands upon our logic that controls the visibility of entries to a coding challenge. The new changes include:

- Refactoring our existing logic into its on function
- Moved the days to hide coding challenge entries into a site setting
- Gave entry visibility to discussion mods
- Added challenge title prefix site setting to allow for entry visibility for challenges that are not old enough yet

## How to Test
I refactored our big if statement controlling entry visibility out into its own function so there's a bit of backtesting that needs to be done as well.

1. First ensure that the following site settings have these values:
	-```Discussions.DaysToHideCodingChallengeEntries```: 10
	-```Discussions.CodingChallengeEntryDisplayOverrides```: -COMPLETE-
	-```Discussions.CodingChallengeMinPostId```: (no value)

2. Go to the discussions tab
3. If there aren't previous discussions with replys create one and reply to it
4. Ensure that replies are visible to a user that has not replied to the discussion.
5. Take note of the post Id, we will use it later.
6. Impersonate a staff member
7. Create a coding challenge and set ```Discussions.CodingChallengeMinPostId``` to its post Id
8. While still impersonating staff create an entry for the coding challenge.
9. Coding Challenge entries should be visible for you.
10. Create another Coding Challenge with -COMPLETE- at the start of its title and post an entry

11. Impersonate a normal user
12. First hit this endpoint with the post Id you noted in step 5
	-https://meta.stackexchange.local/beta/discussions/<postId>
13. Ensure replies are visible as this is a discussion not a coding challenge.
14. Go to the first Coding Challenge you created, you should not see any entries.
15. Create an entry, replies should become visible
16. Go to the second challenge you created and all entries should be visible

17. Impersonate a user whose account Id is contained in this site setting ```Discussions.ModeratorAccessOverrideEnabledFor.AccountIds```
18. All entries on all challenges should be visible

19. Using a staff account set ```DaysToHideCodingChallengeEntries``` to 0 or null

20. Impersonate another normal user, not the one you impersonated in step 11
21. Entries on the first challenge should be visible to you now
22. Using a staff account set ```DaysToHideCodingChallengeEntries``` to 10
23. The impersonated user from step 20 should no longer see entries in the first challenge

24. Update the posts Creation date in sql to be 10 days old using the following script:
```
UPDATE Posts
SET CreationDate = CAST(GETDATE()-10 as DATE)
WHERE Id = --your post id here--
```


25. Refresh the challenge and entries should now be visible to you


[KRAKEN-2320]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/KRAKEN-2320?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
title: expanding coding challenge entry visibility control logic

author: giamir
body:
[STACKS-758](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/STACKS-758)

## Summary

This PR is adding a playground for engineers to extract candidate components for the [official stacks-svelte library](https://github.com/StackEng/Stacks-Svelte). 
It is integral part of the "Contributing to Stacks Svelte" process discussed in the frontend guild session of May 2025.
See [this diagram](https://lucid.app/lucidspark/21dc8333-98ac-48ce-8cb5-6a931f8b5a41/edit?view_items=sY.liz1C~w8W&invitationId=inv_a91415d7-e17f-42d2-b81f-0164b4a8a677) for a full overview of the process.

We used to have a `@stackeng/shared-components` package with few components with unclear ownership. As part of this PR the `signup` part of that package is being moved to the `signup-modal` island given that most of those component are too domain specific for stacks-svelte. The few components shared with the `homepage-wizard` island are directly exposed from the signup modal (see `exports/index.ts`). The remaining `SearchPopover` and `GradientLoadingIndicator` have been moved to the new `@stackeng/stacks-svelte-labs` package since they are more fitting candidates.

The PR also add few unit tests for those 2 candidate components as well as providing a readme describing what should go in this brand new package and an alternative approach for sharing domain-specific components across islands. A storybook story has also been added for `GradientLoadingIndicator` as an example to showcase how to use storybook.

## How to Test

No functional changes are expected from this PR
- Spin up Core locally and check that all svelte islands being touched are working as expected (this is often just a reference change from `@stackeng/shared-components` to `@stackeng/stacks-svelte-labs`). Pay particular attention to the `signup-modal` and the `homepage-wizard` islands as we moved the shared components between the two in the `signup-modal` island
- From the `StackOverflow` folder run the storybook playground for stacks-svelte-labs: `npm run storybook -w @stackeng/stacks-svelte-labs`, consult the overview (same content of the readme) and the simple `GradientLoadingIndicator` story

[STACKS-758]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/STACKS-758?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
title: STACKS-758: create @stackeng/stacks-svelte-labs package for candidate components of stacks-svelte

This is a [known flaky test](https://us3.datadoghq.com/ci/test/runs?query=test_level%3Atest%20%40test.name%3ADelete_DeletesUserVotesAndSetsRequiresRecalc_OnNonEnterprise&agg_m=count&agg_m_source=base&agg_t=count&currentTab=overview&eventStack=&fromUser=false&start=1748523947535&end=1749128747535&paused=false)
- [This one ](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15449737935/job/43495315259)was on `UserPermissions_WhenFilteringByExternalId_AndExternalIdFilterIsEnabled_ShouldReturnUser`. This is a [known flaky test](https://us3.datadoghq.com/ci/test/runs?query=test_level%3Atest%20%40test.name%3AUserPermissions_WhenFilteringByExternalId_AndExternalIdFilterIsEnabled_ShouldReturnUser%20%40test.status%3Afail&agg_m=count&agg_m_source=base&agg_t=count&currentTab=overview&eventStack=&fromUser=false&index=citest&start=1748524068722&end=1749128868722&paused=false)
- [This one](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15449737935/job/43544207058?pr=23014) had two flakes
  - [This one ](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/runs/43545200802) was on `Close_votes_should_age_away_after_14_days_and_allow_recasting`. This is a [known flaky test](https://us3.datadoghq.com/ci/test/runs?query=test_level%3Atest%20%40test.name%3AClose_votes_should_age_away_after_14_days_and_allow_recasting%20%40test.status%3Afail&agg_m=count&agg_m_source=base&agg_t=count&currentTab=overview&eventStack=&fromUser=false&index=citest&start=1746539112083&end=1749131112083&paused=false)

author: dionrhys
body:
This PR adds in logic to retry individual failed integration tests in CI to hopefully drastically reduce the flakiness of the "Build, test and package" workflow.

Whenever a dotnet test run fails and a .trx file was generated (indicating tests did run, it likely wasn't a runner failure), we'll parse the failed tests out of the .trx (XML) file and run dotnet test again with the `--filter` argument set to run the specific tests that failed.

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-test?tabs=dotnet-test-with-vstest#filter-option-details
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/testing/selective-unit-tests?pivots=xunit

This will likely not fix _all_ flakiness, since it doesn't recreate the SQL / Elastic / Redis services (which contain shared state that's a likely cause of flakiness), but should hopefully help at least somewhat.

Here are examples of flakiness where the retry didn't succeed, likely due to not starting from a clean slate in SQL:

- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15470502183/job/43556125305?pr=23005
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15471868080/job/43560084176?pr=23005

I've not applied this to Unit Tests because those shouldn't flake - there's something very wrong with a test if they do.

I've also not applied this to Functional Acceptance Tests (Playwright tests) because those would need a completely different approach since they're run within Docker using different commands and spin up a lot more shared services. It could be valuable to add this to this suite as well though.

# Testing

The main way to test this is to re-run the "Build, test and package" workflow over and over and verify that flaky tests are being retried and that at least once it's succeeding on a retry where the test(s) didn't succeed the first time.

Since it's hard to see if any Integration Tests job resulted in a failure that then succeeded on a second try, I'm using Datadog to [check for any test failures](https://us3.datadoghq.com/ci/test/repositories/github.com%2Fstackeng%2Fstackoverflow/all-services/dion%2FSCALE-521-individual-test-retries/04016e3a7bfaef51f89b1a9c8e8eb8f50a828203?query=test_level%3Atest%20env%3Aci%20%28%40git.repository.id%3Agithub.com%2Fstackeng%2Fstackoverflow%20OR%20%40git.repository.id_v2%3Agithub.com%2Fstackeng%2Fstackoverflow%29%20%40git.branch%3Adion%2FSCALE-521-individual-test-retries%20%40git.commit.sha%3A04016e3a7bfaef51f89b1a9c8e8eb8f50a828203%20%40test.status%3Afail&colorByAttr=meta%5B%27_dd.ci.test_level%27%5D&currentTab=parent-trace&env=ci&eventStack=&graphType=flamegraph&index=citest&sort=time&start=1748513406438&end=1749139956356&paused=false).

Here's an example of this PR working: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15471868080/job/43560089870?pr=23006

![Screenshot of the retry logic working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea6840e7-cfb8-4014-85ec-8e6ad61009f3)
title: SCALE-521 Retry failed integration tests

author: KyleMit
body:
MOD-134 | [Slack Thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C013ERZ5TEE/p1749034348234849)  

Meta: [Didn't get a notification that the Stack Overflow election started](https://meta.stackexchange.com/questions/410496/didnt-get-a-notification-that-the-stack-overflow-election-started)

## Summary

* Election notifications are typically sent to any eligible voter via a background job that runs with `TaskUtil.RunWithoutExecutionContext` in [NotifyUsers](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/26c8c186025361598dca90e2118c0e3a2ba75384/StackOverflow.Common/Models/ModeratorElection.StateChanges.cs#L243) when the election changes state, in this case to the election phase.
* For stack overflow there should be [**974,559 eligible voters**](https://dataexplorer-local.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/stackoverflow/query/38758/eligible-voter-count-in-election?MinRep=150)
* However, we only sent out [**90,307 inbox notifications**](https://dataexplorer-local.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/stackoverflow/query/38757/electionbegins-notifications?SiteId=1&ElectionId=16)
* The election began on [`2025-06-03 20:00:00Z`](https://stackoverflow.com/election/16) which would have kicked of the notification job
* Around the same time, stack overflow was deployed, finishing at [`2025-06-03 20:12`](https://stackeng.octopus.app/app#/Spaces-1/projects/stackoverflow/deployments/releases/2025.6.3.28248/deployments/Deployments-232664)
* This would have restarted the app pool on the server and seems to have killed any background jobs in the middle of executing
* The current election notification code is **NOT** idempotent, and intended to only be triggered a single time.
* This PR adds a one-time backfill route for this election that will get eligible voters, and then remove voters that have already participated, and re-send notifications to the remaining users.

## How to Test

1. You'll want to create an election locally by going to [`/election`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/election)
2. Create an election and get to the nomination and primary phase
3. Check what your current election id by running the following query

    ```sql
    SELECT TOP 1 *
    FROM [Local.StackExchange.Meta].dbo.ModeratorElections
    ORDER BY Id DESC
    ```

4. Before transitioning to the election phase, we want to emulate a scenario in which all election notifications did not go out. To do that, just add `.Take(100)` to the following line of code

    https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/26c8c186025361598dca90e2118c0e3a2ba75384/StackOverflow.Common/Models/ModeratorElection.StateChanges.cs#L252
    
    ```diff
    - foreach (var accountId in accountIds)
    + foreach (var accountId in accountIds.Take(100))
    ```

6. Now you can move the Election into the "Election" phase to trigger the partial set of notifications
  
6. You can test the number of notifications that have gone out on your local DB with the following query
    
    ```sql
    SELECT *
    FROM [Local.Sites].dbo.Inboxes
    WHERE InboxTypeId = 30 -- ElectionBegins
        AND SiteId = 4 -- MSE
        AND ItemId = 1 -- USE YOUR LOCAL ELECTION ID
    ORDER BY Id DESC
    ```

7. You should see a total count of only 100.

8. You can confirm there should be way more eligible voters with the following query

    ```sql
    SELECT AccountId
    FROM [Local.StackExchange.Meta].dbo.Users
    WHERE Reputation >= 150
      and AccountId is not null
    ```

9. Because we use a redis lock to prevent multiple executions, in order to run the same code again, without having to wait an hour, you'll have to kill the redis key that controls the lock by going to the following route

    https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/redis/killglobalkey/election-transition-to-Election-4

    **NOTE**: Make sure to do this every time before you re-try the backfill route or it won't run

10. Now go hit the backfill route

    https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/election/re-send-notifications

11. You can re-check the inbox notifications count and now it should be incremented by **100** and at **200 total**

12. Now run the backfill route again but pass in a query param to increase the number of accounts to run `?numberOfAccountsToRun=999999`

    https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/election/re-send-notifications?numberOfAccountsToRun=999999

11. You can re-check the inbox notifications count and now it should be now contain all notifications.  If you keep running this for a bit, it should keep incrementing while the job is executing

> [!NOTE]
> However, this will all notifications less the account ids that exist in your local db but don't actually exist on sites database because locally they are not kept in sync. 
> I've updated the route to silently fail when there's a mis-match so it can continue adding notifications for other users
title: MOD-134 add dev backfill route to resend election notifications

author: ProductiveRage
body:
… there may be ONE outlier that needs something different, and then you have to undo things for that one test because you tied yourself to a constructor that has code that "surely will apply in _all_ possible cases".

The changes here have ended up being an illustration of how we _could_ do it, rather than being an illustration of where we could immediately _benefit from doing so_.

I made the changes when I was looking at isolating Elastic from the test `UsersCanViewPublicDiscussionList` in `CollectivePublicDiscussionsControllerTests` and imagined that I would mock out Elastic by mocking out `ICollectiveDiscussionsService` (and so I would a different implementation of that interface in this one particular test).

However, the `CollectiveDiscussionsService` implementation of that interface does _a lot_, and mocking out all of it just to isolate Elastic made me feel like the test wouldn't actually be testing much any more! (Which suggests an opportunity to improve the design.. but it's not been a priority).

## What are you trying to do here??
We _can_ structure our code to remove duplication, without shoving it into constructors, which results in test setup code being spread around rather than being nicely localised.

Sadly, it's a pattern that I've seen happen at Stack quite often ("oh, should we throw that repeated code into the constructor") but the benefits don't offset the costs, in my experience. So if we can demonstrate a way to get the best of both worlds (cut down on duplicated code, have localised arrange / act / assert test code, _and_ make it easy for some tests to use a different configuration) then we might be able to slowly turn the tide.

author: dionrhys
body:
This fixes flakiness caused by race conditions when initializing the static `_options` field on `PerfCounters`.

Before this fix, it's possible to have two threads call `PerfCounters.Source` (for example) at the same time, and this could cause the `Options` getter to run concurrently. When this happened, there was a chance that this could happen:

1. Thread A sees `_options` is null and enters the `if` block
2. Thread B sees `_options` is null and enters the `if` block
3. Thread A sets `_options` to new `MetricSourceOptions()`
4. Thread B sets `_options` to new `MetricSourceOptions()`
5. Thread A calls `_options.DefaultTags.Add("role", ...)`
6. Thread B calls `_options.DefaultTags.Add("role", ...)` // BOOM

Since both threads were working on setting up the same `MetricSourceOptions`, they both end up trying to add the "role" key to the `DefaultTags` dictionary, causing this exception: `System.ArgumentException : An item with the same key has already been added. Key: role`.

This ends up cascading up to any other callers requiring access to `PerfCounters.Options`, for example the `Post` class' type initializer which sets various static counters (`webPostDeleted`, `webPostEdited`, `webQuestionClosed`, `webQuestionReopened`).

This caused the following Unit Test failure: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/runs/43442743451

The fix here is to add locking to the options initialization so that only one thread does this. I've done this by wrapping it in a `Lazy<T>` and moving the initialization code into its value factory. `LazyThreadSafetyMode.ExecutionAndPublication` (the default) is set to ensure that only one thread initializes the object and sets the field. This mode _also_ ensures that any exceptions in initialization will be cached (not the case for `LazyThreadSafetyMode.PublicationOnly`).
title: SCALE-473 Remove flakiness from `PerfCounters.Options` initialization

## Summary
The Quick Answer feature identifies questions that are good candidates for quick answers based on specific criteria. This feature helps users identify questions that need immediate attention and _may_ be answered quickly. These questions will nudge users using a badge under Interesting posts for you on the homepage.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d75b113b-42b0-4905-8123-0714c0257be9)

## Features
- Identifies questions that match specific criteria for quick answers
- Integrates with the homepage question list
- Respects user's watched tags
- Supports site-specific configuration
- All criteria is configurable through site settings


## How to Test

author: kylejrp
body:
KRAKEN-2267

## Summary

This PR adds canonical URLs to the tag listing page in more cases than previous.

Before, the canonical URL would only show up when you had multiple tags and no wildcard tags. Now, it'll show up for any number of tags (including 1) and will show up if you're using a wildcard tag.

Note that it's intentional that we're not bringing in any query parameters along (eg. page number, sorting, etc.). We don't want search engines to index a deep page or different sort as the canonical version of a tag listing page. This is based on the advice from the SEO vendor.

## How to Test

1. Visit https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/discussion. The source code of that page should contain a tag that looks like `<link rel="canonical" href="https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/discussion">`
2. Visit [https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/status*](https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/status*). The source code of that page should contain a tag that looks like `<link rel="canonical" href="https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/status*">`.
3. Try typing in `[status-completed] [discussion]` into the search bar and hit `Enter`. There should be a canonical tag that looks like `<link rel="canonical" href="https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/discussion+status-completed">`
5. Try typing in `[discussion] [status*]` into the search bar and hit `Enter`. There should be no canonical tag for this page. (If we did show it, it would have a bunch of sorted `or`s in it and would be incomprehensible/invalid)
6. Try typing in `[status-completed] and [discussion]` into the search bar and hit `Enter`. You're brought to a different route (`/search`) and aren't subject to this canonicalization.
title: KRAKEN-2267 Add canonical tag for tag listing page in more cases

As described in [the Jira ticket](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/FERRET-971), the "Related Tags" UI component is infrequently used and it would make our lives easier when we pursue killing off Tag Engine if we never showed it.

This change introduces a new site setting `TagEngine.DisableRelatedTagsForQuestionLists` that can either have value `DoNotDisable` _or_ it can have one or more of the values `DisableForZeroTags`, `DisableForSingleTag`, `DisableForMultipleTags` (the first value means "do not show 'Related Tags' on the /questions page", the other values relate to the Tag Search Page and will apply based upon how many tags are present in the user query).

I imagine that we could switch it off in all places without really risking much furore from Meta, but I thought that it would be nice to have the option of disabling it first on /questions (where it doesn't really make sense; "Related Tags" that are related to what? _every_ question that have?!) and on multi-tag views of the Tag Search Page (we would set the new site setting to DisableForZeroTags, DisableForMultipleTags` to do that).

Sorry! I made the changes that I needed to, and then wanted to improve some of the unit test code slightly, and update some of the other tests to be more consistent.

author: kylejrp
body:
KRAKEN-2290

## Summary

This PR adds an activity indicator to the left nav. It only appears if you've already dismissed the "new" indicator on the left sidebar. It also only shows if there's a coding challenge created in the past week.

The activity indicator corresponds to the last time you visited the coding challenge listing page. Any challenges posted after your last viewed date should appear as an activity indicator.

Because this is on the master page, there's some heavy caching: 
- We cache per-server in the local cache your last viewed coding challenge date. 
- If we miss the per-server local cache, we go to the site cache (shared between servers) to get your last viewed coding challenge date. 
- When you visit the listing page for coding challenges, we set/invalidate the caches appropriately
- We store the list of coding challenges in a local cache too

## How to Test

Prerequisite: Make sure you have Docker running so we can hit Redis, otherwise the activity indicator will always show

Before testing, you may want to visit the Coding Challenges page on a separate branch without these changes so you have some users that have their `Preference.VisitedAllPublicDiscussionsPage` set to `false`. Otherwise, you'll only see the "New" indicator instead of the activity indicator.

Also, make sure you have created a coding challenge in the past week in your local environment.

1. As a user with `Preference.VisitedAllPublicDiscussionsPage` set to `false`, visit the homepage
2. The left nav should show an activity indicator of 1 corresponding to your currently active coding challenge.
3. After clicking on the left nav item for coding challenges, the activity indicator should disappear.

1. As a user with `Preference.VisitedAllPublicDiscussionsPage` set to `true`, visit the homepage
2. You should see a "New" indicator instead of an activity indicator
3. After clicking on the left nav item for coding challenges, the "New" indicator should disappear and there should be no activity indicator

At this point, you could create another coding challenge to see how it affects the activity indicator on either of your test accounts. You'll need to wait for the cache to clear before it'll update - a rebuild should reset the local cache.
title: KRAKEN-2290 Create activity indicator for coding challenges

author: gabrieltron
body:
## Summary

On APIv3 tests, controllers are tested by spinning up a web server that executes requests received by the tests. The problem is that creating this web server is a very slow operation, and we were doing so for every single test. This caused a huge delay before executing every test. This is a Flame Graph of an APIv3 test on Datadog:

![Untitled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe6b202a-34e6-4f31-b714-bf5364bf3fa9)

Notice that it only starts to actually run the test after 4 seconds, and then the actual test ran in 1 second.

To solve this issue this PR makes so the web app is initialized only once, and then reused for every test. It also uses `AsyncLocal` to override the web app in specific tests that require custom configuration and therefore can't use the default web app.

## How to Test

Check CI runs for the [last commit](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15492807541/job/43622621545?pr=22961). Notice that execution time of APIv3 tests went down from ~12 minutes to 2 minutes. Also, the workflow ran 10 times and APIv3 haven't flaked in any of them
title: SCALE-461: Use shared WebApp for APIv3 test

author: ProductiveRage
body:
Reverts #22763 - as discussed on a call on Friday with Scale Pod, I think that there could be some useful learnings in here for when we start leaning more heavily into unit tests (where "unit test" means no shared state, no out-of-process comms - rather than it meaning "a single unit of code under test") but I also understand that it means that where we used to have test coverage that exercised our Redis integration (even if that isn't explicitly part of the test's intent) we would no longer have that.

I think that we should aim to have fewer tests rely on dependencies that they don't really care about (like Redis, in the case of many tests) but that should be done in tandem with adding some tests that _do_ explicitly test the functionality the relies upon Redis. While the PR being reverted demonstrated how that could be done, it didn't look for everywhere that it _should_ be done, and so it introduced some risk that we think doesn't offset the (hoped-for!) benefits of reduced flakiness (and maybe slight performance improvements, though that was never a primary driver of the changes).

We talked about whether we should revert all of the changes, or whether we should keep some of them (so long as it's clear how one testing strategy should be used compared to another, to avoid making things harder for future work by devs rather than easier) but I think that it makes sense right now to revert it in its entirety. I'm dipping in and out of test initiatives, amongst my other other work, and I _might_ have proposed trying to keep some of this work if that wasn't the case.. or I might not! We'll still have the changes in the commit history, and the old PR will be available, if we want to pick this up again in the future. It might be useful for when we want to consider lifting-and-shifting some integration tests into "fat unit tests" - we'll see, when (and if) that time arises!
title: Revert "EXPERIMENT: Try mocking out Redis for integration tests"

## Summary
This PR prevents a couple of modals from closing when clicking outside because these modals contain information that the users don't want to lose until they dismiss the modals. This is done by adding the `preventCloseOnClickOutside` property. This PR adds that property to modals that contain API key, client secret, as well as the modal for editing app details.

For the API Key and Client Secret modals (generate new and rotate), `preventCloseOnClickOutside` is set based on `panelIndex` value (when it equals 1) so it prevents closing on clicking outside only when the modal contains API key or client secret.

## How to Test

1. [Impersonate user 5](https://22958.stackoverflow.cloud/impersonate/5)
2. [Go to user's application page](https://22958-stackapps.stackexchange.cloud/applications/view/1) and test the following:

### Edit Modal
  - Press 'Edit details' > click outside of the modal > modal does not disappear > click 'Cancel' > modal disappears

### Generate API Key Modal
  - Open modal by pressing 'Generate new API Key' > click outside of the modal > modal disappears 
  - Open modal by pressing 'Generate new API Key' > click 'Cancel' > modal disappears
  - Open modal by pressing 'Generate new API Key' > enter valid name and choose expiration > click 'Generate' > click outside of the modal > modal does not disappear > click 'Done' > modal disappears

### Rotate API Key Modal
  - Open modal by pressing 'Rotate' > click outside of the modal > modal disappears 
  - Open modal by pressing 'Rotate'> click 'Cancel' > modal disappears
  - Open modal by pressing 'Rotate' > click 'Yes, rotate' > click outside of the modal > modal does not disappear > click 'Done' > modal disappears

### Generate Client Secret Modal
  - Open modal by pressing 'Generate new client secret' > click outside of the modal > modal disappears 
  - Open modal by pressing 'Generate new client secret' > click 'Cancel' > modal disappears
  - Open modal by pressing 'Generate new client secret' > enter valid name > click 'Add' > click outside of the modal > modal does not disappear > click 'Done' > modal disappears

### Rotate Client Secret Modal
  - Open modal by pressing 'Rotate' > click outside of the modal > modal disappears 
  - Open modal by pressing 'Rotate'> click 'Cancel' > modal disappears
  - Open modal by pressing 'Rotate' > click 'Yes, rotate' > click outside of the modal > modal does not disappear > click 'Done' > modal disappears

### Tests
  - Review unit tests
  - Run `npm run test:unit:interactive -w api-applications` and confirm all unit tests pass

author: dionrhys
body:
There was a race condition here when accessing the `BaseTestExtensions.Options` property.

It would first store the new options into the static field, then update is converters, then return. If another test using the same method ran in parallel, it could grab the stored options before the converters were added, and use it for serialization/deserialization, at which point the options converters become read-only.

This causes further usages of `ReadFromJsonAsync` to not have the `JsonStringEnumConverter` present, which breaks a whole lot of API v3 integration tests.

This issue was found here:

- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/runs/43181366144
- https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/actions/runs/15345437471/job/43180837368?pr=22763

# Testing

Run the API v3 integration tests many times!
title: SCALE-461 Fix StackOverflow.Tests.Integration.Api.V3 BaseTest.ReadFromJsonAsync flakiness
