author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR includes two small bug fixes:
[YETI2-757](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-757) - Remove `min` and `max` query parameters from the comments endpoint
[YETI2-804](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-804) - Return DTOs for Comment endpoints

### Note
I used some IDs (listed below) to test YETI2-804 and noticed that sometimes the same comment will sometime not include the display name or it may differ depending on the comment endpoint. This is because the methods use different SQL queries. For example, getting a single comment pulls the data only from the PostComment table (it has a `UserDisplayName` column). While getting several comments, attempts to load the Owner object if there is an ID which should always pull the latest display name. This also can result in one response containing a display name but a `null` ID and in another having the display name be `null` (since the user was deleted).

## How to Test
Use Postman requests for faster testing.

### On `main`
YETI2-757
- Use `Content Feeds/Get Comments` and make a request with the `minScore` and `maxScore` query parameters, it should return items that fall within the range
- Go to `api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs` and `minScore` and `maxScore` will be listed as parameters

YETI2-804
- Use all of the requests in the `Comments` folder (there is a total of 4) and notice that the `ownerUserId` property is returned 
   - Some helpful IDs are
      - Question: 20464
      - Question Comment: 104616
      - Answer: 20467 (Parent Question ID: 20464)
      - Answer Comment: 41519

### This branch
YETI2-757
- Use `Content Feeds/Get Comments` and make a request with the `minScore` and `maxScore` query parameters, it will now return items that fall outside that range
- Go to `api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs` and `minScore` and `maxScore` will no longer be listed as parameters

YETI2-804
- Use all of the requests in the `Comments` folder (there is a total of 4) and notice that the `ownerUserId` property should no longer be visible in the response


[YETI2-757]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-757?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
IIS and KestrelProxy set the `HttpContext.Request.PathBase` property differently. This led to the application generating different links on Windows and Mac machines. The outcome of this change is to have IIS and KestrelProxy set the same `HttpContext.Request.PathBase` value. 

If you have a Mac machine, then this PR should be tested using the changes in [this branch of DevLocalSetup](https://github.com/StackEng/DevLocalSetup/pull/409). You’ll need to pull the branch and run `Setup Websites` to use the upcoming changes which will stop the subpath prefix from being stripped by the reverse proxy and therefore received by the backend application.

On Windows, we use IIS and it should just work.

### Changes in PR
#### Data Licensing/Public Platform
- Sets appsettings.json “BasePath” value for the Data Licensing API for all environments and locally for API v3.  
- Data Licensing API: Changes the integration test suite to run with a subpath so that we can assert things that need it (like auth cookie path)  
- Data Licensing API: Use the configuration to also set the auth cookie path and OpenAPI server URL

#### Teams/SO Internal
- I have not yet updated the local appsettings.json files as I’m not sure what the values should be. I would appreciate some help figuring this out. 

### Out of scope
This PR sets the "BasePath" values for local `appsettings.json` only. API v3 contains a handful of redirects that work because “/v3” or “/api/v3”  is hardcoded and matches our deployment configurations. This works if the base path is always “/v3” or "/api/v3” but should be made configurable if there’s a possibility it won't be (like the FBB/Enterprise difference). That type of change should be tested carefully in a test environment so as to not break deployments.

## How to test
Please let me know if you are using a Mac or Windows machine in your review. If you are using a Mac machine, please pull [this version of DevLocalSetup](https://github.com/StackEng/DevLocalSetup/pull/409) and run the corresponding `Setup Websites` step before testing.

### Public Platform
#### Data Licensing API 
Clear the `dldocs` cookie to simulate a log out. 

1. Visit [https://api.stackexchange.local/dl](https://api.stackexchange.local/dl) and it should redirect to the login page  
2. Enter the password and it should redirect to [https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs/](https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs/)   
3. Make a request using Scalar UI and it should succeed  
4. Verify that the auth cookie has a path of `/dl/docs`

#### API v3
1. Enable time based pagination for API v3 to test redirect [https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3\_TimeBasedPagination\_Enabled](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled)   
2. Visit [https://api.stackexchange.local/v3](https://api.stackexchange.local/v3) and it should redirect to the Swagger page  
3. Open the developer console and make a request to /questions with the\`to\` and `from` query parameters, the request should redirect to a similar request but with a default date range appended. The final response in the Swagger page should be a 200\.  
4. Repeat the step above but for the `/content-feeds/comments` endpoint.  
5. Make a call to `/content-feeds/changes/questions` endpoint, the `ApiUrl` property should contain `/v3`. This endpoint does not result in a redirect.

### Teams/SO Internal

#### API v3 FBB
1. Visit [https://api.stackoverflowteams.local/v3](https://api.stackoverflowteams.local/v3) and it should redirect to the Swagger page  
2. Visit [https://api.stackoverflowteams.local/v3/](https://api.stackoverflowteams.local/v3/) (has a trailing slash) and it should redirect  to the Swagger page  
3. Make a request using the Swagger page and it should return a 200.

#### API v3 Enterprise
TODO: Does Enterprise run on a subpath? If yes, where? [From this article](https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/articles/28238) it seems like it is hosted on `/api/v3`.
1. Visit [https://\[your\_site\].stackenterprise.co/api/v3](https://[your_site].stackenterprise.co/api/v3) and it should redirect to the Swagger page

author: kylejrp
body:
KRAKEN-2567

## Summary

This pull request updates the `sitemap.xml` generation logic in `FeedsController` to better align with the site's redirect logic for closed questions, improves filtering for valid posts, and consolidates access checks for sitemap endpoints. The changes ensure that only active, non-deleted, and relevant posts are included in the sitemaps, and that only search engines or developers can access these endpoints unless a manual cache bypass is used.

**Access control improvements:**
- Introduced a new helper method `EnsureSearchEngineOrDeveloperAsync()` to centralize the logic for allowing only search engine bots or developers to access sitemap endpoints, replacing repeated code in multiple actions. Now, all sitemap endpoints use this method for consistent access checks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dR542-R551) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL553-R566) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL715-R747) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL795-R829) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL869-R905) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL943-R981) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL997-R1036) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL1066-R1118) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL1123-R1176)

**Sitemap filtering and consistency:**
- Updated SQL queries for sitemaps to match the redirect logic for closed questions: only include questions that are open, or closed with answers, or closed but not as duplicates, closely matching the logic in `QuestionsController.TryGetRedirectUrl`. This avoids listing questions that would immediately redirect. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL568-R594) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL1018-R1069) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8cf1af0e8f59417075c9e455fb7a4ab893656581b8a797057f862a8e8785af7cR1393)
- Added filtering for `PostState = 1` (active posts) to all relevant sitemap queries, ensuring that only active posts (not deleted, migrated, or otherwise inactive) are included in sitemaps for questions, articles, and discussions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dR646) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL658-R686) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL679-R708) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dR772-R775) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL824-R857) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL894-R929)

**Query and ordering improvements:**
- Changed ordering in sitemap queries from `LastActivityDate DESC` to `Id` ordering for consistency and potentially improved performance in pagination. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dR772-R775) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL824-R857) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL894-R929)

**Documentation and maintainability:**
- Added a comment in `QuestionsController.TryGetRedirectUrl` to note that its logic is now partially duplicated in sitemap generation, to help future maintainers keep both in sync.

### Future work

Part of this PR's intention was to reduce the paging instability. Before, we sorted by LastActivityDate desc. This meant that, while a crawler was going between individual `sitemap-questions-{index}.xml` sitemaps, the order of posts found inside could change. For example:
- The crawler fetches `sitemap-questions-0.xml` and sees posts 1 - 5000
- The crawler fetches `sitemap-questions-1.xml` and sees posts 5001 - 10000
- A question that *would* have been on `sitemap-questions-1.xml` is edited, so it now has a recent LastActivityDate and appears at the beginning of `sitemap-questions-0.xml`, bumping all questions down in the index by one position
- The crawler fetches `sitemap-questions-2.xml` and sees posts 10002 - 15001 (instead of 10001 - 15000). It misses the post that was edited and it won't appear in the sitemap.

I'll open up a separate pull request to fix this paging instability - perhaps generating the sitemaps only from a scheduled route, and then the queries just pull from the cache (but don't regenerate them).


### Testing

Testing is hard - we're not going to inspect all sitemap files. I would recommend:
- Opening one of each sub-sitemap linked from https://meta.stackexchange.local/sitemap.xml to make sure it doesn't blow up
- Comparing the counts in the `sitemap.xml` route with the count found in the inner query of each `sitemap-{postType}-{index}.xml`. For example, comparing the `sitemap.xml` count query:

```
select count(*) from Posts
    where DeletionDate is null
        and MigrationDate is null
        and (
            -- This matches the redirection logic in QuestionController.TryGetRedirectUrl
            ClosedDate is null -- post is not closed
            or AnswerCount > 0 -- post is closed, but has answers
            or IsClosedAsDuplicate = 0 -- post is closed, has no answers, but is not marked as a duplicate
            -- Here, we have a closed post without answers that is marked as a duplicate
            -- To be completely accurate with redirect code, we would also check if the original post that
            -- this is a duplicate exists and is not deleted, but that requires querying PostHistory,
            -- so we'll call this good enough for now.
        )
        and PostTypeId = 1
        and PostState = 1
```

with the count of the inner part of the `sitemap-questions-{index}.xml` query

```
Select p.Id
          From Posts p
          Where DeletionDate is null
             and MigrationDate is null
             and (
                 -- This matches the redirection logic in QuestionController.TryGetRedirectUrl
                 ClosedDate is null -- post is not closed
                 or AnswerCount > 0 -- post is closed, but has answers
                 or IsClosedAsDuplicate = 0 -- post is closed, has no answers, but is not marked as a duplicate
                 -- Here, we have a closed post without answers that is marked as a duplicate
                 -- To be completely accurate with redirect code, we would also check if the original post that
                 -- this is a duplicate exists and is not deleted, but that requires querying PostHistory,
                 -- so we'll call this good enough for now.
             )
             and PostTypeId = 1
             and PostState = 1
      Order By p.Id

KRAKEN-2273 ## Summary This pull request introduces improvements to canonical URL handling and tag encoding for the routes `/`, `/questions`, and `/questions/tagged`; with a focus on preventing double encoding of tags (especially those with special characters like `+`), generating consistent canonical URLs, and ensuring correct rendering of canonical and meta tags in HTML. New tag helpers are added to handle encoding safely, and canonical URL logic is improved in controllers and views. This also adds schema markup to `/questions/tagged/{tags}`, which was missed in #24152. The most important changes are: **Canonical URL Handling and Tag Encoding:** * Added `SafeCanonicalTagHelper` and `SafeMetaTagHelper` to ensure that canonical and meta tags are rendered with correct, single-encoded URLs, preventing issues with special characters like `+` in tags or double encoding (eg. `/questions/tagged/c++` becoming `/questions/tagged/c++` (`StackOverflow.Common/Helpers/SafeCanonicalTagHelper.cs`, `StackOverflow.Common/Helpers/SafeMetaTagHelper.cs`, `StackOverflow/Views/Master.cshtml`, `StackOverflow/Views/_ViewImports.cshtml`). * Refactored tag URL encoding logic in `Tag.cs` to provide consistent, correctly encoded, and optionally sorted tag URLs for canonical links and sharing. This includes new overloads for `TagUrlEncode`, improved handling of sorting, and correct encoding of spaces and `+` characters (`StackOverflow.Common/Models/Tag.cs`). **Controller and View Integration:** * Updated controllers (`HomeController`, `QuestionsController.List`) to generate and set canonical URLs using the improved tag encoding and new helpers, ensuring canonical URLs are consistent and exclude unnecessary query parameters (e.g., `edited`). This includes factoring out canonical URL logic and using it in relevant endpoints (`StackOverflow/Controllers/HomeController.cs`, `StackOverflow/Controllers/QuestionsController.List.cs`). * Updated `StackOverflow/Views/Questions/ListByTag.cshtml` to have CollectionPage markup, like we did for similar pages in #24152 * Updated question list and tag views to use the new encoding logic for canonical URLs, ensuring that tag order and encoding are consistent and correct (`StackOverflow/Views/Questions/ListByTag.cshtml`). **Other Improvements:** * Minor code cleanups and dependency updates to support the above changes (e.g., updated usings, null handling, and method signatures) (`StackOverflow.Common/Models/UserQuestionList.cs`). These changes collectively ensure that canonical URLs and meta tags are generated and rendered in a way that avoids double encoding, supports special characters in tags, and improves SEO consistency across the site. ### How to test 1. For each of these URLs, view the source HTML of the page to ensure that both the `` and `` are working as expected. The `&` character in the URL should get encoded as `&` - this is intended behavior and proper encoding. 1. https://meta.stackexchange.local/ 2. https://meta.stackexchange.local/home (does not redirect, but does reflect the proper canonical url of `/`) 3. https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions 4. https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/list (does not redirect, but does reflect the proper canonical url of `/questions`) 5. https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/{tagNames} - Note: this should properly encode a tag like `c++` as `c%2b%2b` - Testing with multiple tags (eg. https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/discussion%20bug or https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/bug%20discussion should return a canonical order, no matter what order you put the tags in 7. https://meta.stackexchange.local/tags/{tagNames} (does not redirect, but does reflect the proper canonical url of `/questions/tagged/{tagNames}`) 2. For https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions, it should properly render a URL for the `CollectionPage`, eg: ```
...
``` 3. For https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/tagged/discussion, pasting the source of the page into https://validator.schema.org/ should successfully parse the page as a CollectionPage with eventual Question elements inside the schema

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR adds the log enrichment headers to API v2 regardless of the auth method used. Right now, the `Authorization` header auth does not write the log enrichment headers. 

### Notes
There are 3 ways to authenticate to API v2:
1. `key` and `access_token` query parameters - Valid only in PubPlat
2. `X-API-Key` ans `X-API-Access-Token` request headers
3. `Authorization: Bearer {KEY OR ACCESS TOKEN}` header - These values can be stored in either the ApiApplicationKeys table or the ApiApplicationAccessTokens. Both kinds of entries can have a combination of ApplicationId and AccountId.

I have refactored the code and moved the writing of these headers right after we identify the request rather than duplicating part of the auth logic into the `ProfiledController.cs`. This leads to a slighty functional difference since the `HomeController.cs` and `ScheduledController.cs` inherit from `ProfiledController.cs`. 

I think the tradeoff is worthwhile because `ScheduledController.cs` only contains a route that can be called locally and `HomeController.cs` primarily hosts routes that don't require authentication. Auth happens in `ThrottledController.cs`.

We only write these headers for PubPlat!

## How to Test
1. Go to https://api.stackexchange.local/docs/user-inbox#id=1&filter=default&site=meta.stackexchange.local&run=true to generate an access token, copy both the key and access token from the request
2. Go to Postman PubPlat API v2.* collection and use the questions request
3. Modify the auth in the following configurations and verify that the appropriate `X-Account-Id` and `X-Application-Id` headers are written

Query Parameters
`key` only --> `X-Application-Id`
`key` & `access_token` --> `X-Application-Id` and `X-Account-Id`
`access_token` only --> Bad request, requires key

Request Headers
`X-API-Key` only --> `X-Application-Id`
`X-API-Key` & `X-API-Access-Token` --> `X-Application-Id` and `X-Account-Id`
`X-API-Access-Token` only --> Bad request, requires key

Authorization with Bearer scheme Header
`Authorization: Bearer {KEY}` --> `X-Application-Id`
`Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN} --> `X-Account-Id` and `X-Application-Id`
Note: There are other combinations here that are valid but we have not publicized the concept of User type API Application keys. These keys only have an AccountId...they are kind of like PATs.
title: YETI2-560 - Write `X-Account-Id` and `X-Application-Id` log enrichment headers regardless of auth method (API v2/PubPlat only)

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR adds OpenAPI document generation and visualization. In addition, it locks the documents behind cookie authentication. The authentication cookie is generated by a login route that uses a shared password. The endpoints are always accessible but being able to view them is dependent on a new site setting.

### From Magic Query Parameter to Shared Password
The shared password approach is an improvement over the existing magic query parameter used in SE API v3 since the value is not saved in a user’s browser or any server logs. Since it is referred to as a password and not passed around in URLs, it is implied that the value should be kept secret.

The team is aware of the flaws of using a shared password but given the contents (documentation that is the same for all customers) and competing priorities, it is good enough for our current needs. The major flaw is that the password can be “leaked” to others. This flaw is also present in the current magic query parameter.

### Swagger UI to Scalar
We are changing visualization libraries from SE API V3 to provide customers a nicer experience. This includes a more modern UI and increased code generation capabilities.

### Libraries Used
Swashbuckle for OpenAPI document generation. While Microsoft now has a first-party OpenAPI library, the .NET 8 version of it only has methods for Minimal API syntax which we hardly use. It is possible that after an upgrade to .NET 9 and assuming the libraries features are the same as Swashbuckle’s (Swashbuckle has been around for a long time), a migration away from Swashbuckle to Microsoft’s library may be possible.

Scalar.AspNetCore and Scalar.AspNetCore.Swashbuckle for generating the Scalar/OpenAPI visualizations.

#### Licensing
We are clear to use MIT licensing. The Scalar project and the .NET libraries used here are all under MIT licenses.
https://www.nuget.org/packages/Scalar.AspNetCore
https://www.nuget.org/packages/Scalar.AspNetCore.Swashbuckle
https://github.com/scalar/scalar?tab=MIT-1-ov-file

### Security
Writing auth code is scary. Here we introduce cookie authentication to view items under `/dl/docs`. The cookie name is `dldocs`.

- I’ve specified several attributes on the `dldocs` cookie that limits how it can be used. 
- This authentication scheme IS NOT PART of the default policy (and it should NEVER be) which is used when you simply use the `[Authorize]` attribute without defining a policy.
- I don’t think it was needed but I have also added the anti forgery mechanism. 
- I will be creating a follow-up ticket to add rate limiting to this endpoint which will disincentivize brute force attacks.

### Paths
To keep things easy and more “secure”, I have specified `/docs` and `/docs/openapi/{docName}.json` as the paths for the UI and OpenAPI docs. This allows us to issue out as single cookie with the Path attribute set to `/dl/docs` which then results in web browser only sending out that cookie when the path matches.

### Follow Up
There are a few of follow-up Jira cards I will be creating. 
1. Don’t use Stacks CDN and lock in a version
2. Add rate limiting to the login endpoint. Either both application level and/or in Cloudflare.
3. Ask Jeff, if we have to include a link to our Cookie policy in the login screen since we are using cookies (and Scalar also issues out some cookies)
4. Add a new site setting to change the currently used password

### General Flow
1. Visit home `/dl` - Redirects to `/dl/docs`
2. If cookie exists, go to `/dl/docs`. Otherwise, go to `/dl/login`
3. In `/dl/login` enter password, if correct redirect to `/dl/docs`. Otherwise, return to `/dl/login` with error message

## How to Test
### No authentication
Clear the `dldocs` cookie to “logout”.
1. `https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs/` should redirect to the login page
2. `https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs/openapi/v1.json` should redirect to the login page

### General Flow - Visualization Site Setting Enabled
Clear the `dldocs` cookie to “logout”. Open the network inspector tab to see all redirects.
1. Visit the home page `https://api.stackexchange.local/dl` and you should be redirected to the `/docs` page. You shouldn’t be authenticated at this time so you should then be redirected to the `/login` page
3. Enter an incorrect password, it should not create the auth cookie `dldocs` and you should be redirected back to the `/login` page with an error
4. Enter the correct password, it should redirect you to `dldocs` and you should be redirected to the `/docs` page. The auth cookie `dldocs` should be created. It should have multiple attributes that restrict how the cookie can be used.

### Antiforgery
Clear the `dldocs` cookie to “logout”. Also delete the `__dldocs-antiforgery` cookie.
1. Visit the login page https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/login. This will create the anti forgery cookie.
2. Enter the correct password but scramble the value of the `__dldocs-antiforgery` cookie under Application -> Storage -> Cookies in Developer Tools.
3. Submit the form. It should return a 500 error. Note that this is the default .NET behavior…I think it would be nice to handle explicitly but didn’t pursue that work here.

### Visualization Site Setting Disabled
Make sure you already have a cookie.
1. Disable the OpenAPI visualization https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.DataLicensing.EnableOpenApiVisualization
2. `/dl/` should 404
3. `/dl/login` should 404
4. `/dl/docs` should 404
5. `/dl/docs/openapi/v1.json` should 404

### Scalar Docs
Perhaps being a bit paranoid and it is no longer needed but I migrated the code that attaches signals so that crawlers do no index this site. 
1. After authenticating, scan through the docs, make a request and make sure it returns a 200 response
2. Inspect the code and verify that the head element has a meta tag for robots set to none
3. Refresh the request and verify that there is a response header `X-Robots-Tag` set to none
4. https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs/openapi/v1.json and very there is a response header `X-Robots-Tag` set to none
title: YETI2-765 - Add OpenAPI document generation and visualization behind auth cookie to Data Licensing API

author: balpha
body:
We're setting `REGEX_DEFAULT_MATCH_TIMEOUT` on the app domain to set the default timeout for any regular expression that doesn't define their own timeouts.

This value is then read here by the framework:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e0837be345978738d0387055e0eb1e2b989dd787/src/libraries/System.Text.RegularExpressions/src/System/Text/RegularExpressions/Regex.Timeout.cs#L70

-- and it's only read once, during the static initialization of the `Regex` class. In other words, if we set the app domain data *after* the `Regex` class has ever been referenced, it's already too late.

And at lest in `StackOverflow`, that is unfortunately the case:

https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/51139ef7dafdfd0adefb92afbf86830fd2ce4184/StackOverflow/Startup.cs#L721

That ⬆️ happens way before the [call](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/51139ef7dafdfd0adefb92afbf86830fd2ce4184/StackOverflow/Startup.cs#L911) to `UseStackOverflowCommonAspNet`, where we were setting the app domain data. And thus, Stack Overflow never got the default timeout overridden (which therefore remains infinite, which is the "default default").

It's possible that this still worked in the other projects which use `UseStackOverflowCommonAspNet`, but that feels pretty brittle, so I decided to simply remove the `SetData` call from `UseStackOverflowCommonAspNet` and call it in each individual project's `Program.cs`, as the very first thing.
title: set default regex timeout earlier

## Summary

This pull request updates how coding challenge discussions are identified as "complete". The main change is to generalize the logic so that both prefixes and suffixes in discussion titles can be used to mark a challenge as complete, and to centralize this logic in a single helper method. The settings are also updated to support multiple markers for completed challenges.

**Centralization and generalization of coding challenge completion logic:**

* Introduced a new static method `CodingChallengeIsComplete` in `CollectiveDiscussionsService` to determine if a discussion is a completed coding challenge, now checking for both prefixes and suffixes in the post title.
* Updated all usages across the codebase to use the new `CodingChallengeIsComplete` method instead of duplicating the logic or using hardcoded string checks. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50824e5e2439375906bdd529b28d0177a5a9fdda96c3e3b5c23b2503339a474fL175-R175) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50824e5e2439375906bdd529b28d0177a5a9fdda96c3e3b5c23b2503339a474fL250-R250)

**Settings improvements:**

* Expanded the `CodingChallengeEntryDisplayOverrides` setting in `DiscussionsSettings` to support multiple prefixes and suffixes and updated its description to clarify this broader matching logic.

### How to test

See #23033 and #23815 for previous testing instructions for this regression.

author: kylejrp
body:
KRAKEN-2536

## Summary

This pull request updates the schema.org microdata markup for discussions, replies, and user cards to improve semantic structure and accessibility. Major changes include switching reply parent references to use anchor links, refining itemprop usage, and enhancing user card markup for better structured data support. This should resolve the issues in https://search.google.com/search-console/r/discussion-forum?resource_id=sc-domain%3Astackoverflow.com.

**Schema.org microdata improvements:**

* Replaced parent item references in replies from detailed `<div>` blocks with a `<link itemprop="parentItem" href="..."/>`, using anchor links to discussion or reply elements for better semantic linking. (`_Replies.cshtml`, `_CodingChallengeReplies.cshtml`, `PublicDiscussions/_Replies.cshtml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5fb00156879541ff27dd6dbecfa64f76ca39abbf2004adb764a202336ed70932L226-R227) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0e32dece83f89546326fbd0d3917c2e7e75dd3a84c6f614223784aa715f504cfL226-R227) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a7db94a78fadfd808d8037e1846bde6e837dfab08ba22586a078f7cb9fb74759L236-R237)
* Added `id="js-discussion-@discussion.Post.Id"` to main discussion containers to support anchor-based linking. (`Show.cshtml`, `ShowCodingChallenge.cshtml`, `PublicDiscussions/Show.cshtml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-65200c2c4d707147e0f8fbf3a73c65ac81f07b00def8258cf3d7c76a7fc803c3L181-R188) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2532d496f874db52288c707a5053ae64755069c284775ba8fb22e3d30c8df950L179-R186) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e2da3631b9b47bf6838c87fa71fe52a40c7ead6730b9245b4139f93ef5b0740aL181-R188)
* Improved reply markup by adding `itemprop="comment"` to comment containers and removing redundant wrapper `id` attributes for cleaner structure. (`_Replies.cshtml`, `_CodingChallengeReplies.cshtml`, `PublicDiscussions/_Replies.cshtml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5fb00156879541ff27dd6dbecfa64f76ca39abbf2004adb764a202336ed70932L291-R279) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0e32dece83f89546326fbd0d3917c2e7e75dd3a84c6f614223784aa715f504cfL292-R280) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a7db94a78fadfd808d8037e1846bde6e837dfab08ba22586a078f7cb9fb74759L301-R289)
* Removed unnecessary `itemprop="url"` from share links in discussion lists for more accurate microdata. (`Show.cshtml`, `ShowCodingChallenge.cshtml`, `PublicDiscussions/Show.cshtml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-65200c2c4d707147e0f8fbf3a73c65ac81f07b00def8258cf3d7c76a7fc803c3L350) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2532d496f874db52288c707a5053ae64755069c284775ba8fb22e3d30c8df950L348) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e2da3631b9b47bf6838c87fa71fe52a40c7ead6730b9245b4139f93ef5b0740aL368)

**User card structured data enhancements:**

* Refactored `UserCard.v2.cshtml` to conditionally render schema.org properties (`itemprop="author"`, `itemprop="name"`, `itemprop="url"`) for improved semantic markup and accessibility. (`UserCard.v2.cshtml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7351d75385f89bb6a2c23b92d1edf990b7a59ecd8bc68146c80bbd00d67fccc2R18-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7351d75385f89bb6a2c23b92d1edf990b7a59ecd8bc68146c80bbd00d67fccc2L75-R99)

body:
## Summary

This pull request introduces improvements to how schema.org metadata is rendered for post summaries and related components. The main changes ensure that metadata properties like `upvoteCount` and `answerCount` are only included when the `ShowSchemaMetadata` flag is enabled, and that invisible meta properties are conditionally rendered in the UI. Additionally, minor fixes were made to ensure proper Razor syntax for data binding.

**Conditional schema.org metadata rendering:**

* Updated `RenderMiniCountItem` calls in `PostSummary.cshtml` and `OpinionBasedContentInfo.cshtml` to only set `schemaItemProp` to `"upvoteCount"` or `"answerCount"` if `ShowSchemaMetadata` is true, otherwise it is set to `null`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-015fa539495ca2391aa14228dd3efb780b9cc90e1de50cdfa12a8bbda9f689b0L137-R137) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-015fa539495ca2391aa14228dd3efb780b9cc90e1de50cdfa12a8bbda9f689b0L153-R153) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ff2ae4e1e85a7c7f289c2362617c475f82110d9e2f7b80817dc4f35952796e56L34-R34) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ff2ae4e1e85a7c7f289c2362617c475f82110d9e2f7b80817dc4f35952796e56L46-R46)
* Added conditional rendering of `RenderInvisibleMetaProperties` in `PostSummary.cshtml` and within Staging Ground and Opinion-Based Content partials, so invisible meta properties are only rendered if `ShowSchemaMetadata` is true. **Minor Razor syntax corrections:**

* Fixed Razor syntax for the `data-score` attribute in discussion containers to use `@Model.Discussion.Post.Score` for proper data binding in multiple views (`Show.cshtml`, `ShowCodingChallenge.cshtml`, `PublicDiscussions/Show.cshtml`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-65200c2c4d707147e0f8fbf3a73c65ac81f07b00def8258cf3d7c76a7fc803c3L288-R288) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2532d496f874db52288c707a5053ae64755069c284775ba8fb22e3d30c8df950L286-R286) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-e2da3631b9b47bf6838c87fa71fe52a40c7ead6730b9245b4139f93ef5b0740aL294-R294)

## Out of scope

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
Context in [this Slack thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C0966JZRXK6/p1762004072724449)

## TL;DR

Because we're conditionally adding GCP and Azure workload identity but the schemes were hard coded to include those the API would reject all authenticated requests.

## Longer explanation

We're checking for specific configuration to exist before adding GCP and/or Azure workload identity authentication handlers to APIv3. This is to prevent accidentally opening us up to callers that we might not want to enable this for.

Unfortunately, the _authorization policies_ had the list of allowable schemes hard-coded and when no associated _authentication handler_ for a scheme is present this fails at _request time_.

What made this problem worse is that for local deployments, configuration was already added to `environmentsettings.Local.json`. Turns out that integration tests for APIv3 are considered a _local_ deployment and therefore picked up this configuration, registered the authentication handlers and made all the tests pass.

Therefore, this problem wasn't caught in PR / CI and it blew up only when deployed and called.

## Resolution

The configuration from `environmentsettings.Local.json` was removed and the schemes are now conditionally added to the authorization policies.

That ensures that at runtime we're no longer attempting to authorize against a scheme that hasn't been registered in the authentication pipeline

## Future changes

Out of this, _gestures broadly_, situation there are a few things we can learn:

- A synthetic test on APIv3 would have alerted us quickly to a runtime problem with the API. We have an `/auth/test` endpoint we should be able to leverage for that.
- Integration tests should not use a local deployment tier. (Incidentally that would also make [this wart](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/42fa624eb95a9acc8a85e9375a565473743c2b7d/StackOverflow.Common/Models/Authentication/ApiApplication.cs#L94) go away)

body:
KRAKEN-2273

- Fixes https://meta.stackoverflow.com/questions/436375/deleted-usernames-are-rendering-improperly-for-moderators
- Fixes https://opserver.main-prod.int.gcp.stackoverflow.net/login?ReturnUrl=%2Fexceptions%3Fsimilar%3De7d95d6f-f5f3-4285-a427-c06ca9cfb597%26log%3DQ%2526A

This pull request refactors the handling of user display names and URLs in the `UserInfo` model and related views, improving semantic markup and schema.org metadata handling. The changes ensure that user names are returned as a tuple containing the anchor link, display name, and URL, which allows for more precise rendering and metadata output in views. Additionally, comprehensive integration tests have been added to verify the correct rendering of user info under various conditions.

#### Refactoring and Semantic Markup Improvements

* Changed the return type of `UserInfo.Name()` from `StackHtmlString` to a tuple containing the anchor link, display name, and URL, allowing for more accurate rendering and schema metadata. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b535dff3b2d57688a269dc832295d991bfe1b65e87b5ed4706b4c7685915baaeL401-R402) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b535dff3b2d57688a269dc832295d991bfe1b65e87b5ed4706b4c7685915baaeL427-R440)
* Updated `UserInfoDiv` to use the new tuple structure, improving how hidden username and URL metadata are rendered for schema.org compliance. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b535dff3b2d57688a269dc832295d991bfe1b65e87b5ed4706b4c7685915baaeL116-R126) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b535dff3b2d57688a269dc832295d991bfe1b65e87b5ed4706b4c7685915baaeL152-R149)

#### View Updates

* Modified all usages of `UserInfo.Name()` in views to reference the `.AnchorLink` property, ensuring consistent display and markup. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-353f740bacccefe7eed607f4b155a8cd39e0dabe69ebe6908a8d6d0b0bf7f60eL63-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f427c2d09cf9ddbc3c95b2273a25fee5e559dc17c7c6782967147d7b7917339dL10-R10) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-296f1548828afc64e8ec0f8abc9e2d8710f07c537e54a38f67231dc4acd4deffL60-R60)

#### Testing Improvements

* Added a new integration test suite `UserInfoTest` to thoroughly verify the rendering of user info, including schema.org metadata and fallback logic for display names and URLs.

#### Minor Logic Change

* Updated the sort name logic in `GetSortsName` to group `Hot` and `HotNoTime` sorts under the same display name "Hot".

### How to test

1. Go to https://meta.stackexchange.local/ and make sure it renders the same. Paste the entire source of the page into https://validator.schema.org/ and make sure that the CollectionPage validates correctly.
2. Go to https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions and make sure it renders the same. Paste the entire source of the page into https://validator.schema.org/ and make sure that the CollectionPage validates correctly.
3. Go to a deleted question locally to try and reproduce the case described in this meta post https://meta.stackoverflow.com/questions/436375/deleted-usernames-are-rendering-improperly-for-moderators

body: TEAMS-14958 ## Summary This PR adds the ability to put a "Source Name" review queue filter on the URL bar so that when the tasks are loaded the filter will be pre-set. This is the first of three filters we will be adding. When they are all complete, we can link to specific ingestion jobs from the ingestion dashboard. ## How to Test - Follow the instructions from this https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23440 to set up Swagger UI and access Swagger endpoints on SOE. - Access [Swagger UI](https://stackenterprise.local/api/v3/swagger/index.html) - Send valid requests to the `/ingest/questionandanswer` and `/ingest/question endpoints` with `tags` and `externalName` in the `sourceMetadata` - Run this [scheduled route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/sync-ingestion-review-tasks) - Go to the [Ingestion queue](https://stackenterprise.local/review/ingestion) - Test the filters below with the `tags` and `externalName` you sent to the ingestion endpoints in the above step. - Make sure that as you work through the tasks that the filter stays set. The filter should stay set after performing actions like Delete or Verify and Publish. - You should be able to clear the filters - The filter will work alongside the tag filter. Try various combinations - Try this filter URL https://stackenterprise.local/ingestion/review/filters?tags=general&sourceName=Topic (you can change the `tags` and `sourceName` parameters with the ones you sent to the ingestion endpoints in the above step) - Check that it redirects you to the review queue with the pre-filled filters, and the results should match the filters. - You can double-check that the current task in the review queue matches your source name with this query: ```sql select p.Id as PostId, Title as PostTitle, ispm.ExternalName from [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].[dbo].[Posts] p inner join [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].[dbo].[ReviewTasks] rt on rt.PostId = p.Id inner join [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].[dbo].[IngestionSourcePostMetadata] ispm on ispm.PostId = p.Id where rt.Id = ```

author: kirtithorat
body:
## Summary

This is the final follow-up PR for the API v3 setup of the Ingestion app.

When ingestion settings are toggled, this PR updates the logic to add or reset a key in Azure Key Vault with the write access token. This token is used by the Free Refills service of Knowledge Ingestion to ingest content into an SOE instance.

Additionally, this PR removes rate limiting from ingestion routes to ensure smooth ingestion operations.

## How to Test

1. Toggling the [ingestion setting on](https://stackenterprise.local/enterprise/ingestion/settings)
    - adds `ki-enabled:True`  to the key vault
    - automatically creates an API service application called "Ingestion"
    - adds a write access token for the generated app to the key vault: `knowledge-ingestion-api-v3-key:API_V3_KEY=<write_access_token>`
    - validate the `write_access_token` to make a write call using Bruno/Postman, the write should be successful
2. Toggling the [ingestion setting off](https://stackenterprise.local/enterprise/ingestion/settings)
    - updates `ki-enabled:False`  into the key vault
    - automatically removes the API service application called "Ingestion"
    - updates the write access token for the generated app to the key vault: `knowledge-ingestion-api-v3-key:API_V3_KEY=__EMPTY__`
    -  validate the `write_access_token` to make a write call using Bruno/Postman, the write should be fail
3. No direct way to test rate limits, I added tests for it
title: TEAMS-14913: Automatically generate write access token for Ingestion app

author: kylejrp
body:
KRAKEN-2262

## Summary

_This PR summary was mostly generated from Copilot_

This PR introduces a new feature to redirect URLs with trailing slashes to their canonical form, improving consistency and potentially SEO. This pull request also standardizes URL formatting across the codebase by removing unnecessary trailing slashes in places I could find them. The changes also add settings to control this redirect behavior and its logging, and refactor several controller actions and view links for cleaner routing.

Note that a 307 redirect will preserve the HTTP method used when redirecting. That is to say, if you were to request some route "/foo/submit/" with a POST method, it will then perform that same POST request to "/foo/submit". If we used a 302 redirect, it would instead perform a GET request to "/foo/submit", which would be undesired behavior.

**URL Formatting and Routing Improvements:**

* Standardized URLs by removing unnecessary trailing slashes and correcting query string delimiters in route and link generation throughout controllers and views [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2368dc82668f34a51b165172a4a8c09b94eec72e7e07e7b4816480e37dd281c0L106-R106) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-67a15eca01820434f966455c20328eec9d9abaf81efa934cb7ae3edef5ba6aedL18-R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0ff18443d1f116b373d680761949596694607aa3922233737ae6d21a9e0a2f0dL219-R219) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-47988bac40eebe2a7cb9a433eb491569eb26cb6ce97d278fc4da5ab91b67de04L44-R44) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7925a8f738d476b8260d7279c9c2510f279495c6dc0e61ef1f35da787e7a9a38L83-R83) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-cb38338f6bb7ed216d47ecd55f1dadebbfe4d7c6b1e6fcfa9c0d1e7d084a7fd9L275-R275) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-7449d5ac35d0f74f471240fcb12d38a2f61e4ac7b6ab473149c6f95f24cc64bdL183-R183) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-7b031ba13498fd56080abf5dba0cce553b0af2cb4109888bd4fa755327765de4L139-R139) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-0f4688cb8a928deec4967f6d5428a4a46a81cd377e01f87625e5835804435ed3L30-R30) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-1eaf8948978df809262ef09dd4466f44ef909e79f815cab60c3061563116eba7L74-R74) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-1731cd71ecf12a80309b3963d802a887d174a517535451e11adc74de2d7203cbL155-R155) [[12]](diffhunk://#diff-63b653cac8989cd3003b01dc697f08f771a3417ab4e161fa08f292cc56424c99L34-R34) [[13]](diffhunk://#diff-6da44801785ec4123a43595a92f02a4e53f0ce75fccff625a4644f7f89243e6bL43-R43) [[14]](diffhunk://#diff-6da44801785ec4123a43595a92f02a4e53f0ce75fccff625a4644f7f89243e6bL146-R146) [[15]](diffhunk://#diff-66f63844044fe2d47de1114dd2da86e7e9bc86bc8660f2244d762fa0cb75b49eL3017-R3017) [[16]](diffhunk://#diff-ff05335d9c3c26a9afed452f53dcc6c78ae3536bef5b7e74b101ca8b9b958f08L131-R131) [[17]](diffhunk://#diff-55936309e0285e35b333fd3f5aae671cc2d9a2586ddbdc27516e0ab650a30236L28-R28).

**Trailing Slash Redirect Feature:**

* Added new settings `EnableTrailingSlashRedirect` and `LogExceptionForTrailingSlashRedirect` to control trailing slash redirect behavior and logging.
* Implemented the `RemoveTrailingSlash` middleware in `Startup.cs` to redirect URLs with trailing slashes to their canonical form using a 307 Temporary Redirect, with optional exception logging [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-73b4435f668249845d6540a6077914dd02eb2310e7ce5defeea2ff9ac8b5e4efR874) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-73b4435f668249845d6540a6077914dd02eb2310e7ce5defeea2ff9ac8b5e4efR1053-R1093).

**Refactoring and Dependency Updates:**

* Updated `Startup.cs` to include necessary dependencies for URL manipulation and request handling [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-73b4435f668249845d6540a6077914dd02eb2310e7ce5defeea2ff9ac8b5e4efR2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-73b4435f668249845d6540a6077914dd02eb2310e7ce5defeea2ff9ac8b5e4efR13-R18).

**Minor Logic Fixes:**

* Corrected logic for building URLs in helper methods to avoid double slashes or incorrect query string delimiters [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-468c26226d65f10fa30d2fcd757b60c00884ddb5d1a45c2eaa3bf33165f0dfa3L34-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-09f380bd69db2b11955da17889d84066968324d0439092c256f7816f15b86f57L682-R682).


### How to test

1. Visit https://meta.stackexchange.local/. There should be no redirect.
2. Visit https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions. There should be no redirect.
2. Visit https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions/. There should be a redirect. An exception will be logged locally on https://meta.stackexchange.local/admin/errors.
title: KRAKEN-2262 Add a trailing slash redirect for SEO (eg. "/questions/" -> "/questions")

author: kristinalustig
body:
This PR addresses a couple of issues from the [CAS requests thread](https://meta.stackexchange.com/q/413210/344828).

It makes the spoiler blocks in posts tabbable, and allows you to either click or hit enter/space on them to reveal.

It also (in a separate commit so you can look at the two changes independently, please lmk if you'd prefer that I put these into separate PRs) creates a very basic framework for comment spoilers behind a site setting. When enabled (by default locally), users can use this format:

`[! Here is my huge spoiler !]`

And it will render a "reveal spoiler" link that reveals the spoiler once it's clicked (or you hit enter/space on it). It works as many times as you'd like in a comment, but no nested comments.

I felt that this was the simplest way to do it without faffing around with complex comment markdown code.


To test part 1:
- Create a spoiler in a post (the syntax is `>! Here's my spoiler`)
- Make sure you can tab to it (I suggest focusing somewhere in the voting buttons so you can get there quickly
- Make sure that pressing enter reveals the spoiler

To test part 2:
- Create a comment with multiple spoilers as outlined above
- View the comment and reveal the spoiler by clicking and by tabbing/entering

Please let me know if you have questions or ideas for how to improve these changes!
title: Fix spoiler accessibility and add comment spoilers

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
.NET 7 introduced a source generator (`RegexGenerator`) for regular expressions. This source generator is meant to replace the use of `RegexOptions.Compiled`, having the upside of fast execution without the downside of having to interpret the regex and emit the IL to get the compiled version when the regex is instantiated. 

More information on the downsides of `RegexOptions.Compiled` and how the source generator addresses them can be found [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/regular-expression-source-generators).

Also from that linked document, this is the recommendation of when to use the source generator:

> The general guidance is if you can use the source generator, use it. If you're using Regex today in C# with arguments known at compile time, and especially if you're already using RegexOptions.Compiled (because the regex has been identified as a hot spot that would benefit from faster throughput), you should prefer to use the source generator. The source generator will give your regex the following benefits:
> 
> - All the throughput benefits of RegexOptions.Compiled.
> - The startup benefits of not having to do all the regex parsing, analysis, and compilation at run time.
> - The option of using ahead-of-time compilation with the code generated for the regex.
> - Better debuggability and understanding of the regex.
> - The possibility to reduce the size of your trimmed app by trimming out large swaths of code associated with RegexCompiler (and potentially even reflection emit itself).

So, moving forward, we should move from `RegexOptions.Compiled` and use the `GeneratedRegex` instead. This PR moves pretty much every existing compiled regex to a source generated one. 

## Why should we do this?
First and foremost, it's Microsoft recommendation since .NET 7 (we are in .NET 8 and in a few months moving to .NET 10). But also, we've been trying to soften the CPU spikes that we are seeing during startup, as they are a problem in the SOE shared architecture when we deploy to multiple tenants in the same cluster at the same time. During startup a lot of types are loaded and with them their static properties, including lots of compiled Regex that need to be interpreted and a compiled version generated (emitted IL). With the source generated version, nothing really happens. 

Disclaimer: I wasn't able to measure a startup execution time difference with these changes. Startup times has a lot of variance and the impact of the changes seem to fall withing that variance. That being said, it's a fact that the app has to do less work during startup with the source generated version of the Regex, so it's still a net positive change.

## How to review and test it
There are so many changes in this PR, but fortunately, they are very straight forward. What I did after pushing all the changes, was to go file by file in this PR and check that the old version Regex matches the right version (ctrl+f) and that the options also match, minus the `RegexOptions.Compiled`.

About testing it, we have automated test which hopefully will are covering most of them, and then I think we can YOLO it in Pubplat prod and monitor exceptions.
title: PRODPLAT-207 Use source generator for compiled regex

author: TheSpivack
body:
Jira: DISCOCD-204

## Summary

In #24072, custom middleware was added to support web socket connections through the Fragment Proxy.  

With that implementation, the JWT token that is sent for all other fragment proxy requests was not included. This impacted the upstream service which expects likely expects the web socket connection to be authenticated in the same way that all other requests are authenticated. 

After many attempts to get the JWT created in the middleware, it was proving to be exceedingly difficult to get `Current.User` working in the custom middleware.  If the middleware was added before `.UseMvc()` the authentication context was not yet available.  If the custom middleware was after the `.UseMvc()`, then the web socket requests were being handled by the default MVC controller and never handled by the middleware.

Instead, that custom middleware has been removed, instead replacing its functionality directly in the `HtmlFragmentProxy` code

## How to Test

1. See instructions at https://github.com/StackEng/AskStack/pull/216
title: [DISCOCD-204] Support JWT authentication when using the fragment proxy  with web sockets

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
This PR attempts to resolve an issue where webpack builds would be triggered too often.

The issue here seems to be that when building webpack and the resulting manifest _contents_ do not change, the last modified time of `webpack-manifest.json` isn't updated which on the surface kind of makes sense.

However, this could cause problems when the generated client side product events would have a newer modification time than `webpack-manifest.json` as MSBuild solely checks on file modification times.

As the `webpack-manifest.json` would never be touched, this meant that webpack would always be called on build even if no changes were made to the generated Typescript files.

In this PR we no longer remove `webpack-manifest.json` (which is one approach to solve this) but instead only _touch_ the file to change its modification time. While this is technically the same, it's a bit more robust.

Additionally a problem was identified in the client side product events which triggered this behaviour.

As the original C# class (or `record`) name would be used as the file name for the generated Typescript class this was susceptible to name collisions. And that's exactly what happened, there were naming collisions for:

- QuestionTitleLinkClickEvent
- ModalDismissedEvent
- ModalCompletedEvent

Effectively this meant that the files would be continuously overwritten and therefore receiving a new modification timestamp.

The Roslyn generator has been updated to detect this and raise the `PE0002` diagnostic if it finds a conflict.
title: [DX] Client side product events generation

KRAKEN-2271

## Summary

This PR adds [schema.org Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) markup to the `Master.cshtml` page. This is only enabled for public sites and always points to Stack Overflow as the organization. Most things are configurable in `SiteSettings.Master.cs`. If we want to turn this off in production, we just need to disable `Current.Site.Settings.Master.ShowStackOverflowOrganizationSchema` globally.

### Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp updates

This PR also updates `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis` and `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` to their latest version because I was running into [this error](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79673681/error-constructors-of-types-with-required-members-are-not-supported-in-this-ver) when trying to render models with `required` members.

## How to Test

1. Open any page on https://meta.stackexchange.local/
2. Ensure that the schema.org markup is present towards the top of the page source. Locally, it looks like:  
```
<script type="application/ld+json">
    {
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@graph": [
    {
      "@type": "WebSite",

5. Make a request to an endpoint that basic tier (so all DL) has access to> should return a 200

**Data Licensing - Premium**

4. Verify your configuration with the query below
5. Make a request to an endpoint that basic tier (so all DL) has access to> should return a 200

**Data Licensing - AWS**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as data licensing https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=4&dryRun=false
2. Clear any existing tiers from the DB `DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @appId`
3. Use developer route to mark your app as AWS https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=3&dryRun=false
4. Verify your configuration with the query below
5. Make a request to an endpoint that basic tier (so all DL) has access to> should return a 200
6. Make a request to premium-only endpoint > should return a 403 with tier upgrade message

**Data Licensing - AWS & Premium**
**Note: This is a hypothetical scenario where AWS becomes a Premium customer and should also have access to Premium routes but with their custom allowed sites list. In reality, AWS is a Basic customer.**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as data licensing https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=4&dryRun=false
2. Clear any existing tiers from the DB `DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @appId`
3. Use developer route to mark your app as Premium https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=2&dryRun=false
4. Use developer route to mark your app as AWS https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=3&dryRun=false
5. Verify your configuration with the query below
6. Make a request to an endpoint that basic tier (so all DL) has access to> should return a 200
7. Make a request to premium-only endpoint > should return a 200

**Data Licensing Tier Caching**
1. Add breakpoints to `GetDataLicensingTiersFromApiApplicationAsync` and `ClearApiApplicationDataLicensingTierCacheEntry` in `DataLicensingTierService.cs`
2. Make a request > validate that the value is cached and then fetched from cache on subsequent calls
3. Update the data licensing tier on an app and validate that the cache entry is removed

**SQL Query to validate your configuration**
```
SELECT AA.Id, AA.Name, AAT.Description AS [ApplicationType], DLT.Description AS [Tier] FROM ApiApplications AA
JOIN ApiApplicationTypes AAT ON AA.ApplicationTypeId = AAT.Id
LEFT JOIN ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier AADT ON AA.Id = AADT.ApiApplicationId
LEFT JOIN DataLicensingTiers DLT ON AADT.DataLicensingTierId = DLT.Id
WHERE AA.Id = Id
```

author: kylejrp
body:
KRAKEN-2273

## Summary

This PR adds schema.org markup to Questions\Show.cshtml and Homepage\QuestionsList.cshtml as part of the SEO audit. It adds support for rendering this markup in PostSummary.cshtml as well.

### schema.org structure

The Questions\Show.cshtml and Homepage\QuestionsList.cshtml are both considered to be a [schema.org CollectionPage](https://schema.org/CollectionPage). That CollectionPage contains a [ItemList](https://schema.org/ItemList), which contains several [ListItems](https://schema.org/ListItem). Those each ListItem contains a [Question](https://schema.org/Question). If the PostSummary is displaying a Question/Answer pair, it the Question would also contain an [Answer](https://schema.org/Answer), but that doesn't happen on these specific pages.

### PostSummary changes

PostSummary now contains two extra model parameters:
- `ShowSchemaMetadata`, which turns on rendering of schema.org markup
- `SchemaMetadataPosition`, which renders the schema.org position attribute on the ListItem

When `ShowSchemaMetadata` is `true`, we wrap the entire PostSummary inside a `div` which acts as a ListItem. This breaks the border rendering which depended on each `.s-post-summary` being sibling elements, so we have to manually add the border classes to the containing div.

### ItemType and ItemProp helpers

I added two methods to PostTypeId that support all current PostTypeIds:
- `GetSchemaItemType` which gets the schema.org item type
- `GetSchemaItemProp` which gets the schema.org item property

I also added corresponding helpers to Post so you can do `post.GetSchemaItemType()` and `post.GetSchemaItemProp()`. 

I replaced all references to these schema item types and props in other pages to keep it centralized.


### Exceptions for unsupported PostTypeIds

If we ever try to render schema.org markup for an unsupported PostTypeId, this will log an exception and only throw if it's in debug. This means that if someone else tries to render a PostSummary with `ShowSchemaMetadata` or tries to use one of the other helper methods on an unsupported PostTypeId, they'll catch it early in development. None of these should get hit in production, but if they do, we'll see a crapton of exceptions in our logs.

## How to Test

1. Go to https://meta.stackexchange.local/ and make sure it renders the same. Paste the entire source of the page into https://validator.schema.org/ and make sure that the CollectionPage validates correctly.
2. Go to https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions and make sure it renders the same. Paste the entire source of the page into https://validator.schema.org/ and make sure that the CollectionPage validates correctly.

Note that you won't be able to validate this schema markup with [Google's Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results) because CollectionPage is not [one of the supported objects on that test](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery).
title: KRAKEN-2273 Add schema markup to Questions\Show.cshtml and Homepage\QuestionsList.cshtml

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
In SOE, the monolith deployments use the default values defined by the charts for the liveliness and readiness health probes. These values were just some defaults introduced when the charts were created but with the intention that each product adjusted them with sensible values for their context, which didn't happen for SOE. 

For example, the liveliness and readiness probes in several apps has a period of 10 seconds. This has a few undesirable consequences:
- If a pod becomes unready (readiness probe conditions do not pass), it takes K8s up to 10 seconds to realize and stop sending traffic. In practice this is not an issue, because our readiness probe doesn't do anything fancy, just returns if the webserver is app, and if the pod crashes, K8s will stop sending traffic immediately. However, if we later add more logic to the readiness health probe, this might become an issue.
- During a rolling deployment, a pod will be started and we'll check every 10 secs if it's ready. That means that if the pod gets ready at the 11th second, we'll be unnecessarily be waiting for 9 extra seconds. This happens for every pod that starts. 

The second point is what concerns us for SOE deployments and what we are trying to address with this PR. The idea is to decrease the readiness/liveliness periods to 1 second, so that once the app is ready, we mark the pod as ready asap. As mentioned above, we don't do anything crazy in these health checks, so doing a request per second, even during startup, it won't overload the pod. 

By dropping the liveliness probe to 1 sec, with a failureThreshold of 3, it would mean that the pod would need to start in less than 3 seconds or it will be restarted. To address this scenario, several apps already support startup probes, and this PR adds support to the deployments that didn't. 

When the startup probe is setup, K8s will hold the liveliness and readiness checks until the startup probe succeeds. So we give the startup probe a period of 1 sec and a failureThreshold of 300, allowing for a startup of 5 minutes (we can extend it if we need to). After that the liveliness and readiness probes will run every sec, quickly picking up tha that the pod is ready.

Finally, this PR also updates the `successThreshold = 1` for the readiness probe. I'm not entirely sure why the default has been 3 for all apps, because that means that K8s has to wait for 3 successful readiness checks until it marks the pod as ready. Given that our readiness endpoint only checks if the webservers is responding and that K8s default is 1 (good for most use cases), I think that 1 is a good value, which will also make startups faster.
title: PRODPLAT-178 Add startup probe and reduce liveliness/readiness periods in SOE

## Summary
This PR adds the `BlockSensitiveSiteAttribute.cs` attribute to the DL API project so DL apps are blocked from accessing sensitive sites. This PR also adds some units tests & updates integration test setup so tests run for an allowed site and pass instead of throwing a 403. 

## How to Test
**note: copied some steps from #23590  

1. Follow the steps below to set up you app as a DL app with Premium tier. It will set Literature SE (id 668) as a sensitive site and set Meta SE (id 4) as an allowed site. Note that the tier is not really relevant here since we haven't migrated the `TierRequired` attribute yet.
```
DECLARE @AppId INT = YourAppID
DECLARE @DataTierId INT = 2; -- Premium
DECLARE @MetaSiteId INT = 4; -- Meta SE
DECLARE @LiteratureSiteId INT = 668; -- Literature SE

/*--------------------------------
* Setup application
--------------------------------*/
UPDATE ApiApplications SET ApplicationTypeId = 4 WHERE Id = @AppId
DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @AppId
INSERT INTO ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier(ApiApplicationId, DataLicensingTierId) VALUES (@AppId, @DataTierId)

/*--------------------------------
* Setup sites
--------------------------------*/
DELETE FROM DataLicensingTierSites WHERE DataLicensingTierId = @DataTierId AND SiteId IN (@LiteratureSiteId, @MetaSiteId)
INSERT INTO DataLicensingTierSites (DataLicensingTierId, SiteId) VALUES (@DataTierId, @MetaSiteId)
```
2. Validate the query output.
```
DECLARE @AppId INT = YourAppID
DECLARE @MetaSiteId INT = 4; -- Meta SE
DECLARE @LiteratureSiteId INT = 668; -- Literature SE

/*--------------------------------
* Validate output
--------------------------------*/
SELECT AA.Id, AA.Name, AAT.Description AS [ApplicationType], DLT.Description AS [Tier] FROM ApiApplications AA
JOIN ApiApplicationTypes AAT ON AA.ApplicationTypeId = AAT.Id
LEFT JOIN ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier AADT ON AA.Id = AADT.ApiApplicationId
LEFT JOIN DataLicensingTiers DLT ON AADT.DataLicensingTierId = DLT.Id
WHERE AA.Id = @AppId

SELECT DT.Name, S.Name, S.BaseHostAddress, S.Id FROM DataLicensingTierSites DTS 
JOIN Sites S ON DTS.SiteId = S.Id
JOIN DataLicensingTiers DT ON DT.Id = DTS.DataLicensingTierId 
WHERE SiteId IN (@LiteratureSiteId, @MetaSiteId)
```
3. Make requests. It should pass with `meta.stackexchange.local` but fail on `literature.stackexchange.local`.

## Summary

This PR adds support to add/ update keys on a customer key vault on SOE instance. 

Infra team created a test key vault for us on `nova` for local testing: [novaue1dev-local-kv](https://portal.azure.com/#@soedev.onmicrosoft.com/resource/subscriptions/daa60db7-9c52-4dc5-9707-24d63104d93a/resourceGroups/novaue1dev/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/novaue1dev-local-kv/secrets)

Behavior:
1. On first run, new secret key-value pairs would be created

To avoid dealing with retention and purging mechanism, we are going with this approach.

NOTE: test key vault does allow us to delete and then purge the keys with no vretention period but that won't be true for our SOE instances.

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
In the new SOE cell architecture, we've seen that our deployments had too much of a spread between CPU requests and limits. As a consequence, K8s scheduled too many new pods into the same node generating big CPU spikes. 

We increased the requests, however that has the undesirable effect of "reserving" that CPU capacity for the whole lifetime of the pod, although big CPU spike happens only at startup. 

@SanderKnape found [this K8s controller](https://github.com/google/kube-startup-cpu-boost) by Google that mutates pods request/limits by boosting them during startup and then dropping them back to their normal levels. 

To add this behavior, we need to deploy a custom resource of type `StartupCPUBoost`, specifying which pods it affects and which of their containers, together with the boosted requests/limits and the condition to drop it back to normal. 

The initial idea was to add this customer resource to each of the helm charts, however Helm doesn't guarantee an ordering in which resources are created, and when the deployment gets created before the StartupCPUBoost is, the pods are created without the boost. 

So, we decided to create a small chart inside the cnab folder that creates the `StartupCPUBoost`. The idea is that we install that chart in the same namespace that the apps will be running, before the app chart is installed. 

Everything is configurable ([this PR](https://github.com/StackEng/deployment-pipeline-variables/pull/305) sets the values), so we can enable/disable it per app and set boosted cpu requests and limits per app. 

When we decide to disable it, the cnab scripts will check if a release of the `startup-cpu-boost` was already created and uninstall it, removing the StartupCPUBoost .
title: PRODPLAT-171 Add startup cpu boost for SOE deployment

author: dionrhys
body:
This PR adds in publishing of this repo's container images to the new Azure Container Registry and GCP Artifact Registry that we've set up to migrate container images away from Cloudsmith. It does not remove the existing publishing of images to Cloudsmith and does not switch anything to _consume_ the images from these new registries either.

There's quite a few changes to get this working. I've rebased the PR to make it a little easier to review commit-by-commit instead of looking at all file changes at once.

Here's a summary of the changes:

- **Support multiple Docker registries in the Bake file**
  - This refactors the docker-bake.hcl file to support tagging images with multiple repositories instead of just one - the main change being to the `get_tags` function in the HCL
- **Login to ACR and GCP registries**
  - This refactors the repeated docker login steps in the workflows to be a shared step at [.github/actions/login-docker-registries/action.yml](.github/actions/login-docker-registries/action.yml)
  - It changes the three image-building workflows (acceptance-tests, create-releases, and pr-environment-create) to use this new shared action and adds sign-in to ACR and GCP
- **Remove registry login from Acceptance Tests**
  - The Functional Acceptance Tests don't actually publish or source images from Cloudsmith so the login to Cloudsmith, ACR and GCP was removed from this workflow and comments added to explain that
- **Don't build SO CNAB image in PR envs**
  - The Pubplat PR environments don't need the SO CNAB image and building that was requiring the pr-environment-create workflow to login to Cloudsmith to get the so-pubplat-cnab-v1 image
  - This commit fixes that by taking the CNAB building out of the main `public_and_teams` build target so that we could remove the login from the PR env workflow
  - This also meant I added the CNAB target explicitly to the create-releases workflow so the real image building workflow would still publish the CNAB image (this also matches how it's done for Enterprise)
- **Remove GCP login from SOE**
  - SOE doesn't run on GCP so we're not going to publish its images there
- **Multi-publish real images and PR env images**
  - This does the actual publishing of images to the new registries
  - The create-releases workflow will publish the real app images for deployment to AKS or GCP clusters
  - The pr-environment-create workflow will publish PR environment images for deployment to the AKS cluster
- **Remove GitHub org/repo prefix from image names published to ACR and GCP Registry**
  - This repo's images were always prefixed "stackeng/stackoverflow" which bloated the image name quite a bit
  - We don't typically prefix image names like this for Free Refills based repos
  - We agreed in Slack to remove these prefixes from the images published to ACR and GCP Registry: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C09712XAE3S/p1760634431575139
  - Images published to Cloudsmith still use the prefixes

# Testing

Check out the workflow runs for these workflow jobs below:

- Create Releases / Public and Teams release
- Create Releases / Enterprise release
- Functional Acceptance Tests
- PR Environment Create / Build Docker images

You can see the images being published to the new registries here:

- https://portal.azure.com/#@stackoverflow.com/resource/subscriptions/e485d432-33f7-4a10-b06a-90efad85d7d5/resourceGroups/mgmt-container-registry/providers/Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/stackeng/repository

author: SteffiPeTaffy
body:
## Hydrate OpinionBasedContentType for posts

### Summary
This change adds support for preloading the **opinion-based content type** when hydrating posts (e.g., for question lists).  
The goal is to make `Post.OpinionBasedContentType` available immediately during hydration, avoiding a separate lazy-loading query per post.

### Changes
- **Database**
  - Added an index on `OpinionBasedContent(PostId)`
  - This allows fast lookups and joins when hydrating multiple posts at once.

- **Model**
  - Updated `Post`:
    - Made `OpinionBasedContentType` internally settable.
    - Retained lazy-loading logic only as fallback when type not hydrated.

- **Type handling**
  - Registered a new Dapper type handler for `OpinionBasedContentType`
    - Maps the DB `VARCHAR(50)` value to the enum (case-insensitive).
    - Registered in `SqlMapperExtensions.Configure()`.

- **Hydration**
  - Updated `QuestionListViewData.LoadPosts()` to:
    - Add a **LEFT JOIN** on `OpinionBasedContent` (by `PostId`).
    - Select the `ContentType` column.
    - Assign the enum value directly to `Post.OpinionBasedContentType` during materialization.

### Why
- Removes the need for one query per post when checking if a post is opinion-based.
- Reduces latency and DB load on question list pages.

### Out of Scope
- No frontend or rendering changes in this PR.
- The `PostSummary` and `OpinionBasedContentInfo` UI updates will follow in a separate PR.
title: CE-1953 Add opinion-based content hydration and index for Post

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
In SOE cell clusters we host multiple customers apps in the same cluster. This means, that if we have 10 customers, we’ll have 20 StackOverflow pods, 20 Apiv2 pods, 20 Apiv3 pods, etc (2 pods per deployment). 

We currently set topologySpreadConstraints to try to run the 2 pods per deployment in different nodes, however, there is no spread definition between the different customers. So technically, it’s possible that K8s places 10 StackOverflow pods in NodeA and 10 StackOverflow pods in NodeB, while playing 10 Apiv2 pods in NodeC and 10 Apiv2 pods in NodeD. 

This is not ideal for multiple reasons:

- When we deploy, we deploy multiple instances simultaneously, and they all deploy the apps in the same order. This means that StackOverflow pods will all start at the same time. If all these apps go to the same 2 nodes, instead of being spread between all nodes, those 2 nodes will be overwhelmed during the app startup (CPU spike). We have already seen deployments failing due to this. 
- Each app has a different CPU profile, they use the CPU at different moments and at different rates. If we run different apps in the same node, their profiles won’t match exactly, meaning that some CPU peaks from one app might match with CPU valleys of another app, smoothing the CPU utilization profile. This is particularly important when we think about scheduled routes, where for example the daily route hits every instance at 3am, so the Stack Overflow pods all start working at the exact same time, doing some heavy tasks.

This PR makes this section conditional of the `topologySpreadConstraints`:
```
matchLabelKeys:
            - pod-template-hash
```
Each pod gets a `pod-template-hash` that's unique per deployment. By not adding this, we can tell K8s to spread pods as even as possible (`maxSkew: 1`) just considering the service name. The service name is `stackoverflow`, `apiv2`, `apiv3`, etc, it's the same between the different customers, so K8s would try to spread all the stackoverflow pods as evenly as possible, indepedently of the customer. 

Enabling this behavior is controlled by the `spreadAppsOnlyByServiceNameAcrossNodes`, and only used for cell based customers, we are not making any changes for non-cell customers. 

This PR requires this deployment pipelines PR to be merged first: https://github.com/StackEng/deployment-pipeline-variables/pull/302
title: PRODPLAT-168 Spread SOE apps across the nodes more evenly
