author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
[**Jira - YETI2-711**](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-711)

This PR removes the site setting code path from `AppTypeRequiredAttribute.cs`. Like `BlockSensitiveSiteAttribute.cs`, this attribute uses `OnActionExecutionAsync` which is not as straightforward as it's synchronous counterpart. `OnActionExecutionAsync` can execute code before AND after an "action" occurs. 

Primarily, we need to be careful of:
1) Using `return` when `context.Result` is null. Doing this will return a 200 status code but with an empty response. It is okay to `return` after `context.Result` has been set so we can short-circuit the request.
2) We need to call `next()` at least once so we can actually continue executing the request. This should only happen if `context.Result` remains `null`.
3) We must always call `next()` on Teams and never execute any other logic. This is why there is an if/else block on the method.

This PR also removes several site settings we have been using for Data Licensing customers. The main site setting `APIv3_OverflowAPI_AppIds_DbValue` will be removed as part of another Jira card ([YETI2-767](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-767)).

The `BlockSensitiveSiteAttribute` clean up was addressed in another PR. https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23715

## Notes on Testing
There was a handful of integration tests that I had to update since I was removed several OAPI site settings. One pain point, is the `BlockSensitiveSiteAttribute.cs` which requires that the site be listed in the `DataLicensingTierSites` table. Since tests run in parallel, we need to be careful of the modifications we make to this table, otherwise we could introduce flaky Data Licensing tests. 

To avoid potential flaky behavior, I tried different approaches:
1) A test collection - This would cause the tests in the collection to run sequentially (but in parallel to other collections). We have enough tests to probably not notice a change in run time but feel it's a slippery slope.
2) Toggle attribute with site setting - My gripe with this is that I was introducing a site setting for testing only. If this was only a DL code base, I would not want to "feature flag" this behavior. 
3) No-op implementation - Use a no-op implementation and only sub the real implementation when we are testing the block sensitive site attribute.

Ultimately, after flip-flopping between the no-op implementation and site setting, I decided to settle on the no-op implementation since I felt it was the "cleanest" approach. 

## How to Test
**Note: Verify that [time based pagination is off](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled) and that [`meta.stackexchange.local` is an allowed site for all tiers](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/allowed-sites).**

**Regular Application** 
1. Use developer route to mark your app as regular https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=1&dryRun=false
2. Verify your configuration using https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/app-info?appIds={appId}
3. Run the test script below and validate the output  - Only /questions return 200. The rest return a 403 and should not have a message about "upgrading".

**Moderator**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as moderator https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=2&dryRun=false
2. Verify your configuration using https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/app-info?appIds={appId}
4. Run the test script below and validate the output  - Only /questions and /discussions return 200. The rest return a 403 and should not have a message about "upgrading".

**Data Licensing - Basic**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as data licensing https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=4&dryRun=false
2. Clear any existing tiers from the DB `DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @appId`
3. Use developer route to mark your app as basic https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=1&dryRun=false
4. Verify your configuration using https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/app-info?appIds={appId}
5. Run the test script below and validate the output  - Only /questions return 200. The rest return a 403 with a message on "upgrading tiers".

**Data Licensing - Premium**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as data licensing https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=4&dryRun=false
2. Clear any existing tiers from the DB `DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @appId`
3. Use developer route to mark your app as premium https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=2&dryRun=false
4. Verify your configuration using https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/app-info?appIds={appId}
5. Run the test script below and validate the output - All return 200

**Data Licensing - AWS**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as data licensing https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=4&dryRun=false
2. Clear any existing tiers from the DB `DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @appId`
3. Use developer route to mark your app as AWS https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=3&dryRun=false
4. Verify your configuration using https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/app-info?appIds={appId}
5. Run the test script below and validate the output - Only /questions returns 200. The rest return a 403 with a message on "upgrading tiers".

**Data Licensing - AWS & Premium**
**Note: This is a hypothetical scenario where AWS becomes a Premium customer and should also have access to Premium routes but with their custom allowed sites list. In reality, AWS is a Basic customer.**
1. Use developer route to mark your app as data licensing https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/update-app-type?appIds={appId}&appType=4&dryRun=false
2. Clear any existing tiers from the DB `DELETE FROM ApiApplicationDataLicensingTier WHERE ApiApplicationId = @appId`
3. Use developer route to mark your app as Premium https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=2&dryRun=false
4. Use developer route to mark your app as AWS https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/data-licensing/add-tier-to-app?appIds={appId}&tierId=3&dryRun=false
5. Verify your configuration using https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/api/app-info?appIds={appId}
7. Run the test script below and validate the output - All should return 200

**Test Powershell Script**
1. Copy the script below to a `.ps` file locally
2. Open the command prompt and run the command `powershell .\yeti2-706-test-script.ps1 -AuthorizationToken "YOUR_API_KEY"`

```
param (
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [string]$AuthorizationToken
)

$Routes = @(
    "https://api.stackexchange.local/v3/sites/meta.stackexchange.local/questions",
    "https://api.stackexchange.local/v3/sites/meta.stackexchange.local/discussions",
    "https://api.stackexchange.local/v3/sites/meta.stackexchange.local/content-feeds/changes/questions?to=7/31/2025&from=7/25/2025"
)

$Notes = @(
    "A route available to everybody",
    "A route available to only premium DL customers and moderators",
    "A route available to only premium DL customers"
)

if ($Routes.Count -ne $Notes.Count) {
    Write-Error "The number of routes must match the number of notes."
    return
}

for ($i = 0; $i -lt $Routes.Count; $i++) {
    $url = $Routes[$i]
    $note = $Notes[$i]

    try {
        $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer " + $AuthorizationToken } -Method Get -ErrorAction Stop

        Write-Output "URL: $url"
        Write-Output "Note: $note"
        Write-Output "Status Code: $($response.StatusCode)"

    } catch [System.Net.WebException] {
        $errorResponse = $_.Exception.Response
        $statusCode = $errorResponse.StatusCode.Value__

        Write-Output "URL: $url"
        Write-Output "Note: $note"
        Write-Output "Status Code: $statusCode"

        if ($statusCode -eq 403) {
            $responseStream = $errorResponse.GetResponseStream()
            $reader = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($responseStream)
            $reader.BaseStream.Position = 0
            $reader.DiscardBufferedData()
            $responseBody = $reader.ReadToEnd();

            Write-Output "Response Body: $responseBody"
        }
    }

    Write-Output "`n"
}
```

[YETI2-767]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-767?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ
title: YETI2-711 - Remove site setting code path in `AppTypeRequiredAttribute.cs` and remove several Overflow API site settings

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
This PR introduces a new authentication handler specifically for service-to-service calls in the StackOverflow landscape as described in [Simplifying Authentication for Monolith Integration](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iREdZc-DC3R6gASxSQKdnmog6109EMagQXQDTepRthk/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.5zki3rrsw04p).

Depending on configuration, this will allow services using Workload Identity in Kubernetes to authenticate against APIv3 and provides them with the authorization to make _read_ and, when configured via an allow list, _write_ calls.

The way this works is that a service deployed to Kubernetes can request a token via Workload Identity.
That token is then applied in the `Authorization` header on the HTTP request being made to APIv3.

APIv3 is configured to accept tokens from the identity providers in Azure and GCP, which allows it to verify:
- That the issuer is trusted
- That the token signature is valid
- That the requested audience is allowed in

When a token is deemed valid, the handler checks if an `ApiApplication` already exists for the _subject_ (the `sub` claim).
If not, a `ApiApplication` entry is created automatically and linked to the Community User (`accountId` of `-1`). It is also assigned write permissions when the subject identified in the token is on the allow list in the `APIv3_WorkloadIdentity_SubjectsAllowedToWrite` site setting.

The `ApiApplication` is given the type `ApiApplicationType.StackExchange` so we can identify it as one of ours and we can use that information when segregating API call volumes for example for billing purposes.

Subsequent calls will locate the `ApiApplication` by name (the `sub` claim from the token) owned by the community user.

Once these are provided, the `ClaimsIdentity` is constructed similar to the `JwtAccessTokenAuthenticationHandler` or `OpaqueAccessTokenAuthenticationHandler` which in turn is provisioned on the `Current.User`.

## How do we know this works?

Good question!

There are a set of integration tests that verify the behaviour
title: [AUTH] Support Workload Identity authentication for APIv3

## Summary

A new svelte island for filtering suspicious votes with additional options, in advance of Free Votes.  We can now filter by the voter rep, target user rep, and the date of detection.

## Known issues

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR removes the site setting code path from `BlockSensitiveSiteAttribute.cs`. Unfortunately, it was not a cut and paste as I anticipated. `OnActionExecutionAsync` is not as straightforward as its synchronous counter-part. This method can execute code before and after an action. It uses the delegate `next()` to continue along the request pipeline.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/mvc/controllers/filters?view=aspnetcore-9.0#implementation

There are three things I had to be cautious of when updating this:
1. Be careful of using `return`. If `context.Result` is not set then it can return a 200 with an empty response even though the action didn't execute/pipeline.
2. Setting `context.Result` will short-circuit the request which is fine if validation fails. But `context.Result` must be `null` if we want to continue going through the request pipeline and it must be followed by `next()`.
3. `next()` should be called only once and must always be called on Teams and Enterprise. 

There are several different ways to organize this code. I initially opted to keep a separate method that returns an `ObjectResult` to do the validation and not worry about when to call `next()` but felt it was awkward and roundabout. I finally settled on more nested conditionals.

## How to Test
The testing steps from this PR can be used ---> https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23590 (Database implementation steps only)

Personal digests were failing with the error:

```plaintext
.Url() error. Fragment (starts with https?://): https://{hostURL}/posts/comments/{commentId}?r=MsTeamsPersonalDigestReminders&noredirect=1

body:
## Summary

Reintroduces control of deleted follow-ups to the backend, based on moderator status. This is necessary as currently deletion user data is visible to non-mods who happen to view the question page source (and are in the 10% with Jones enabled, of course).

Essentially mods will still have everything (included deleted FUs) delivered, with Svelte then used to control visibility.

Non-mods should never be able to see deleted stuff, so they're filtered out for them.

The one caveat: non-mods _should_ be able to see deleted 'middle' FUs, i.e. those that have a non-deleted reply and show as `[deleted] [deleted]`. These should have the deletion user data stripped out.

There are also a couple of very small UI tweaks, mainly not showing the middle deleted FUs in red as it looks a bit weird if you're a non-mod who never otherwise sees that.

## How to Test

1. Jones on (for all, or logged-in at least)
2. Probably want a second (incognito) window; one impersonating a mod, the other a non-mod
3. Find or create the following scenario:
  a. Deleted top level FU
  b. Deleted 'middle' threaded FU (obviously need 2 levels of nesting here)
  c. Deleted 'end' threaded FU (just 1 level is fine)
  d. Deleted 'middle' _and_ 'end' FUs
  d. Enough other FUs that 'show more' is showing
4. Check across the two windows that everything makes sense:
  a. Both views are the same initially; only the 'middle' deleted FU with non-deleted reply is visible, showing as `[deleted] [deleted]`
  b. Mod can see all deleted FUs (after hitting 'show deleted'), non-mod can't
  c. All counts are correct (total number, 'show more' number, Remember that 'middle' FU doesn't contribute to count), including when mod shows deleted
  d. Check that `DeletionUser` prop does not exist in page source for non-mod
title: [CE-1835] filter deleted comments on backend for non-mods

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR updates the API v3 identity rate limiter to work on a 24-hour fixed window based on the time of the first request to discourage users from all using the API at the same time. Previously, all users had their request count reset at the start of the UTC day.  API v2 also uses a 24-hour window that is unique per user.

### Limitations of fixed window
Fixed window algorithms do not address "burstiness". However, we have other rate limits in place both at the application and edge level that do. 

### **Sliding vs Fixed Windows**
Originally, we set out to use a sliding window however the **sliding window log** algorithm but this approach is memory intensive and unlikely to scale well. This method requires that every single request be logged. The set of logs is then continuously trimmed to represent the last time period. The main issue for us is the amount of time we are tracking (24-hours vs 30 minutes) and the high rate limit (100k for Data Licensing customers) means we would be using quite a bit of memory to keep track. In addition, we would need to use Lua script to perform the operations atomically. This code must run fast on Redis since it blocks all other operations. 

An alternative to sliding window log is **sliding window counter**. This approach is used by companies like Cloudflare. It is a lot less memory intensive than window log and implementations either uses 2 counters OR a much smaller set. The drawback of this approach is that it is prediction based and therefore not precise. Tracking over a 24-hour period increases the chances of being "off". 

- https://www.figma.com/blog/an-alternative-approach-to-rate-limiting/
- https://blog.cloudflare.com/counting-things-a-lot-of-different-things/

| Approach  |  Pros |Cons   |  
|---|---|---|
| Fixed Window Counter  | Simple to implement. Easier for users to keep track of when their limit will entirely reset.  |  Does not prevent burstiness.  Less forgiving to users than sliding window. |
|  Sliding Window Log | Precise and more forgiving to users since the number of allowed requests is rolling. Prevents burstiness.  | Very memory intensive.   | 
| Sliding Window Counter  | Less memory intensive than window log. Prevents burstiness. | Not precise since it is based on prediction.   |  

## How to Test
1. Make a request to the API and record the number of requests left ` x-rate-limit-calls-left` and the number of seconds to reset `x-rate-limit-seconds-until-reset`. This value should be 86400 (60 seconds * 60 minutes * 24 hours).
2. Wait about a minute and make another request. The number of calls left should be reduced by one and the number of seconds to reset should be less than 86400. 
3. To test that the entry actually expires, you can change the value of `FixedWindowSeconds` to something like 3 minutes. After 3 minutes, your calls left should reset.
title: YETI2-180 - Change identity rate limiter to use a 24-hour fixed window based on first request

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

This implements the banner saying that the user can now comment. It's both implemented in Razor and in svelte, just in case, cause I don't know what UI will be released when we inform users that they can comment.

Why use banner and not for example typical achievements? This way we can inform only part of users => that allows for gradual rollout. It also gives us an option to roll it back if needed (I don't think it's super easy with achievements).

Open question is whether we use a user preference to steer the banner or we create a new table.
- Why user settings? That's the pattern we generally use even for dismissing banners. It also introduces no changes to the db, so it _looks simpler_.
- Why a separate table? Cause we want to have this banner only temporarily. A user setting, if once used, shouldn't be reused, and it's all saved in one column in the db as serialized string. So after we no longer need this setting, some mess still remains. _This is cleaner._

I went with a new table that can be later cleaned up easily.

## How to Test

1. Make sure the [new comments ui is enabled](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.ShowNewFollowUpUIFor)

6. See the banner
7. Enable [Jones for all](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Comments.FollowUpsIndianaJonesEnabledFor)

This PR enables the delete action functionality for the ingestion review queue.

If the user has deletion rights (testengadmin), they will be presented with a browser confirmation dialog to confirm. If the user confirms, the post will be deleted and the review task will be completed and deleted.

If the user does not have deletion rights, (testquestionasker, testquestionanswerer), there will be no confirmation dialog and the post will be flagged as "RecommendDelete". Once a threshold is hit, stored in the site setting Ingestion.RecommendedDeletionTaskResultsToDeletePost, the post is deleted and the review task is completed.

## Note to PR reviewer

The existing review queue system uses the VoteAsync endpoint in PostsController.Voting for delete actions. The reason this works for us is that there is a check to see if the user doing the deletion has permission to delete a post. If they do, the post is deleted.

Because of the above, when a post is deleted by an admin the post history type is set to "Post Deleted" instead of "PostDeletedFromReview". This is because at the point that the deletion happens, we no longer have the context that the deletion is coming from a review queue. When a post is deleted by hitting the recommendation threshold, we control the deletion and it is set to `PostDeletedFromReview`.

This is preexisting behaviour and there is precedent for it in the Late Answer queue. We could change the deeper delete code if desired so that it knows that we are in the context of a review queue but I'm not sure we want to go that far.

## How to Test

#### To set up a testing scenario

1. Use the instructions on [this PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23440) to create a new ingested QA pair. Make sure you get a 201 back.
2. Hit [this developer endpoint](https://stackenterprise.local/developer/review/sync/15) in your browser to create a review task for the Ingested_Draft post that you imported with the Swagger page.
3. Navigate to the ingestion review queue at https://stackenterprise.local/review/ingestion to find an ingested post to review. 

#### For admins

5. Select the delete option in the radio button list and click "Submit".
6. There will be a browser confirmation dialog. Select "Cancel" - the dialog should close with no action taken
7. Selected delete again and submit and accept the confirmation dialog.
8. The post will no longer be visible in the queue. The review queue task will be completed and deleted, and the posts (question and answer) will be deleted.
9. Re-run the developer endpoint from step 2 to re-sync
10. The post should not be re-synced. If you only had one thing in your queue when deleting, your queue should still be empty. You can also use the query below to confirm that no new task was added.

#### For regular users

5. Log in as a non-admin user 
6. Select the delete option in the radio button list and click "Submit". There will be no confirmation dialog.
7. The review queue task will appear to be gone for this user, but the post is not deleted and the review queue task is not complete.
8. Log in as a second non-admin user
9.  Select the delete option in the radio button list and click "Submit". There will be no confirmation dialog.
10. The review queue task will be completed and deleted, and the post in question will also be deleted.

Using the query below on your `Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams` DB may be helpful to see that the ReviewTask is completed:

```sql
select rt.Id, rts.Name as ReviewTaskState, rt.CreationDate as ReviewTaskCreationDate, rt.DeletionDate as ReviewTaskDeletionDate, rtt.Name as ReviewTaskType, p.DeletionDate as PostDeletionDate, pt.Name as PostType, p.Title
from ReviewTasks rt
inner join ReviewTaskTypes rtt on rtt.Id = rt.ReviewTaskTypeId
inner join Posts p on p.Id = rt.PostId
inner join PostTypes pt on pt.Id = p.PostTypeId
inner join ReviewTaskStates rts on rts.Id = rt.ReviewTaskState
order by rt.CreationDate desc;
```

Query the posts table to confirm that your ingested question and its answer are both deleted:
```sql
select Title, DeletionDate from Posts order by CreationDate desc;
```

author: b-kelly
body:
TEAMS-14781

## Summary

This PR adds support for removing operations and schemas based on if a `Feature` is enabled. The major additions are:

1. `[FeatureCheck(Feature.Foo)]` - action filter on the controller that returns a 404 at runtime if the feature is not enabled for the current site
2. A document filter that keys off of the `FeatureCheckAttribute` to remove operations ("endpoints") from the OpenAPI doc (i.e. removes from Swagger) at runtime
3. A document filter that removes all unreferenced schemas ("models") from the OpenAPI doc at runtime

Items 2 and 3 are unfortunately both needed together. Simply removing an api operation doesn't also remove the schemas. I dug deep into the SwaggerGen and AspNet source code to ensure that this was the only way to achieve this goal _at runtime_. The [officially suggested solution](https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/blob/master/docs/configure-and-customize-swaggergen.md#omit-arbitrary-operations) unfortunately only happens at app startup, which means that we don't have a "current context" (no Site or DB access) when the code runs.

I also added some new helpers to better test Swagger code. The `SwaggerGeneratorHelper` class within the unit tests allows us to easily add tests for all the other (currently untested) filters.

## How to Test

1. Enable `Ingestion.APIEnabledFor` setting
5. Observe that the operation (`/ingest/questionandanswer`) and schemas (`Ingestion: Question Answer request model`, `Ingestion: Question Answer pair summary`) are present
6. Disable `Ingestion.APIEnabledFor` setting
7. Observe that the above operation _and_ the schemas have been removed

Additionally, you'll want to compare the `swagger.json` documents from both this and the `main` branch to ensure they are identical: https://stackenterprise.local/api/v3/swagger.json

body: MOD-221 | Previous PRs #23464 #23624 ## Summary * When legitimate content is take from a post and then resubmitted as spam, it can make that legitimate content show up in our recent spam list. Never reference any spam that was created more recently than the original post to guarantee that doesn't happen. Unfortunately, it also means that edits to old posts basically get a pass. But no way currently to mitigate this without worrying about false positives on edits from edits looking like themselves. ## How to Test 1. Find any post and mark it as spam That post should not be included in spam analysis for edits 2. Create a new post that is nearly identical to the spam post and it should be flagged in AEH as spam 3. Edit a post to nearly identical to the spam post whose creation date is **prior** to the creation date of the first post. It should **not be** flagged as spam Can search for posts something like this `created:..2022-11-03` 3. Create a new legitimate post (neccessarily after the first spam post deletion date). Then Edit it to be nearly identical to the spam post. It should **be** flagged as spam

TEAMS-14775

## Summary

This PR implements the Verify and publish action for the ingestion review queue process, as described in the Jira ticket.

## How to Test

### Setup
Setup goal: Have a question or Q/A pair with the PostState of 'Ingested_Draft` so that it shows up in the review queue.

#### 1. Add an ingested QA pair

Navigate to the review queue at https://stackenterprise.local/review/ingestion in your browser. You should see your new ingested question and answer (the answer will be in a tab).

#### 2. Verify and publish the post
Select the "Verify and publish" action radio button and click "Submit"

The review queue will now be empty, assuming this was your only reviewable ingested post.

author: nhu-van
body:
## Summary

Jira Teams-14752

<ins>**Issues**:</ins>
We updated the daily tag digest scheduler to send every 30 minutes instead of once per day. The scheduled job also sends emails in batches, processing 1000 subscriptions each time. This causes some users to receive multiple emails during a day in the following cases:
- When a user has multiple subscriptions, and their subscriptions are processed in 2 different batches.
- When a user already receives their daily digest email, but they add new watched tags. They will receive another email about the newly added tags at the next scheduled time.

<ins>**To fix the above issues**</ins>:
I updated the subscription query to:
- Group the subscriptions by owners. The batch size will be based on owners instead of individual subscriptions.
- Add `LastProcessedDate` column to indicate that a subscription is picked up by the scheduled route. It may or may not send out an email. 
- Exclude subscriptions if there are subscriptions already processed to the same owner within 24 hours.


## How to Test
- Log in as 3 different users (Example: user1, user2, user3)
- On the home page, add at least **3** watched tags for them. 
- Set watched tags for the first 2 users as "Daily", and the third one as "As soon as possible".
- Add some questions with the above watched tags (Might need to rebuild the Elastic Search to make it work)
- Update the [batch size](https://stackenterprise.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Tags.TagSubscriptionDailyBatchSize) to 1 for testing purposes.
- Run the [daily tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily)
- Check that only 1 email is sent to the **first** user (Ex: user1) and the subscriptions for this user are updated with the last sent date. (Ex: if you have 3 rows in the `TagSetRows` for user1, all 3 rows should be updated) 
```
-- Checking emails
SELECT *
FROM [Local.Enterprise.Sites.Teams].[dbo].[EmailMessages]
ORDER BY CreationDate desc

-- Checking tag subscriptions
SELECT *
FROM [Local.Enterprise.StackOverflow.Teams].dbo.TagSetRows
WHERE TagSetTypeId = 1 AND NotificationFrequencyTypeId = 2 AND OwnerUserId = {YOUR_USER_ID}
```
- Go back the Home page and add a new watched tag for the first user (Ex: user1)
- Run the [daily tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) again
- Check that you only receive 1 email for the **second** user (Ex: user2). The subscription row (`TagSetRows`) of the newly added watched tag should have `NULL` for the `LastSendDate` column. 
- Run the [daily tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-daily) again
- Check that you don't receive any other email
- Run the [15-minute tag digest route](https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/tag-digest-fifteen-minutes)
- Check that you receive 1 email for the **third** user (Ex: user3) and all the subscription rows for this user are updated.
title: Teams-14752-Update tag subscription query to not send new tags within the same day

## Summary

See TEAMS-15384

We introduced `IngestionFileUploads` table after the `IngestionSourcePostMetadata`. 
`IngestionSourcePostMetadata.IngestionFileUploadId` is a FK that was backfilled with a placeholder `IngestionFileUploads.Id = -1`
when we introduced `IngestionFileUploads` table.

This issue will not happen with live customers. This is atm happening on our test environments where a user tries to delete an old file that was uploaded prior to the introduction of `IngestionFileUploads` table.

## How to Test

1. Find an old IngestionSourcePostMetadata entry with IngestionFileUploadId = -1 i.e., pointing to the placeholder fileuploadid. If you don't have one in your local environment then just update one of the old records to point to one. You will have to update all the `IngestionSourcePostMetadata` entries associated with an uploaded file.
2. Go to the Ingestion homepage, find the ingestion job for the specific file and perform Delete action on it.
3. Delete action should be succesful and not throw a 500
4. Verify that the IngestionSourcePostMetadata entries were deleted in the db
5. Not adding additional tests as we already have tests in this workflow and I would be adding more tests soon when we switch up the sequence for TEAMS-15324.

author: jacob-adams
body:
The API response for the Customer Engagement User Id endpoint had the field name `stackOverflowUserId`, but it should just be `userId`. This was a mistake in my last PR when I was refactoring this. The attribute name that gets sent to Braze is `stackoverflow_user_id`, but this API endpoint exists for all sites and it returns the user ids for the site that the request hits, thus the field name should be `userId` instead of `stackOverflowUserId`.

I named it `userId` in my [original PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24922) when there were two endpoint, but then I messed it up with my last PR that refactored the two endpoints into a single endpoint.

body:
Updated the Braze SDK initialization to respect the user's OneTrust consent preferences for Targeting Cookies.

author: jacob-adams
body:
## Summary

This collapses the two original API endpoint into a single endpoint that can be called multiple times to get "pages" of results.

See the [original PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24922) for a description of what this is used for.

The main different with this implementation is that the request contains a date range and a maxResults field. The endpoint will only return `maxResults` items in the response. The endpoint can be called again by passing in the `updatedDate` from the last record in the prior response as the `startDate` in the new request.

## Testing

Here is a curl command that you can use locally to test this endpoint:

```
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://meta.stackexchange.local/api/customer-engagement/user-id?key=<simple-api-secret>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
	"startDate": "2025-07-29 16:11:30.120",
	"endDate": "2025-08-03 16:11:30.120",
	"maxResults": 10000
}'
```

## Summary

Article tags were appearing in weekly summary notifications, so the query was filtered to exclude article reserved tags.

## How to Test

1. *Steps to test*

I couldn't find a way to simulate the email, mainly because it would use customer data, but what I did was create several articles in my local environment and run the queries with the UserId -1 filter.

Query without filter shows knowledge-article tag
`SELECT TOP 1 t.Id, t.Name
FROM Tags t
WHERE t.Id IN (2)
    AND NOT EXISTS(
        SELECT 1
        FROM UserMappings um
        WHERE um.SubjectMatterExpertTagId = t.Id
            AND um.DeletionDate IS NULL
    )`

Query filtering the article tags (UserId -1 means reserved article tag)
`SELECT TOP 1 t.Id, t.Name
FROM Tags t
WHERE t.Id IN (2)
    AND t.UserId <> -1
    AND NOT EXISTS(
        SELECT 1
        FROM UserMappings um
        WHERE um.SubjectMatterExpertTagId = t.Id
            AND um.DeletionDate IS NULL
    )`

author: giamir
body:
**The `Edit Tag Wiki` page is used in both Internal and Pubplat. The migration affects both products.** 

## Summary

Migrates the Edit Tag Wiki page from the legacy WMD editor to the Stacks Editor to fix inaccessible toolbar controls. The WMD editor rendered toolbar buttons as `<li>` elements that were not reachable or operable via keyboard, violating WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard Only, Level A). The Stacks Editor has built-in keyboard-accessible toolbar controls.

## Related Issue

[A11Y-145](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/A11Y-145)

## Changes

- **`StackOverflow/Views/Tags/EditTagWiki.cshtml`**
  - Replaced WMD editor markup (`wmd-input`, `wmd-button-bar`, `wmd-preview`, `wmd.js` include) with Stacks Editor markup (`js-stacks-editor-content` backing textarea, `js-stacks-editor-container`, editor facade partial)
  - Removed explicit `tabindex` attributes (101, 102, 103, 109, 110, 111) from all form fields to allow natural DOM order keyboard navigation
  - Replaced synchronous `StackExchange.editor.initIfShown()` with async `StackExchange.using("externalEditor", ...)` + `StackExchange.prepareEditor()` for proper module loading
  - Moved `navPrevention.init()` inside `StackExchange.using("stacksEditor", ...)` callback where the module is guaranteed to be available, covering `#summary`, `#usage-guidance`, and `#js-stacks-editor-content`
  - Wired markdown preview to the site-level `StacksEditorPreviewEnabled` setting

## WCAG Criteria

**2.1.1 — Keyboard (Level A)**
All editor toolbar controls (Bold, Italic, Headings, Links, etc.) are now keyboard-accessible through the Stacks Editor's built-in toolbar, which uses proper `<button>` elements with ARIA attributes. All form fields follow natural DOM tab order without explicit tabindex overrides.

## Verification Steps

1. Navigate to any tag's "Edit Tag Wiki" page (e.g. `/edit-tag-wiki/1`)
2. Press Tab repeatedly — verify focus moves through: Summary → Usage Guidance → Editor toolbar buttons (Bold, Italic, etc.) → Editor content area → Edit Summary → Save Edits → Cancel
3. Verify toolbar buttons are operable: Tab to Bold, press Enter/Space — confirm it toggles bold formatting
4. Verify the editor content is editable: type markdown text, switch between Rich Text and Markdown modes
5. Make changes to Summary or Usage Guidance, then attempt to navigate away — verify the "unsaved changes" warning appears
6. Submit an edit and verify it saves correctly

## Screenshots / Before & After

**Before:** WMD editor with `<li>`-based toolbar buttons that are skipped by keyboard Tab navigation
**After:** Stacks Editor with `<button>`-based toolbar controls that are fully keyboard accessible and follow natural tab order

body:
# Summary

These API endpoints will be used by the Customer Engagement Service to backfill the `stackoverflow_user_id` attribute in Braze.

There are 2 endpoints:

- Discovery endpoint: Returns a list of account Ids for all Stack Overflow users that were created within the date range arguments in the request.
- Data Retrieval endpoint: Accepts a list of account ids and returns a list of account ids and user ids for the supplied account ids.

The reason there are two endpoints is so that proper batching can be done. The discovery endpoint returns a list of all account ids in the date range, and then the data retrieval endpoint will be called with a maximum of 1000 account ids to retrieve the data needed to do the backfill.

# Testing

Besides the automated tests that are included in the PR, I also ran this locally and verified that the endpoints return the expected data.

Here's some curl commands if you want to test locally:

Discovery endpoint:

```
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://meta.stackexchange.local/api/customer-engagement/user-id/discovery?key=<use-simple-secret>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
	"startDate": "2025-07-21 16:11:30.120",
	"endDate": "2025-08-30 16:11:30.120"
}'
```

Data Retrieval:

```
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://meta.stackexchange.local/api/customer-engagement/user-id?key=<use-simple-secret>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
	"accountIds": [27763852]
}'
```

author: giamir
body:
## Summary

The expandable section headings on the Tools page (`/tools?tab=stats`) are plain `<h3>` elements with only jQuery click handlers. Keyboard users cannot reach or activate the expand/collapse controls, failing WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A). This PR wraps each heading's content in a native `<button>` element following the WAI-ARIA Disclosure pattern, providing keyboard accessibility without custom key handlers.

## Related Issue

[A11Y-141](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/A11Y-141)

## Changes

- **`StackOverflow/Views/Tools/Index.cshtml`**
  - **HTML**: Wrapped each `<h3>` heading's content in a `<button type="button">` with `aria-expanded="false"` and `aria-controls` linking to the content panel. Added `id` attributes to content panels. Used `s-btn s-btn__unset` for unstyled button appearance.
  - **CSS**: Removed `cursor: pointer` from `.island .expander-arrow-small-hide` (now handled by the button's `c-pointer` utility class).
  - **JS click handler**: Changed delegated event selector from `"h3"` to `".island button[aria-expanded]"`. Added `aria-expanded` state toggle on each click.
  - **JS `loadNext`**: When a section has no collapsible rows, removes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` from the button so it's not announced as a toggle control. Removed the `h3` cursor pointer line.

## WCAG Criteria

**2.1.1 — Keyboard (Level A)**
All expand/collapse controls are now native `<button>` elements that are keyboard-focusable (Tab) and activatable (Enter/Space). `aria-expanded` communicates the current expanded/collapsed state to assistive technologies. `aria-controls` associates each button with its content panel.

## Verification Steps

1. Navigate to `/tools?tab=stats&daterange=last30days`
2. Tab through the page — each expandable section heading should receive visible keyboard focus
3. Press Enter or Space on a focused heading — the section should expand/collapse
4. Verify `aria-expanded` toggles between `"true"` and `"false"` in DevTools
5. Test with a screen reader (VoiceOver) — buttons should announce as e.g. "Highest score, collapsed, button"
6. Verify sections with no collapsible content do not announce as toggle buttons

body:
TEAMS-15319

## Summary

An API V3 endpoint, `/available`, that can be called to determine if the ingestion feature is available. It checks that ingestion is turned on, that the API is enabled, and that the user is within billing limits.

🤖 Some aspects of this are ai-assisted. Most notably the switch to using `Lazy` in the `AzureKeyVaultProvider`.

## How to Test

You can use [swagger](https://stackenterprise.local/api/v3/swagger/index.html) to hit the endpoint. 

Make sure your auth has write privileges. The entire ingestion feature set requires it. 

### Ingestion is available
1. Make sure ingestion is enabled locally in the [ingestion admin settings](https://stackenterprise.local/enterprise/ingestion/settings).
2. Hit the endpoint in swagger. It should return true.

### Ingestion is turned off
1. Disable ingestion with the switch found in the admin settings
2. Hit the endpoint in swagger. It should return false.

### Billing limits are reached
1. Reenable ingestion in the admin settings
2. Hit the endpoint in swagger. Make sure it returns true.
3. Billing limits are hard-coded to a very large number to disable them. You can change the code in the `GetPublishedPostLimit` method found in `IngestionBillingLimitsService.cs` to return 1. Make sure you have at least two published ingested posts from this month.
5. Hit the endpoint in swagger. It should return false.

author: threefjefff
body:
## Summary

When MS Teams starts up, it begins looping through a bunch of write-paths to send chat messages for AutoAnswer. In order to do this, it needs an access token, which is obtained through MSAL. Unfortunately, this can throw exceptions due to poor setup, and due to the fact the Client sets this up, we have no control over throwing a bunch of exceptions in a loop when credentials expire.

In `MicrosoftTeamsApi.GetAuthTokenAsync()` we already have defensive coding around this. AutoAnswer uses a mix of this api and `GraphApiService`, which did not.

This PR adds a `try/catch` for known MSAL exceptions, such that they're propogated to existing exception handling in the AutoAnswer queue
title: Add defensive coding around GraphApi token retrieval paths

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
We want to capture the user's top 10 watched tags in Braze. With this in mind, this PR emits an event each time that a tag is watched, ignored and cleared (unwatched, unignored).

**Why not emitting 3 product events instead (watched, ignored, cleared)?** 
Doing so, although more generic and reusable for other consumers of product events, it adds significant complexity on the Customer Engagement Service. We would need to:
- Keep state of the tags watched by the user
- Query the monolith via an api endoint to determine which 10 of the user's followed tags have the most questions. 

This approach has some implications:
- This is a very Customer Engagement product event, less reusable by other consumers.
- We'll emit it every time that a tag is watched, ignored or cleared. If the user already watches 10 very popular tags and starts watching an 11th one but less popular, the top 10 watched tags will still be the same, although the product event will still be emitted. This is not really a problem as consumer of events should be idempotent, and in our case, we'll just update the user attribute with the same array. 

**Why so many files changed?**
Async spread like a wildfire. None of the 3 methods `TagSetRow.Watch`, `TagSetRow.Ignore`, `TagSetRow.Clear` were async, and in order to be able to fire an internal event and later handle it in the `ProductEventsDispatch` class, I had to async-ify them. 

Don't worry though, the main changes are focused in a handful of files:
- `ProdcutEventsDispatch.cs`: Adds the internal handler that sends the new product event.
- `Events.cs`: Added 3 new internal events
- `TagSetRow.cs`: Sends internal events when a tag is watched, ignored or cleared. Adds a new method that returns the top 10 most popular tags for a user. Defines the new product event.
- `UserWatchedTagsEventsTests.cs`: Integration tests
title: PRODPLAT-106 Emit product event when top 10 watched tags change

author: nhu-van
body:
## Summary

Jira: TEAMS-15242

Changes to the duplication logic: 
- If a question is created not through the Ingestion APIs -> we will check duplication from all active and deleted posts
- If a question is created through the Ingestion APIs -> we will check duplication from active posts only (exclude deleted posts)

## How to Test
- Follow the instructions from this https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/23440 to set up Swagger UI and access Swagger endpoints on SOE.
- Access [Swagger UI](https://stackenterprise.local/api/v3/swagger/index.html)

**Testing duplication with a question created from SOE**
1. Create a question from the SOE site (not through API)
2. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - normal flow:</ins> Create another question from the SOE site that is duplicated with the question in step 1 -> You should receive a duplication error
3. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - ingestion flow:</ins> Send a request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint with the same body as the question in step 1 -> You should receive a duplication error
4. Delete the question in step 1
5. <ins>Testing duplication with deleted question - normal flow:</ins>: Create another question from the SOE site that is duplicated with the question in step 1 -> You should receive a duplication error
6. <ins>Testing duplication with deleted question - ingestion flow:</ins> Send a request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint with the same body as in step 1 ->  You should receive a success message.

**Testing duplication with a question created from ingestion APIs**
1. Send a request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint to create a new question -> You should receive a success message
2. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - normal flow:</ins> Create another question from the SOE site that is duplicated with the question in step 1 -> You should receive a duplication error
3. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - ingestion flow:</ins> Send another request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint with the same body as the question in step 1 -> You should receive a duplication error
5. Delete the question in step 1
6. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - normal flow:</ins> Create another question from the SOE site that is duplicated with the question in step 1 -> You should receive a duplication error
7. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - ingestion flow:</ins> Send a request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint with the same body as the question in step 1 -> You should receive a success message
8. Send a request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint to create a new question -> You should receive a success message
9. Publish the question in step 8
10. Delete the question in step 8
11. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - normal flow:</ins> Create another question from the SOE site that is duplicated with the question in step 8 -> You should receive a duplication error
12. <ins>Testing duplication with undeleted question - ingestion flow:</ins> Send a request to the `/ingest/question` endpoint with the same body as the question in step 8 -> You should receive a success message

author: aalear
body:
This PR adds support for allowing certain requests to simulate logged-in users based on a special cookie, without affecting real user sessions. 

This action is protected by a few gates:

- The required `__so-lt` cookie that carries info about what kind of a user we want to impersonate. Currently supported options are `random` and `skeet`. The former picks a random user with at least 1000 reputation, and the latter always picks Jon Skeet since there's a lot of data attached to his account.
- The required "beta access" cookie. Not to be confused with the SHINE beta, this cookie allows users to access "private beta" SE sites. The load-test environment is currently configured as a private beta, but this could work for any SE site if we need to test in other environments. The key point here is that this is cookie (currently called `rawr.dev2` in dev and test environments) must carry a value that the monolith knows how to validate.
- There's a tier check to prevent this code path from ever executing in production.

In the end, this allows us to set up k6 scripts to pass the beta access and the `__so-lt` cookies with each request so that we can exercise the internal API via the chrome service. This does _not_ make the monolith treat the user as logged in, so if/when we want to start load-testing user actions, we'll need to modify this to generate actual sessions.
title: PRODPLAT-396 Add support for generating a JWT for an arbitrary user in load tests

body:
The `_base-primary-unified-fragment.less` import chain pulls in v2 Stacks `body.less`, which sets `font-size: var(--fs-base)` on `html, body`. In FragmentLayout, the UI Composer injects v3 styles where the correct font-size is `var(--fs-body1)` (set on `body` only).

This PR overrides the v2 font-size to align with v3 behavior, and improves the comments to document why these overrides are needed (v2 vs v3 `body.less` differences).

### Changes
- Add `body { font-size: var(--fs-body1); }` override in `_base-primary-unified-fragment.less`
- Update comments to explain the v2/v3 stacks-dynamic discrepancy

This fix a bug where the font-size of the left navigation is 16px for legacy pages (e.g. question list) and 14px for new pages (e.g. question show).

author: giamir
body:
## Summary

In @stackoverflow/stacks@v3.0.0-beta.24 we [swapped](https://github.com/StackExchange/Stacks/pull/2172) all references to `--su-static*` sizing custom properties with `--su*` to better support user preferences and accessibility. This means that `--su-static*` were not present anymore in the v3 css bundle we served.

Now, we could have expected the [stacks-v2-scoped file](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/main/StackOverflow/Content/Shared/stacks-v2-scoped.less) to inject those variables for the legacy pages but unfortunately it did not. This is because the `--su-static*` variables are defined in stacks v2 under the `body` selector ([see source code](https://github.com/StackExchange/Stacks/blob/develop/packages/stacks-classic/lib/atomic/spacing.less)) and there is no `body` scoped under our @scope `stacks-v2-start`.

There are though plenty of v2 stacks classes relying on those static variables being exposed which resulted on completely messing up the legacy pages in the beta site. [See thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C097YESGSMB/p1770317888146239)

The solution is to expose those variables again at the scope level (not under the `body` selector) in the stacks-v2-scoped file. This is what this PR does. 

I have tested it locally with a version of the UI composer using the latest stacks.css and things restarted to look good again. Once this PR is merged we can unpin the version of stacks in the UI composer (or at least upgrade the pinned version to the latest).
title: fix(shine): add patches for old static spacing units

body:

[YETI2-918](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-918): default date logic

## Summary

This PR updates 2 things:
1. Updating error message for DL plan upgrade
  - The detail field in problem details cannot have a clickable link. We can add a custom field for support email but not sure if that will add much value.
2. Move default date logic from controller to service layer for the `/questions` and `/content-feeds/comments` endpoints

## How to Test
#### Set up
1. Enable [time based pagination site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled)
2. If not set, set the [max day range window for **questions** site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxDayRangeWindowForQuestions) to 30
3. If not set, set the [max day range window for **comments** site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxDayRangeWindowForComments) to 7

#### Without date filters
1. Using Postman, set `Automatically follow redirects` is off
2. Make a request to the `/questions` endpoint without date filters > you will get a 302 response
3. . Set `Automatically follow redirects` is on
4. Make a request to the `/questions` endpoint without date filters > you will get redirected and get a 200 response with default dates set based on the max day range set above. You probably won't see any results because there's new data
5. Repeat the steps above (1-4) with the `/content-feeds/comments` endpoint without date filters

#### Different date filters
1. Leave `Automatically follow redirects` to on
2. Make a request to endpoints with **valid** date filters
   * `creationFrom=12/25/20&creationTo=1/21/21` > get a 200 for `/questions` endpoint
   * `creationFrom=1/1/21&creationTo=1/6/21` > get a 200 for `/content-feeds/comments` endpoint
3. Make a request to endpoints with **invalid** date filters:
   * `creationFrom=1/1/28&creationTo=1/1/400` > get a 400 with error  message "'From' date cannot be in the future."
   * `creationFrom=1/1/2030&creationTo=1/1/2028` > get a 400 with error  message "'From' date cannot be in the future."
   * `creationFrom=1/15/2026&creationTo=1/1/2028` > get a 400 with error message "'From' and 'To' are required parameters. The date range between 'From' and 'To' must not exceed 30 days."
   * missing `creationFrom` or `creationTo` > 400 with error "'From' and 'To' are required parameters. The date range between 'From' and 'To' must not exceed 30 days."

#### DL plan error message
1. With your DL basic app, make a request to an endpoint that basic tier (so all DL) has access to> should return a 200
2. Make a request to premium-only endpoint (discussions and changes endpoints) > should get an error message "_This endpoint is not a part of your plan, please reach out to api-support@stackoverflow.com for more information._"
3. With your DL premium app, make the same request from step 2 > should return a 200

author: threefjefff
body:
## Overview

Adds support for the `offline_access` grant, which issues a Refresh Token that is redeemable without user intervention to claim an Access Token for up to 30 days after the initial issuance.

This works across all product tiers:
- In Public and Enterprise, the refresh tokens are stored in the Sites DB. They are unadorned at rest and carry a `refresh_` prefix for ease of distinction in transit.
- In FBB, refresh tokens are given channel marks identically to Access Codes. 
    - These encode the channel number and a HMAC in the token such that the outer site can proxy to the correct Channels instance.
    - They are stored in the `Teams.Channels` database, alongside Tokens and Codes.

If an access token is claimed with a client secret, the refresh token must be redeemed with a client secret. The code verification steps for PKCE are intentially a one-shot pass, and cannot be reused in this way, and equally the redemption of refresh tokens is prescribed as a single call.

All refresh tokens are redeemable once. If someone attempts to redeem the refresh token a second time, all refresh tokens associated with the user login session are invalidated, and a new Authorization Code flow will have to be started with user intervention. 

This is in line with [RFC recommendations](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13#section-4.3.1-10.2.1) for issuing refresh tokens to public clients.

## Test

### Public
- Initiate an Auth Code exchange with the `offline_access` scope.
```
https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth
?client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/login_success
&scope=offline_access
&state=lol
&code_challenge=oNH5nU7TKfJhjmQrVd8iUFaafq6fggrTHcZD_FlZILw
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Grab the Code from the response URL
- Exchange the code for a token, ensuring you get a `refresh_token`
```
POST https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmeta.stackexchange.local%2Foauth%2Flogin_success
&code=<CODE_GOES_HERE>
&code_verifier=M5hBOxU0Pxve7ffvo776cANLWqDYuamoltpFfTWZV-RDET8I0akJxxKz7zormRTUelg4bFHMHEETpGJ05Tte8A
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Exchange the refresh token for a token, ensuring you get both a token and refresh token
```
POST https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&refresh_token=<REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE>
&grant_type=refresh_token
```
- Ensure your new access token works, that both the access token and refresh token are different from the original.

### FBB
- Initiate an Auth Code exchange with the `offline_access` scope and the `access_team` scope.
```
https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth
?client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/login_success
&scope=offline_access access_team
&state=lol
&code_challenge=oNH5nU7TKfJhjmQrVd8iUFaafq6fggrTHcZD_FlZILw
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Grab the Code from the response URL
- Exchange the code for a token, ensuring you get a `refresh_token`
```
POST https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&redirect_uri=https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/login_success
&code=<CODE_GOES_HERE>
&code_verifier=M5hBOxU0Pxve7ffvo776cANLWqDYuamoltpFfTWZV-RDET8I0akJxxKz7zormRTUelg4bFHMHEETpGJ05Tte8A
&code_challenge_method=s256
```
- Exchange the refresh token for a token, ensuring you get both a token and refresh token
```
POST https://stackoverflowteams.local/oauth/access_token/json
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

client_id=2
&refresh_token=<REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE>
&grant_type=refresh_token
```
- Ensure your new access token works for your selected team (but not another team), that both the access token and refresh token are different from the original.
title: Add the Refresh Token flow to Auth Token endpoint

author: stephen-vakil
body: ## Summary We are seeing occasional performance blips in the Internal API in beta prod. This adds some trace steps to various parts of the internal API so that they will show up in datadog, hopefully allowing us to see exactly where it occasionally blips. Traces added to: - The current context methods that look up site and user - The JWT auth validation methods - Site Chrome services that interact with the monolith # Datadog Version bug fix This also fixes an issue with datadog tracer mismatches. The base layer in our Dockerfile was installing version 2.45 of the agent. Our nuget package was version 3.16. The mismatch meant that traces were going missing. The traces I added were not showing up at all in fact. Once I fixed the version mismatch, not only do those traces show up, but a lot of other trace spans are now present. Checking the history, it looks like the package [was updated in this PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/22701), which did make an attempt to align the package version to 3.16 in both places. Unfortunately, it made the assumption that the docker layer describing datadog installation was what was used in the rest of the layers. That wasn't the case. In fact, that whole layer was removed because it was unnecessary in [this PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24480). So it looks like we've has mismatched versions since May of 2025 and possibly/likely haven't had full trace information during that time. ## How to Test 1. Poke around on ascn-dev beta as a logged-in user 2. View traces in datadog for ascn-dev chrome-service and verify that new internal API spans show up
title: KRAKEN-2812:  Add tracing to Internal API

author: aalear
body:
The monolith does a lot of "internal IP" checks and currently none of the requests from the UI Composer are coming across as internal, which means nothing will work at all once we're no longer the only ones visiting the beta site via Zscaler that routes through a proper "internal IP". The core of the issue is that the monolith determines the client's IP address from the X-Forwarded-For header.

This PR strips `X-Forwarded-For` from UI Composer requests to `/oauth/token` since we're unable to remove the header when the requests are being issued. Hopefully as we move away from nginx, the token exchange bits will move into the UI Composer itself and this will no longer be necessary.

Additionally, any routes required by the UI Composer to render the site must not use internal IP checks. The best we can do at the moment is checking whether the `X-UIComposer-Request` header is present.

See also: https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.UIComposer/pull/100
title: PRODPLAT-381 Strip X-Forwarded-For from UI Composer auth requests

author: threefjefff
body:
## Summary
This is some ground-laying work to make the inclusion of a `grant_type` easier. Functionally, OAuth defines two major endpoints (`Authorization` and `Token`) and prescribes various ways of ushering us through them.:
- `Authorization Code flow` - Well, that's what was already here.
- `Client Credentials flow` - would just be a call to the token endpoint with the right grant type specified
- `Refresh token flow` - is a call to the token endpoint, reidentifying yourself (if required) alongside your refresh token
- even the `Implict` flow was a means of requesting a token response from the `Authorize`  endpoint

Long story short, we've been overcomplicating this for a while, and as we have a need to add a `grant_type` (in order to enable `refresh_token` flow) this is in place to cut down the noise before adding more complexity.

- Renaming the Authorization and Token endpoint handlers to succumb to industry standard nomenclature (we don't even _use_ `implict` flow any more, and `explict` was never the name of the other kind of flow!)
- Simplifying the form data/json endpoints such that they share an implemntation, and hand off interpreting the response to a respective handler.

## How to Test

Log in.

Tested by unit/integration tests
title: Auth - Rename Authorization and Token endpoints to convention, simplify paths

author: qheaden-stack
body:
MOD-432 MOD-487 | [Slack Thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C097YESGSMB/p1769002961751469)

## Summary

The `Site.Url()` method returns the URL to the current SE site. For Shine beta, this will be `beta.stackoverflow.com`. But this link changes depending on if you are on the beta site or not. This can result in the monolith still generating `stackoverflow.com` for a link even if you are on beta which can take the user off the beta site at best or break AJAX calls at worst.

This PR updates the `Site.Url()` method (both the base and fragment overloads) with a new flag named `allowBetaConversion`. If this flag is set to true, and the user is accessing the monolith through the UI composer (used for the beta site), it will use `Site.TryGetShineBetaUrl` to convert the URL to the beta version.

The `allowBetaConversion` flag is defaulted to `true` since we ideally want this conversion to always happen when coming through the UI composer. The `Current.Site.Url()` method is called in a lot of places, so we keep the flag for now in the case there is a spot we want to disable this conversion.

## How to Test

### Testing for [MOD-432](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/MOD-432) (Challenges breadcrumb link)

**NOTE:** This involves testing challenges. To enable challenges, first ensure discussions are enabled (should be enabled by default), then set the site setting `Discussions.CodingChallengeMinPostId` to `0`. After this, you should see "Discussions" in the left sidebar turn to "Challenges", and you can create a challenge.

1) Create a new challenge
2) View the challenge detail page and hover over the first breadcrumb with the Stack Overflow logo
3) Ensure the breadcrumb points to `meta.stackoverflow.local` when viewing the monolith directly and `localhost:7205` when viewing through the UI composer

### Testing for [MOD-487](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/MOD-487) (Profile all actions expand button gives error)

1) Visit a user's Profile > All actions page
2) Click one of the expand buttons next to an activity detail
3) Ensure the info loads and doesn't give any request errors

[MOD-432]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/MOD-432?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: alexwarren
body:
The copy button on code blocks was generating incorrect attribution URLs for anonymous users. The URL would show "/q" instead of "/q/postId" because the code always stripped the last URL segment, assuming it was a user ID.

For logged-in users, share links include a user ID (/q/postId/userId), so stripping the last segment correctly removes the user ID. For anonymous users, share links only have the post ID (/q/postId), so stripping the last segment incorrectly removed the post ID itself.

Fixed by only removing the last segment when there are 3+ segments present, indicating a user ID exists. Added tests for both logged-in and anonymous user scenarios.
title: DISCOCD-330: Fix code block copy attribution URL for anonymous users

body:
Our attempts to repeat the load tests we created during Ascension against the `load-test` environment were crashing all SO pods at fairly low traffic levels. Looking at the APM traces from one of the test runs on this [DD dashboard](https://us3.datadoghq.com/dashboard/ghg-the-nha/load-testing-pub-plat-in-gcp?fromUser=false&refresh_mode=paused&tpl_var_cluster_name%5B0%5D=gke-pubplat-load-test-uc1-a&tpl_var_host%5B0%5D=load-test.stackoverflow.dev&tpl_var_service%5B0%5D=stackoverflow&from_ts=1769460540000&to_ts=1769460900000&live=false), I noticed that we're running this query multiple times per question page, once per answer on the page (plus the question itself):

```
SELECT ContentType
FROM OpinionBasedContent
WHERE PostId = @Id
```

This query comes from the `OpinionBasedContentType` property on the post. Once accessed, the value is memoized, but this can definitely add up on questions with larger answer counts. This PR loads and sets content type when the answers are fetched in the first place.

This PR was deployed to `load-test` (will be overridden by the daily deployment in about 10 minutes though) and here are the stress test results. ## Summary

This PR adds the interesting question list to the beta homepage for both anonymous and logged in users. It also includes a modification to the interesting question algorithm that boosts questions with popular tags for anonymous users. This behavior is controlled via an optional parameter to avoid modifying behavior on the older `?tab=interesting` view.

This new interesting question list does not contain staging ground questions nor quick answer badges. Styling for those would need to be factored into Stacks Svelte. 

### Notes on Interesting Questions
- The behavior for prioritizing popular tags is controlled via an optional parameter that defaults to false to avoid modifying behavior on the older `?tab=interesting` view
- The behavior can be turned on/off with a site setting for the beta homepage
- The result is cached for 5 minutes 
- There is no caching for logged in users
- Any tags that contain a popular tag will be boosted (popular tag `c#` will also boost `c#-4.0`)

**Logged In**

**Anonymous**

2. Visit `https://meta.stackexchange.local/?tab=interesting`
3. Visit the homepage from the UI composer `https://localhost:7205/`
4. Validate that the lists are the same (this is true as long as the interesting algorithm doesn't run a second time since it introduces some randomness, however the top results should be the same)

body:
Jira: [YETI2-914](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-914?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYzYzZmY2ODI1NDFkNGE0OGEzMzc5NWQzMjQ1NDhkNTUiLCJwIjoiaiJ9)

## Summary

This PR contains changes for date filter validation. I cherry picked commits from #24716 to make the scope smaller because moving the date logic from the controller to the service layer might need additional testing on a mac. 

## How to Test

#### Set up
1. Enable [time based pagination site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_Enabled)
2. If not set, set the [max day range window for **questions** site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxDayRangeWindowForQuestions) to 30
2. If not set, set the [max day range window for **comments** site setting](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Api.APIv3_TimeBasedPagination_MaxDayRangeWindowForComments) to 7

#### Without date filters
1. Using Postman, set `Automatically follow redirects` is off
2. Make a request to the `/questions` endpoint without date filters > you will get a 302 response
3. Set `Automatically follow redirects` is on
4. Make a request to the `/questions` endpoint without date filters > you will get redirected and get a 200 response with default dates set based on the max day range set above. You probably won't see any results because there's new data
5. Repeat the steps above (1-4) with the `/content-feeds/comments` endpoint without date filters

#### Different date filters
1. Leave `Automatically follow redirects` to on
2. Make a request to endpoints with **valid** date filters
   * `creationFrom=12/25/20&creationTo=1/21/21` > get a 200 for `/questions` endpoint
   * `creationFrom=1/1/21&creationTo=1/6/21` > get a 200 for `/content-feeds/comments` endpoint
3. Make a request to endpoints with **invalid** date filters:
   * `creationFrom=1/1/28&creationTo=1/1/400` > get a 400 with error  message "'From' date cannot be in the future."
   * `creationFrom=1/1/2030&creationTo=1/1/2028` > get a 400 with error  message "'From' date cannot be in the future."
   * `creationFrom=1/15/2026&creationTo=1/1/2028` > get a 400 with error message "'From' and 'To' are required parameters. The date range between 'From' and 'To' must not exceed 30 days."
   * missing `creationFrom` or `creationTo` > 400 with error "'From' and 'To' are required parameters. The date range between 'From' and 'To' must not exceed 30 days."

author: qheaden-stack
body:
## Summary

Currently, when on the Shine beta site, if an action triggers a flash message to show on page refresh, the flash message will continue to pop up after every refresh or page navigation. It is expected that after seeing it once, it will go away after clicking it off, refreshing the page, or navigating to another page.

Flash message works by the server setting a cookie named `flash-message-json` with JSON data describing the flash message content and style. This is done in C# with a call to the `SetFlashMessage` method. On the client side in JS, once the flash message is shown, it uses the jQuery cookie plugin to remove the `flash-mesasge-json` cookie which prevents the message from showing again.

The JS code that removes the cookie scopes the removal to a domain retrieved from `document.domain`. This gives the domain of the current page as seen in the browser's address bar. With Shine, the UI Composer proxies most page requests to the monolith. The monolith sets cookies on the domain defined in JS by `StackExchange.options.site.cookieDomain`. In the local and beta environments, this URL is different for the UI composer entry and the monolith, so the code to remove the `flash-message-json` cookie doesn't work since the cookie is defined for a different domain.

This code adds a second cookie removal using `StackExchange.options.site.cookieDomain` as the domain. You might ask why we don't just remove using that value and not use `document.domain` at all. The reason for keeping the `document.domain` removal is that with the current UI Composer code, when running it locally, it is set up to rewrite cookies to the `localhost` domain. So while using `StackExchange.options.site.cookieDomain` would work in dev and production, it wouldn't work locally.

## How to Test

(This can work with anything that uses a flash message, but I had originally discovered the bug by leaving a collective)

1. Impersonate a user
2. Join a collective
3. Leave the collective and then notice the flash message
4. Refresh the page or navigate to another page and ensure the flash message no longer shows
title: [MOD-462] Fix broken flash message dismissal

author: franciscodua
body:
# Summary

Some Enterprise customers are having problems with Enhanced search. And the problem seems related to a cancellation token being cancelled during the process of getting an answer/summary.
While investigating the problem, I found a cancellation token being reused to send events, and this token could've been cancelled before the event was sent. This could cause the error those customers are seeing.
This only happens if the `MapReduceService` gets an answer from the search results. That's why it only happens at times, even for the same query.

## Notes

I added a new cancellation token to that method and I'm using it for calls that receive one. I did this to avoid the reuse of that wrong token again. Rider advises me to add a new cancellation token to that send method, and the automated fix is to add the wrong token again. It detects an available cancellation token and assumes that's the right token to use. That's probably how this problem came to be.

# How to Test

To reproduce the problem I ended up having to go through a lot of steps (not all were needed in the end). I'll list them here for documentation purposes:
1. Add a connection string to `environmentsettings.Local.Enterprise.json` under `AzureEventHubs.Hubs.ConnectionString` (there are 2). Value: `ref+azurekeyvault://so-local-kv-xhb9/evh-dev-pubplat-connection-string`
2. Build StackOverflow in `DebugEnterprise` mode
3. Add a question to your instance that is very easy to answer, e.g., who's Ferret's tech lead?
4. Add an answer to that question that is clearly the right answer (the clearer it is, the more likely the LLM will assume it's the right answer outright).
5. On the product's search bar, ask that same question, e.g., who's Ferret's tech lead?

By the end of these steps, you should see results, or an error (if you're on main). But sometimes you might still see an answer. This is because sometimes the LLM doesn't give you the answer immediately based on the content you have. To make sure you can place a breakpoint here https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/12396c6353e4b15fa6b6a077fd735b381222e6e8/src/StackOverflow.Module.AiEnhancedSearch/Services/AiEnhancedSearchService.cs#L139 to make sure you're going through the step that caused the problem before.
title: FERRET-1176 Fix enhanced search early cancellation

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
When we moved to the cell architecture, we started seeing failed deployments due to timeouts due to concurrent deployments spiking in CPU usage and overwhelming the nodes. This was because the requests and limits were quite far apart, but we didn’t want to reserve more capacity for the whole lifetime of the pods just due to the startup spike. 

The Startup CPU Boost is a custom resource that allows us to temporarily increase the requests until the app starts up, and then drop to the normal request.

This ended up not working as well as we expected due to node pool instability (scaled up and down lots of times). 

We disabled it via the feature flag, but we still have code in the helm charts and CNAB deployments that references to it. This PR deletes that usage.
title: PRODPLAT-280 Cleanup startup cpu boost usage from SOE deployments

NPM 11 introduces a new peer resolution system that adds a bunch of `"peer": true` properties in the package-lock.json file and these changes have been committed to the repo in #24662. This PR requires Node.js 24 LTS / NPM 11 or above to avoid this package-lock.json flapping behaviour.

author: animuson
body:
## Summary

Jira: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-15168

Fixes:

- `itemsPerPage` returned in GET calls will be the number of items in the resource response, _not_ the expected maximum number of items, in compliance with the (confusing) SCIM specs.

Adds:

- New site settings for `UpdateDisplayNameFromSCIM`, `UpdateRealNameFromSCIM`, and `UpdateVerifiedEmailFromSCIM`, all set to off by default with verified email being a hidden site setting.
- New site setting for `UpdateRealNameFromIdPUponLogin` set to on by default, for consistency with the other site settings, preserving existing behavior.
- Allows updating display name, real name, and verified email from SCIM PUT and PATCH calls if the relevant site setting for that property is enabled (otherwise does nothing).
- Additional tests for PUT calls to account for these three extra pieces of info.

While Okta only requested being able to update DisplayName, we already had code set up to do all three and it made sense to implement all three in one go, rather than doing one and potentially having to add the other two later. Due to the potential risk associated with updating verified email in this way, we opted to keep that setting hidden from admins, and they won't be able to update it without talking to Product Support and getting a hidden site setting link.

## How to Test

Send a GET call and ensure that `itemsPerPage` matches the number of users returned in the response (can use `?startIndex=` to force a lower number of users to return at the end).

Other functionality has integration tests to cover it, but you're welcome to send PATCH/PUT calls to update other values.
title: TEAMS-15168: Okta SCIM fixes
