author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
Build upon https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24702

For work on Amplitude events for Knowledge Ingestion we are going to introduce two new properties on all post related events (see [here](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C0A3ZC7A9P1/p1768228831038799)):

**creation_method** :point_right: How was it made?
    Values: `manual`, `ai_generated`, `ai_augmented`
    Goal: High-level breakdown of human vs. AI contribution.

**creation_source** :point_right:  Where did it come from?
    Values: `native`, `confluence`, `github`, `jira`, `slack`, `ms_teams` etc etc
    Goal: Identify which integrations are driving the most content.

The problem currently is that the inheritance structure of domain events in the monolith doesn't allow us to simply pick a base "post" event and slap those properties on there.

This PR introduces a better base class for post related events.

The challenge here is that some of these events use `post_id` as a property, others `PostId` and yet others have `QuestionId` / `question_id` or `AnswerId`. PRIZM and Amplitude already have event data with these property names so we cannot change those (not easily anyway).

I've used Claude code to find events related to posts and introduce two new base types. This PR is the result of that
title: TEAMS-15171: Common post base event

author: aalear
body:
I originally added this exception with the intent to be more descriptive than a null ref or similar being thrown further downstream, but this is causing problems for routes that don't actually require a site at all (e.g. health checks). This ends up being very spammy in the exception logs due to the `PerformHttpsRedirects` step in the request pipeline that attempts to load `Current.Site` (and handles a null ref there gracefully) to check HTTPS settings.

```
System.InvalidOperationException: No site id found in either the JWT token or the header.
   at StackOverflow.Api.Internal.ApiInternalCurrentContext.get_Site() in /app/StackOverflow.Api.Internal/InternalCurrentContextProvider.cs:line 41
   at StackOverflow.Helpers.RequestUtil.PerformHttpsRedirectsAsync(HttpContext context, Func<T> next) in /app/StackOverflow.Common/Helpers/RequestUtil.cs:line 94

Full Trace:

   at StackOverflow.Helpers.RequestUtil.PerformHttpsRedirectsAsync(HttpContext context, Func<T> next) in /app/StackOverflow.Common/Helpers/RequestUtil.cs:line 94
```

So this PR adjusts the Internal API `Current` context provider to only throw if an attempt to provide a header was made and ignore it otherwise. The auth and `SiteId` middleware should otherwise check the most common failure cases with reasonably descriptive errors.
title: PRODPLAT-295: (InternalAPI) Only throw if the X-Site-Id header has an invalid value

author: DavidSnoble
body: ## Summary https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-15162 This PR introduces a "For You" notification system for the Ingestion review queue. When users have 5 or more ingested posts awaiting review in tags where they are Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) or tag watchers, they receive a notification in their For You feed. The notification displays the total post count and up to 3 relevant tag names, with a direct link to the ingestion review queue. To prevent notification fatigue, the system enforces rate limiting by only notifying users once per week if they don't have an existing unread notification from the past 7 days. The implementation includes a new scheduled task (ForYouNotificationIngestion) that runs the notification logic, a repository layer for querying users with posts needing review, and integration with the existing UserFeedItem notification system using a new InboxType (ID 126). The feature respects ingestion privileges and only notifies users who have access to the review queue. Supporting changes include refactoring the IsIngestionAvailable helper method in Feature.cs for better reusability, adding comprehensive unit and integration tests, and updating the front-end to render the new notification type with appropriate icon and formatting ## How to Test Please run your database migrations in dev local setup 1. To test create at least 5 q&a pairs with the same tag via the ingestion question and answer pair endpoint https://stackenterprise.local/api/v3/swagger/index.html 2. Login in as TestEngAdmin and Sync the review queue items with this developer route here https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/sync-ingestion-review-tasks 3. Make youself a SME on the tag or watch the tag for the posts you added in the ingestion queue 4. run this route to create the notification https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/ingestion-for-you 5. This PR adds the watched/ignored tags modal that appears when a user clicks on the "Customize your feed" link. It is only visible to logged in users.

The code for this modal is mostly a copy of the existing watched tags modal (Svelte island) on Stack Overflow with a few stylistic differences. We must ensure that the existing modal remains the same. 

I believe a client-side rendered Svelte island is acceptable for this modal since the modal does not need to be immediately available as it is not visible on page load. It is also fairly interactive.

## How to Test
#### **`ascn-dev` - New Modal**
1. Visit https://ascn-dev.stackoverflow.dev/ and login, then visit https://beta.ascn-dev.stackoverflow.dev/ and you should be logged in
2. Click the "Customize your feed" link top open the modal, upon opening a "/stackevent" should be sent with a `tagLocation` value of 12
3. Add a tag under "Watched", verify the tag was added and that a "/stackevent" was sent
4. Remove a tag under "Watched", verify the tag was removed and that a "/stackevent" was sent
5. Repeat steps 3 and 4 from the "Ignored" tab
6. Move a tag from "Ignored" to "Watched" and vice versa (from "Watched" to "Ignored") by selecting a tag that is already listed in the other tab, verify the tag is removed from the other tab and added to the selected tab
7. On modal close, if there were changed the page will be reloaded. Verify that all changes to watched/ignored tags were applied
8. Reopen the modal and close it, do not make any changes. Confirm that the page does not reload.

#### **Local - New Modal**
The styling is not quite right when running this through the UI Composer/monolith due to conflicting Stacks v2 and v3 styles. See the section below for how to better test for design.
1. Setup the UI Composer and it's dependent services locally
4. Open Developer tools and go to the "Network" tab

7. Remove a tag under "Watched", verify the tag was removed and that a "/stackevent" was sent
8. Repeat steps 4 and 5 from the "Ignored" tab
9. Move a tag from "Ignored" to "Watched" and vice versa (from "Watched" to "Ignored") by selecting a tag that is already listed in the other tab, verify the tag is removed from the other tab and added to the selected tab
10. On modal close, if there were changed the page will be reloaded. Verify that all changes to watched/ignored tags were applied
11. Reopen the modal and close it, do not make any changes. Confirm that the page does not reload.

#### **Styling**

2. Run `npm run standalone -w watched-tags-modal` to see Stacks v3 styling

## Summary

Currently in the monolith, when a user clicks the achievement button in the topbar, it loads achievements and then [marks them all as read](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/26dbf8842cf4e2084dbfdab633c9d0ecafe10877/StackOverflow/Controllers/TopBar/TopBarController.cs#L402) before returning the data to the browser. 6. Reload the page, and verify that the topbar counts for achievements are still the same
7. Use the internal API Swagger to test the `/achievements/{id}/read` route 
8. Reload the page in ui-composer and verify the topbar no longer shows anything new

When called in the context of a loaded site, which StackAuth does, we need this check to work on the instance of the loaded site and not the current site, which would be StackAuth, and so it was giving strange behaviour when handling the third party logins.

Weirdly, the third party login worked locally before this change which makes no sense.

---------------------------------------------------

body:
Jira: [YETI2-907](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-907?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWJmNmFhMWNiYWFiNDA3YTliNWNkNTBkYzhiZTMxMGQiLCJwIjoiaiJ9)

## Summary
This PR updates `TryGetSiteFromUrl` logic in `StackOverflow.Api.V3.Common/SiteContextProvider.cs` to correctly get the site name in DL API. This allows `GetSiteByApiName` method to use the correct site name to validate instead of defaulting to the main site. If the site name does not exist, the request now returns a 404 with the error message "site does not exist".

In PubPlat API V3, `TryGetSiteFromUrl` worked because `Request.Path` started with the site prefix `/sites/`. However, DL API path includes a version prefix (/v1/), causing the method to return null for `siteName`. This resulted in all requests falling back to the main site, regardless of the site name provided.

There are multiple ways to resolve the issue in DL API and after discussing with Doug, what I decided on is extracting the site name by locating where the site prefix (`/sites/`) and the next ending slash (i.e. slash that ends the site name segment). This means we can ignore whatever comes in front of the site prefix like the version.

## How to Test

Before
1. Either on dev or local (main branch), make requests to DL API using valid site value (like meta.stackexchange.local, literature.stackexchange.local)
2. Make requests to DL API using invalid site values > no errors for invalid site & you will get results for the main site
3. Add a breakpoint where `TryGetSiteFromUrl` method is in `C:\Code\StackOverflow\StackOverflow.Api.V3.Common\SiteContextProvider.cs` and step through the code. Notice what Request.Path looks like.
4. You could also test how it works in PubPlat API v3 to see the `Request.Path` pattern there.

After
1. Checkout this feature branch `llee/YETI2-907-dl-api-site-validation`
2. Make requests to DL API using valid site value
3. Make requests to DL API using invalid site values > get a 404 with an error message "site does not exist"
4. Check the method `TryGetSiteFromUrl` by adding a breakpoint

DL Docs site
  * Make sure you can still log in

author: aalear
body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up PR to #24645 and #24669, fixing additional issues with the `RequireSiteIdHeaderForAnonymousRequests` middleware blocking routes that should be accessible without the X-Site-Id header:

1. Health check endpoints blocked - Kubernetes liveness (/health-checks/live) and readiness (/health-checks/ready) probes were being rejected with 400 Bad Request when the middleware couldn't find the X-Site-Id header, causing pod health check failures.
2. Swagger UI showing X-Site-Id for all endpoints - the header was displayed in Swagger documentation even for endpoints that require authorization (where the header is not needed since the user is authenticated).

This PR standardizes on an array-based approach to checking specific route names (Swagger, health checks) and adds a `SiteIdNotRequired` attribute to allow ad-hoc exemption of additional routes or controllers.

Swagger documentation should now only be showing the header field for routes that allow anonymous access and aren't marked with `[SiteIdNotRequired]`.

## Testing

Added automated tests for the new attribute and path-based exemptions and also tested the deployment manually in `ascn-dev`.
title: Internal API: exclude health checks from SiteId middleware [PRODPLAT-295]

body:
## Summary

**Note:** This does not include Stacks v3 styling yet! That can be added after https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24658 is merged. The goal of this PR is to create the new homepage so that we can start adding our components to it.

-------

This PR adds a new view for the homepage that will be served from the new beta site. We must retain the existing homepage behavior for Stack Overflow and other SE sites.

The new site setting `BetaHomepage.ShowFor` acts as an emergency measure should we need to rollback to the previous experience.

We have a couple of site settings that control home page behavior for SE sites:
1. [Home.NewHomepage.ShowNewHomepageFor](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.NewHomepage.ShowNewHomepageFor) Stack Overflow is the only site that appears to have this site setting enabled. Anonymous users are redirected to `/questions`. This homepage is behind a `PeopleSelector` site setting and could technically be enabled on any site.
2. When the site setting above is off, the default behavior is to serve a question list. The list between logged in users and anonymous user differs slightly. The anonymous user's list appears to be made out of popular tags while the logged in users one highlights post that contain a tag from your watched list. 

I have added integration tests to verify existing behavior and the new UI Composer enabled behavior. 

## How to Test
### SHINE
1. Setup the UI Composer and it's dependent services locally
2. Set https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.BetaHomepage.ShowFor is set to "All" 
3. Visit the home page at https://localhost:7205/ as an anonymous user, you should see an AI assist text box and the text "Trending Posts"
4. Visit the main site at https://meta.stackexchange.local as an anonymous user and you should see a different view than the one from the UI Composer
5. Visit the home page at https://localhost:7205/ as a logged in user, you should see an AI assist text box and the text "Interesting Posts for You"
6. Visit the main site at https://meta.stackexchange.local as a logged in user and you should see a different view than the one from the UI Composer

### SHINE Fallback
In the event, that we need to revert back to the old experience
1. Set https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.BetaHomepage.ShowFor to "0"
   - "All" is the code default for local and dev environments
2. Set https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.NewHomepage.ShowNewHomepageFor to "All"
3. Visit the home page at https://localhost:7205/ as an anonymous user, you should be redirected to `/questions`
4. Visit the home page at https://localhost:7205/ as a logged in user, you should see the existing homepage (similar to Stack Overflow)

### Existing Behavior
1. Set https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.ShowAnonProductPage to "false"
2. Set https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.NewHomepage.ShowNewHomepageFor to "All"
3. Visit the homepage as an anonymous user and you should be redirected to `/questions`
4. Visit the homepage as a logged in user and you should see the existing homepage (similar to Stack Overflow)
7. Set https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Home.NewHomepage.ShowNewHomepageFor to 0
   - The code default is `Employees` but were trying to hide it from everyone
8. Visit the homepage as an anonymous user and you should see a question list
9. Visit the homepage as a logged in user and you should see a question list

---------------------------------------------------

## Summary

Pulls through a relative time string from the server, which will be based on the requesting user's timezone.

## How to Test

*n.b. this won't actually work locally: I believe that's because running the local server means its time is set to your machine's system time. Whereas our deployed servers should(?!) all be running in UTC, so the relative stuff should just work. So check in the PR env!

1. Site setting etc
2. Find/create OBC, including replies
3. Edit a reply
4. Check that the modified string shows, and says some amount of seconds ago (i.e. not '4 hours ago')
5. Check that stuff which isn't modified still shows the posted date & looks OK
6. Change your system time to spoof a different timezone
7. Repeat step 4

This PR lets StackOverflow be built with a newer major version of Node.js. It now supports Node.js >= 20 instead of == 20, so that the solution continues to build while DevLocalSetup is updated to install Node.js 24 LTS.

I had to disable one of the `QuickSearch.test.ts` tests "should render results" because the `waitFor` call inside it consistently fails with Node.js 24 and I couldn't figure out why. Here's a Slack thread with further context and input from folks: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C04EFFRL6G0/p1768483712505809

This PR needs to be merged before https://github.com/StackEng/DevLocalSetup/pull/423 is merged.

# Testing

1. Check out https://github.com/StackEng/DevLocalSetup/pull/423
2. Upgrade Node.js using that branch
3. Verify local Node.js is v24 by doing `node --version`
4. Build and run the StackOverflow solution (`dotnet build` in the root of this repo or in the `StackOverflow` subdirectory should be sufficient)

Jira: [YETI2-894](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-894)

## Summary

This PR is to make a set of small updates to DL API.
1. Remove `type` field from problem detail errors ([commit 1](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/682f42b4fb56cbf5c7fe126606bfab12ac744cc5), [commit 2](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/99c6f8731c35bc416bf02bfc7cb817ded53280d6))
    * [Per RFC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457.html#:~:text=not%20been%20present.-,3.1.1.%20%22,using%20HTML%20%5BHTML5%5D), the "type" field is optional and when it's not present, its value is assumed to be "about:blank"
    * Had to update some tests due to this change ([commit 3](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/15711f7886365db5f38169d89fd8c39bec964918), [commit 4](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/2855a90fd13d1d150ca4268610d835e740c28422))
    
2. Add an example for the "slug" parameter in Collectives endpoints ([commit](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/f6b51c45a4ebfba8e3f2d261085a3804adafe9a4))
   * Example used: `audiobubble`

3. Rename fields in `/collectives` and `/collectives/{slug}` responses ([commit](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/97c8d2cd12efb7c1813f502e91a5a646c2bb97a5))
   * "externalLinks" to "externalUrls" 
   * "link" to "url"

4. Add an example for the "site" path parameter for all endpoints ([commit](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/fc8ae13b81a50de166f631fdf6f56bfe2306c172))
   * Example used: `stackoverflow.com`
   * Created `SiteParameterOperationFilter` because the example is part of the parameter object (`parameter.Example`). Using an operation filter is the most direct approach instead of using schema or document filter.

5. Extra: found a parameter description that doesn't match the  param name so I fixed it ([commit](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/24660/commits/01d62c3ebdc911a854327728732dd42c4051591b))
## How to Test

**Remove `type` field from problem detail errors**
1. Checkout main branch and test some of the endpoints with invalid parameters. Note that you see the "type" field in the response
2.  Checkout this branch (llee/YETI2-894-dl-api-updates) and repeat steps above. Validate that the "type" field is removed

**Add an example for the "slug" parameter in Collectives endpoints**
1. Go to Collectives section on the DL API docs site
2. Review endpoints that require a slug and validate the example is added. Hover over and it should show `audiobubble`

**Rename fields in `/collectives` and `/collectives/{slug}` responses**
1. Make successful requests to 2 endpoints above > validate the responses have updated field names like "externalUrls" and "url"

**Add an example for the "site" path parameter for all endpoints**
1. Go to the DL API docs site
2. Spot check endpoints and validate the site path parameter includes an example. However over and it should show `stackoverflow.com`
3. Download OpenAPI Document and confirm the site example `stackoverflow.com` is added

author: giamir
body:
[SPARK-153](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/SPARK-153)

## Summary

This PR is adjusting the styles for the FragmentLayout view the monolith returns for the UI composer. Specifically it address a few things that brings the responsiveness of those legacy pages to its original state. Note that the new Left Sidebar now measure 282px (compared to old one that was 164px). The responsiveness of most pages is decent but not as good as if they are rendered on the old legacy chrome due to this 118px width difference.

**What changed?**
- Configuration of breakpoints and css-reset for scoped v2 css is now specified correctly
- Now all elements with a s-* class regardless of the placement of the class get their v3 attributes reverted
- Now we make sure global resets continue to be respected (things like `box-sizing` and `font-weight` set on the `body` or `html` continue to be honoured despite the `revert: all` property)
- Stacks v2 scoped styles are now wrapped on a @layer to ensure non-stacks styles (for example styles set by primary.css or secondary.css continue to have the same css specificity and take precedence when appropriate
- Removed practical example of how @scope limits work in the FragmentLayout (it was using activity indicator as an example)

## How to Test

- I have deployed this PR in ascn dev so you can check
  - https://beta.ascn-dev.stackoverflow.dev/tags
  - https://beta.ascn-dev.stackoverflow.dev/users

If you want to have a reference on how this was looking before you can checkout main test

## Summary

This allows for the third party OAuth logins, e.g. Google, Github, Facebook, etc, to work with the Shine Beta.  

When an OAuth login request is sent to the provider we include a small bag of json data called `OAuthLoginState`.  In this bag we include the siteId.  Because the shine site is not a "true" site with its own siteId, when StackAuth receives the authenticated login request from the provider, it loads up the main site using the siteId that we sent in the data bag and redirects to there. This then fails with an error about forgery because it's not the same host that requested the login.

This PR adds a flag to the `OAuthLoginState` data bag to say that the request comes from a shine beta site.  StackAuth will then verify that the site with the SiteId from the data bag has Shine Beta enabled and will replace the host in the redirect url to the configured shine url for the loaded siteId.

To enable this, I needed to separate the concepts of "being allowed to use the shine beta url" from "whether the incoming request is from the UI Composer". The authenticated redirect back from StackAuth will not be a UI Composer request, so the existing logic would ignore the shine host and redirect back to the main site. This is effectively a breaking change for existing use-cases, which I have updated in this PR.  [Slack Thread](https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C09712XAE3S/p1765813914569899?thread_ts=1765807705.437709&cid=C09712XAE3S) with how we got here.

To be exact:  `Current.Site.TryGetShineBetaUrl` no longer includes the check `Current.IsUIComposerRequest` and so both will need to be called if both checks are required.

I also refactored the Auth handling controller to reduce duplication as the provider handlers shared virtually all of the same code.

Note: There's a couple of security issues raised by CodeQL, but I've dismissed them. Nothing has been made worse with this change, and the strings are just the way the OAuth redirects work 🤷🏻‍♀️.

## How to Test

1. On meta.stackexchange.local ensure that logging in with Google, Github, etc still work.
2. Ensure you've got all that's needed set up locally to run the Shine Beta (inc UI Composer, Site Chrome, etc). See [Onboarding Tab in the Shine Tech Plan](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12aT9irYEmEvPqyssvV4myLP2VjC7xJio_JMKTAiR3g0/edit?tab=t.m44njmxncpsi#heading=h.3811qyt58k4e).
3. On the Shine Beta site, ensure that logging in with Google, Github, etc work.

## Summary

We are currently hard-coding the achievement count in the chrome service's topbar.  This includes the required two fields for achievements to properly show the achievement counts:

- Does the user have any unread non-rep achievements?
- What is the sum of all unread rep-change achievements?

1. Figure out your accountId

4. Get an auth token for yourself to test the API via swagger.  (You'll need to open dev tools, network tab, and get the Bearer token): https://meta.stackexchange.local/oauth/token

author: elcart
body:
## Summary

Whoopsie. In tweaking the server response for the new OBC replies (to just return a bog standard 200), we used a check for the existence of the `opinion-based-content-type` field in the submitted answer form.

Problem is - that field exists on the traditional Q&A form too: a hangover from when we were using the razor `Questions/Show` answer form for OBC (pre-Svelte).

We could _probably_ just rip the field back out at this point, but if for whatever reason we need to disable threading for anyone, they'll revert back to this form and without the field OBC answers wouldn't submit correctly.

So the fix is to check for a value in the field; if empty, it's a Q&A answer.

## How to Test

1. Make sure OBC and threading are enabled
2. Submit a trad Q&A answer; page should auto-reload due to redirect, with the new answer now visible, no errors
3. Submit an OBC reply; replies should refresh _without_ a full reload, new reply now visible
title: [CE-2143] check for OBC Type value in answer submit form

## Summary

This is essentially a light-touch version of the editor draft functionality (see Ask V3).

We store an object in the island state which is essentially a mapping of the postId used by each specific editor (the 'editorId', if you want) against whatever's been entered into it.

### Save/delete logic
Currently:
- hitting esc: draft retained
- opening another editor: draft retained
- clicking 'cancel': draft deleted

The above probably want discussing with the wider team.

### All that other crap

Yeah sorry about this; as part of the changes here I extracted our constants from state and stopped using context for them. (Fingers crossed that doesn't make a mess of SSR if and when we get round to it...service might do it differently anyway though so who's counting)

author: elcart
body:
## Summary

We'd chopped the sides off the editor. Turns out `overflow-hidden` wasn't the right way to go, we wanted `wmn0`, and here's why:

```
In a flex row, items have min-width: auto by default, which means "don't get narrower than
your content's intrinsic width." A long code block therefore sets a minimum width larger than
the container, and the flex item refuses to shrink, causing overflow.

Setting min-width: 0 removes that intrinsic minimum, so the flex item is allowed to shrink below
its content width. Then the overflowing content can be clipped or scrolled
(e.g., via overflow-x: auto on the <pre>), keeping the parent from expanding.
```

## How to Test

1. Find OBC
2. Reply using a loooong code block (all on one line preferably)
3. See that it doesn't overflow, should get a scrollbar
4. Hit reply or edit - editor should get full blue border
title: [CE-2119] fix missing editor border sides

author: jdarcyso
body:
## Summary

Certain large reply with code snippets causing overflow on page

## How to Test

1. Enable OBC
2. Create OBC question
3. Copy in this reply and check it doesn't result in overflow:
Do note, however, that TIdHTTP does support receiving and returning HTTP cookies. So, if Cloudflare happens to send you cookies, you can potentially use them in this case, but you might have to store and set them manually between your application sessions.

That being said, there are several other general problems with your code (not related to the Cloudflare issue):

You are using TStringStream without specifying a TEncoding, so it will use TEncoding::Default which is ANSI on Windows and UTF-8 on other platforms.  If you want to send UTF-8 encoded data, use TEncoding::UTF8 explicitly, eg:

TStringStream * Send = new TStringStream(rtf, TEncoding::UTF8);

You are passing a string to TStringStream's constructor and then immediately writing a byte buffer to the same stream using its Write() method. The constructor will encode and write the string but will leave the stream's Position property at 0, so the bytes written with Write() afterwards will overwrite the string written by the constructor.

You are setting the TIdSSLIOHandlerSocketOpenSSL's SSLOptions->Method property to sslvSSLv23, which is not advisable. For one thing, setting  sslvSSLv23 will enable SSL 2.0 and 3.0, which are not secure. But also, the SSLOptions->Method property has been deprecated for a long time. Use the SSLOptions->SSLVersions property instead, eg:

IdSSLIOHandlerSocketOpenSSL->SSLOptions->SSLVersions = TIdSSLVersions() << sslvTLSv1 << sslvTLSv1_1 << sslvTLSv1_2;

"utf-8" is not a valid Content-Encoding value.  If you are sending a UTF-8 encoded JSON, you should set the TIdHTTP's Request->CharSet property instead. However, the application/json media type does not require a charset attribute, and RFC 8259 requires UTF-8 when exchanging JSON between systems, so you don't actually need to specify a CharSet explicitly in this case.

You are setting the TIdHTTP's Request->AcceptCharSet property, but not setting its Request->Accept property.  If you are expecting the response to always be JSON, then you should set the Request->Accept property to "application/json" (or whatever JSON-based media type the server actually sends).
title: [CE-2109] - Fix reply overflow

Instead of creating the row in the Questions.Controller, we will now do it more or less concurrently with post creation, way down in the bowels of the business logic.

2. Check the OBC table to make sure everything looks right

Caveat: I've not actually done this, but should work:

author: DougWhitley
body:
## Summary
[YETI2-857](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/YETI2-857)
This PR adjusts how we send requests from the API Docs page to the API. Currently the API Sends requests with a `key` or `access_token` parameter. This PR updates the `console.js` file to send that information with an `Authorization Bearer` header.

## How to Test

From my testing it appears that the PR environments don't automatically have an app setup for the docs site so it is best to test locally.

### PubPlat

#### Questions
1. Visit the [Questions page](https://api.stackexchange.local/docs/questions)
2. Open your network tab.
3. validate that there are a few calls to `https://api.stackexchange.local/2.3/sites?pagesize=100&page=2&filter=!ZUhMc95zeV2ux` with different `page` parameters.
4. Validate that none of them include a `key` param, and that they are passing an Auth header using a bearer token.
5. Make sure that the site selector is set to `Meta Stack Exchange` and run the endpoint test in the docs page.
6. Validate in the network tab that the API call was made without a `key` param and that it passed an Auth Bearer token.

#### Notifications
1. Visit the [Notification page](https://api.stackexchange.local/docs/notifications) 
2. Make sure that your local instance of the docs app is not disabled in the Database
3. Use the get token button to auth through the docs app
4. Run the test call
5. Validate that the api call does not pass an `access_token` param and that the token you generated is passed as a bearer token in the network tab.
6. You may still get a disabled app result in the response, but we just need to validate that the call is being made correctly.

#### Comments
Comments has some extra code around it so we will test that doc too
1. Visit the [Comments page](https://api.stackexchange.local/docs/comments)
2. Make sure that you have the `Meta Stack Exchange` site selected.
3. Click the Run button 
4. Validate that the network tab doesn't show any calls being made with a `key` parameter, and that they are being made with a bearer token.

### Teams
1. Validate that the docs pages are operating as expected for Teams instances of API v2,x.
5. Running through the tests from the PubPlat section should cover all the bases.

body:
**This touches a hot path, so please review carefully.**

This PR adds the minimal integration needed for the **swaperoo**.  
Eligible anonymous users (via people selector) who load an **opinion-based, non-deleted** question are routed to a new Razor wrapper view that loads the Content Service UI.

### What this enables
- Quick production test of the new service under real traffic
- Validation of routing, load times, and stability
- Safe, temporary experiment (easy to switch off before code freeze)

### What’s included
- Early exit in `Show` for OBC posts
- New `OpinionBasedQuestionShowModel` + Razor view
- Guarded by `ContentServiceEnabledFor`

This is intentionally minimal and only for the swaperoo phase.  
The goal was to be least invasive to existing code and easy to revert.

We will later decide how and where we orchestrate things like:
- ask-question button
- guidelines
- ads
- other sidebar items

author: SteffiPeTaffy
body:
### Summary
This PR refactors the thumb-vote flow to use a single, consistent `ThumbVoteResult` model and centralizes all validation and vote execution logic in one place. It also fixes an existing bug where the code incorrectly used `Current.User` instead of the user provided to the vote service.

### What changed
- Added enriched internal `ThumbVoteResult` (Success, Error?, Message?).
- Reworked controller to use the new model while keeping the wire contract unchanged (only `success` + `message` for external callers).
- Fixed use of `Current.User` inside vote paths; now consistently uses the explicit user parameter.
- Consolidated scattered checks (read-only, invalid type, already voted, non-OBC, etc.) into a unified service function.

### Why
- Prevents subtle bugs caused by mixing `Current.User` with explicit user inputs.
- Makes the vote logic easy to reason about and test.
- Reduces duplication across multiple controller endpoints.
- Internal errors are now represented explicitly via the Error enum, while external behavior remains 100% backward-compatible.
title: CE-2089 Fix User Context Bug and Consolidate Thumb Vote Handling into a Single Path

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR removes the `TotalCount` and `TotalPages` properties from the DL API layer and adds `HasMore`. This is in preparation for the upcoming DL API release and will allow us to drop the intensive count queries in the future without breaking the API contract.

The change here is only on the surface since it uses the current page and `TotalPages` from the `Api.V3.Common` layer to determine if there is another page. To completely remove the dependency to `TotalPages` on each endpoint, we need to dive into whether permission checks happen before or after a result set is returned from SQL. If items are removed after, then `hasMore` must take that into account. Otherwise, counting the total number of items returned against the page size can be used to determine if there is another page (except in the case when the page is actually full and the last item is contained, in that case the next call will return an empty result set).

One issue that arose from this change is that several integration tests began failing because it could not handle a computed property. This is because integration tests return the response in JSON which is then deserialized. However, since `HasMore` was initially computed the response does not contain the properties needed (`TotalPages` and `TotalCount` in this case) to determine the value and it was always false. The work here calculates that value in `FromCommonDto` for each pagination object. 

An alternative is to create a separate constructor for each paginated response and mark it as `JsonConstructor` so that it used for JSON de/serialization. However, this leaves the `totalCount` constructor available in the DL API project which we may eventually want to move away from.

```
    [SwaggerSchema(Title = "Paginated changes")]
    public class PaginatedContentFeedChanges : PageResponseModel<ContentFeedChangeSummaryResponseModel, ContentFeedChangeSortParameter>
    {
        public PaginatedContentFeedChanges(int totalCount, int pageSize, int page, ContentFeedChangeSortParameter sort, SortOrder order,
            ImmutableList<ContentFeedChangeSummaryResponseModel> items) : base(totalCount, pageSize, page, sort, order, items)
        {
        }

        [JsonConstructor]
        public PaginatedContentFeedChanges(bool hasMore, int pageSize, int page, ContentFeedChangeSortParameter sort, SortOrder order,
            ImmutableList<ContentFeedChangeSummaryResponseModel> items) : base(hasMore, pageSize, page, sort, order, items)
        {
        }
    }

```

## How to Test

1. https://api.stackexchange.local/dl/docs/openapi/v1.json and Ctrl+f `totalCount` and `totalPages` there should be no results. `hasMore` will return multiple results.
2. Spot check the docs page there should be no references to `totalCount` and `totalPages`, you should now see `hasMore`

**Endpoints**
Spot-check the property on a few endpoints
1. `/content-feeds/comments` - Last page 34327 should have `hasMore` = false, 34326 should have `hasMore` = true
2. `/questions` (time-based pagination off) - Last page 3253 should be `hasMore`=false, 3252 should have `hasMore`=true
3. `/tags`- Last page 42 should have `hasMore` = false, 41 should have `hasMore` = true
title: YETI2-879 - Remove `TotalCount` and `TotalPages` props, add `HasMore` to PageResponseModel

author: KyleMit
body: MOD-393 | Duplicate of #24475 ## Summary * Update spam detection mechanism to handle identical ML and cosine risks * Refactor ComparePostToSpamAndActAsync for easier flow ## How to Test 1. Set thresholds for warning very low `0.0001` and danger very high `0.9999`. (try to guarantee a warning level for both ml and cosine) * [`SpamML.FlaggingEnabled`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=SpamML.FlaggingEnabled) - `true` * [`SpamML.WarningThreshold`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=SpamML.WarningThreshold) - `.001` * [`SpamML.DangerThreshold`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=SpamML.DangerThreshold) - `.999` * [`SpamSimilarity.FlaggingEnabled`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=SpamSimilarity.FlaggingEnabled) - `true` * [`SpamSimilarity.WarningThreshold`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=SpamSimilarity.WarningThreshold) - `.001` * [`SpamSimilarity.DangerThreshold`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=SpamSimilarity.DangerThreshold) - `.999` 2. Create any post - realistically, any post will fall between these ranges 3. Check if the detection mechanism is both: ```sql SELECT * INTO #SpamDetectionTypes FROM (VALUES (0, 'Unknown'), (1, 'Cosine'), (2, 'ML'), (3, 'Both') ) AS e(Id, [Name]); SELECT TOP 10 sdt.Name AS SpamDetectionMechanism, f.[Data], f.* FROM Flags f JOIN #SpamDetectionTypes sdt ON sdt.Id = JSON_VALUE(f.Data, '$.SpamDetectionMechanism') WHERE FlagTypeId = 46 -- PostSpamAuto AND ISJSON(f.[Data]) = 1 ORDER BY f.Id DESC ``` 4. Set similarity threshold super low -> create post -> should be ML 5. Set ML threshold super low -> create post -> should be Cosine
title: MOD-393 When both Cosine Similarity and ML Model record the same threshold, update the logging to record both

author: dionrhys
body:
Slack context: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/CBVG8MJQN/p1764757459301799

> @WouterDeKort: Anyone seeing this error when building the monolith locally?
> ```
> Error (active)	CS8103	Combined length of user strings used by the program exceeds allowed limit. Try to decrease use of string literals or try the EXPERIMENTAL feature flag 'experimental-data-section-string-literals'.	StackOverflow.Localization	D:\code\StackOverflow\StackOverflow.Localization\CSC
> ```

Oh boy, that's some compile error.

I've written the background and explanation of the problem and fix into the change itself here.

**Background tl;dr** As of #24209, the combined size of all our translated strings from Transifex has gotten so large (over 16 MiB in UTF-16) that the .NET assembly cannot contain them all in the `UserString` heap (where string literals normally go). We get a CS8103 compile error when trying to build the project in Visual Studio.

**Fix tl;dr** Earlier this year, Microsoft brought in the [experimental-data-section-string-literals](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/560ae426c0bd44657119b2a5fcdf5e927e833de5/docs/features/string-literals-data-section.md) feature for these cases, which moves string literals that are above a certain length to somewhere else in the assembly that doesn't have the size limits. This comes with potential performance caveats and the risk of the feature changing or being removed at any point.

The alternative ways to fix this (e.g. splitting the SO.Localization assembly into multiple assemblies) might take more effort to implement and some folks are currently blocked on building locally with Visual Studio. It appears this is because Visual Studio 2026 doesn't respect our global.json to use the .NET 8 SDK when the `PrecompiledLocalizationDictionary` generator analyzer is running and uses the .NET 10 SDK instead; using the newer SDK causes the limit to be hit for some reason. `dotnet build` works at the moment without this PR because it respects the global.json file and builds with .NET 8 SDK. If I bump the SDK to 10 in the global.json file, `dotnet build` also fails.

# Comparisons

Here are size comparisons before and after this PR. I had to revert dac689f4ecca55f2c294d4177e5292feefb668bf and cf124e342ee008734d05e05b81a80db8f9d54380 locally to get the project to build.

-|Assembly size|UserString heap size
-|-|-
Before|20,144,640 bytes|15,259,824 bytes
After|20,242,432 bytes|10,730,200 bytes (70.3% of original)

The maximum UserString heap size is 16,777,216 bytes.

# Testing

**This is a big underlying change** to how the localization strings are stored, and we use all these strings all over all our hot paths, so this needs a really good sanity check to be sure this doesn't affect our performance too much.

@StackEng/team-product-platform I'll need your help for this. Ideally we need to compare startup times and page rendering durations if possible. Ideally also a canary deployment would be great but I don't think we have that capability at the moment post-Ascension.
title: Fix StackOverflow.Localization exceeding the assembly UserString heap limit

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
Context in this Slack thread: https://stackexchange.slack.com/archives/C05U5BB3YQN/p1764775578859249?thread_ts=1764770596.818929&cid=C05U5BB3YQN

After a bit of digging to see when the response may have been started before we attempt to set a status code I've found that with web sockets the situation is a little different from regular HTTP calls.
Turns out that when you `await httpContext.WebSockets.AcceptWebSocketAsync()` this sends a `HTTP 101 Switching Protocols` to the client effectively starting the response...
Normally when no problems occur when pumping websocket data back-and-forth the fragment proxy sends a `EmptyResult()` on completion which doesn't touch the `HttpContext.Response` at all.

However, when an exception occurs while we're pumping data we land in a try/catch and return a `ProxyResult.Error` and we drop into the `DevMessageOrErrorPage()` route which _does_ try to change the `HttpContext.Response` and triggers the error we're seeing.
title: [FRAGMENT PROXY] Return empty result when response has already started

body:
[KRAKEN-2555](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/KRAKEN-2555)

## Summary
This PR adds the MarkAllAsRead endpoint to our internal api, I also fixed `InboxMessageModel.HasBeenRead` as it was opposite of what the name implies. This pr goes hand and hand with my [chrome-service pr](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.SiteChrome/pull/69)

## How to test
1. First get the latest version of my [chrome-service pr](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.SiteChrome/pull/69) and build it
2. Find a user that has unread notifications on meta.stackexchange.local
3. Get that users jwt token using the /developer/users/get-impersonation-jwt/{userId} route
4. Using Requestly add the authorization header for both localhost and api-internal.local
5. Launch our chrome-service and WebApi
6. Open the notification inbox

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

Yet another special case in how we handle account history:
1. When the user became a developer (thus an employee), we didn't store the related account history - that sometimes happens (still).
2. Then the person left the company and that was stored correctly.
3. Then the person deleted the profile.
4. Then the profile was recreated.
5. If the profile gets recreated shortly after deletion, the createddate is restored from logs. If more time passes, Current.Time is set as creationdate.

So we have a past employee, where we don't have info when this person started the job. I was taking profile creation date as the beginning of the tenure, but that's incorrect in this case... So maybe we should just take min of starting date and the oldest history entry.

Maybe you could even just take the date of the oldest history entry of any type for the related account? That sounds even safer.

## How to Test

There's an integration test added. The edge case is not easy to reproduce locally:
1. Create a user.
7. Make it an employee or a developer through the db, so that no entry occurs. There's also another way to achieve that through our API, but I'm not sure how. Editing account type correctly stores the account history, so that's not helpful in this case.
8. Ask a question.
9. Edit the account type to Registered.
10. Delete the user.
11. Modify the traces in log to delete "creationdate" from log entry.
12. Undelete the user.
13. Go to the created question and see the badge (or don't, if it's fixed already).

Alternatively you could clear the log entries and recreate the user, but I'm not sure how to do that locally.
title: fix a weird edge case in calculating employee tenures

body:
## Bug Fix for [TEAMS-15089](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-15089): Remove Close Option from Manage Dropdown for Obsolete Questions (Teams Only)

### Problem
When an Admin or Moderator user opens an obsolete question on a **Teams site**, the "Manage" button incorrectly displays three options: "Unmark Obsolete," "Delete," and "Close." The "Close" option should not appear for obsolete questions on Teams.


### Root Cause
The `showCloseLink` condition in the manage dropdown doesn't consider whether a question is obsolete on Teams sites.

### Solution
1. **Updated PostMenuPolicy.ShouldRenderCloseLink()** - Added `isObsolete` and `isPubPlat` parameters
2. **Teams-aware logic** - Only blocks close link when `not isPubPlat && isObsolete`
3. **Public sites unchanged** - Obsolete parameter ignored on non-Teams sites
4. **Modified view logic** - Pass both obsolete state and site type to policy method

### Changes Made

#### 1. PostMenuPolicy.cs
- Added `isObsolete` and `isPubPlat` parameters with default values
- Added return `false` if question is obsolete AND it's a Teams site

#### 2. PostMenu.cshtml
- Updated `ShouldRenderCloseLink` call to include both `p.IsObsolete` and `Current.Site.IsPubPlat`
- Simplified manage dropdown condition (Teams/obsolete check now in policy)

#### 3. Extended CloseLinkPolicyTests.cs
- Obsolete questions don't render close option
- All existing should work as before

## Summary

This PR adds four rate limiters ( `TokenBucket`, `BurstThrottle`, `Identity` and `Backoff`) to the DL API and Common API code. The Implementation for the `IdentityRateLimiter` is in the DataLicensing Presentation layer, and the other three are in the shared common code.

Unit tests have been added for these tests to the appropriate testing collection, and integration tests have been added to the Data Licensing Integration Tests.

## How to Test

1. Adjust your testing applications rate limit to be low enough that you can hit the API 10-20 times for this test
2. Hit the API with Postman and validate that you have header information for all four rate limiters.
3. Repeatedly hit the API with requests and validate that the `TokenBucket`, `Identity`, and `BurstThrottle` rate limiters all decrement as expected.
4. Adjust the site setting for the backoff rate limiter to be very small, and hit the API to trigger the back off
5. Validate that you cannot hit the API again until the backoff rate limiter timer has expired.
6. Continue to hit the API until you have exhausted the amount of calls for the identity rate limiter
7. Validate that you cannot hit the API any more with your current app key
8. Validate that you can hit the API with a different app key.

author: aalear
body:
MOD-342

## Summary

Before Ascension, we built a service in Providence that took a list of account ids that were manually marked by CMs as spammers and looked up other account ids with matching Providence cookies in an attempt to identify networks of spam accounts. This mechanism was migrated to Snowflake when Providence was deprecated as part of Ascension.

Unfortunately, many users were mistakenly merged together in early-ish 2024, leading to the data it collected becoming unreliable for some major spam accounts, and by the end of 2025 the use of the feature is pretty much non-existent.

This PR removes all code related to it with the exception of a way to mark/unmark an account as a spammer. We may find another use for that in the future and we're also preserving existing data.

Note that while we did use Providence/Snowflake to flag other accounts, those accounts were never automatically marked or unmarked as spam, so all the data on this that we have in the Sites DB should be as reliable as we trust ourselves to be.
title: MOD-342 Remove code related to the spammer service running in Snowflake

body: MOD-294 ## Summary * Adds two new counters with the prefix `web.spam.*` * Adds new spam metric logger service we can DI into services * Wires up event handlers during post undeleted and flag clearing to increment metrics when appropriate ## How to Test 1. To view events, locally, Clone [DogStatsMonitor](https://github.com/StackEng/DogStatsMonitor) 2. Run the following command to start the project and listen for spam metrics ```bash dotnet run --project ./src/DogStatsMonitor/DogStatsMonitor.csproj -- metrics --metric "web\.spam.*" ``` 6. Create a post that casts a post spam auto flag of any type - flag counter should increment 7. Look for pending flags - https://meta.stackexchange.local/spam/recent-auto-flagged?statusFilter=PendingFlags 8. Load up the post and dismiss a flag as **helpful**, invalidated counter should **not increment** 9. Load up another post and dismiss a flag as **declined**, invalidated counter should **increment** 10. Look for binding flags - https://meta.stackexchange.local/spam/recent-auto-flagged?statusFilter=BindingFlag 11. Load up post and undelete, invalidated counter should increment ## Debugging Dog Stats Monitor 1. If you're going crazy trying to figure out if dog stats monitor is even working, you can add this test endpoint ``` [StackRoute("developer/similarity/test-send-metrics", HttpVerbs.Get)] public ActionResult TestSendMetrics([FromServices] ISpamMetricLogger spamMetricLogger) { spamMetricLogger.IncrementSpamAutoFlagRaisedCounter(true, SpamDetectionMechanism.Both); return TextPlain("Incremented SpamAutoFlagRaisedCounter"); } ``` 3. Go to [`/developer/similarity/test-send-metrics`](https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/similarity/test-send-metrics) 4. It takes quite a while and sometimes you have to scroll up and down, but you should see the events in the logged output

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
SOE deployments run with 2 replicas each, however, right now we are only using topologySpreadConstraints to reduce the skew but schedule anyway if it can’t be fulfilled. 

We should introduce podAntiAffinity rules so that we force that both replicas go to 2 different nodes, so that if one node goes down, there is not an outage.

This PR uses the `.nodeScheduling.scheduleOnSeparateNodes` which control the already built-in podAntiAffinity rules in the helm charts, so that on cell customers the pods are always scheduled in different nodes. It also added podAntiAffinity rules for some channel deployments that didn't have them already.
title: PRODPLAT-169 Schedule SOE pods on separate nodes

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
This PR is the back-port of the changes we made to support the `Content-Security-Policy` HTTP header specifically for Bank of America.

When the `Security.ContentSecurityPolicyNonceGeneration` site setting is enabled, we will generate a nonce on every request and apply that to all `<script>` and `<style> tags that have the `asp-add-nonce` attribute specified.
This is handled by a Razor tag helper that handles removing the `asp-add-nonce` attribute (always!) and setting the nonce (if enabled!).

The nonce is generated in the ASPNet Core request pipeline via middleware and is stored on the `HttpContext.Items` and the `Current.Items` property bags so the value is accessible to all possible pieces of the monolith.

The `Content-Security-Policy` is constructed based on these site settings:

- `ContentSecurityPolicyHeader`
- `ContentSecurityPolicyHeaderScriptSrc`
- `ContentSecurityPolicyHeaderStyleSrc`

What's important is that `ContentSecurityPolicyHeader` shouldn't ever have `script-src` or `style-src` if the second two site settings have a value. If they do, the keywords will appear twice. (sucks I know, problem for `$future_me`)

When `ContentSecurityPolicyReportUrl` is set, the monolith will generate the  `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` HTTP header which will have the exact value as `Content-Security-Policy` but with `report-uri {the URL}` appended which sends all the CSP violations the browser detects to the report URL.

Most of the commits here are the changes to the individual Razor views.

A couple of notable things:

- Because we're using a Razor tag helper, all inline Razor functions need to be `async`. Most of these functions don't `await` anything which is why you'll see the `#pragma warning disable CS1998` directive popping up everywhere.
- Intercom and Freshdesk widgets are _broken_. There is currently no way to support the very strict CSP header BofA is apparently requiring and what these widgets are dynamically generating 🤷 There is a plan to deal with this but that's going to be a pig of a job.

This PR is _huuuuge_, apologies but it is what it is.
title: INFRA-595: BofA CSP (#25556)

author: jtoom4SO
body:
## Summary

Jira: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/ZAMB-124

Ask Team Members user search returned "No results" for queries with reversed name order (e.g. `Smith John` for "John Smith") or trailing whitespace (e.g. `Smith `). The matcher did a plain substring check on the whole query string. This tokenizes the query on whitespace and requires each token to appear (in any order) within one of the user's name, email, or external ID fields.

**Scope:** minimal fix for the originally-reported reverse-name-order and trailing-whitespace cases. Cross-field token matching (e.g. one token matching the name and another matching the externalId on the same user) is intentionally out of scope.

## How to Test

1. Open a question editor that includes the **Ask team members** widget
2. Search for an existing user by reversing first/last name (e.g. `Smith John` for "John Smith") — should match
3. Search with trailing whitespace (e.g. `Smith `) — should match
4. Confirm forward-order, single-token, email, and external-ID searches still match
5. `npm run test:unit` from `_Scripts/islands/user-editor/` passes (`Candidate.test.ts` has 6 new cases covering tokens, whitespace, and the all-tokens-must-match invariant)
title: ZAMB-124: Match user search by name tokens in any order

body:
## Summary

This is an important event for Braze since it will remove a user from Braze so we stop sending emails to them. Due to its importance, we want this to be published via the outbox so we have guaranteed delivery.

Originally, this event was being published in `ProductEventsDispatch` via an internal event handler. The only thing that event handler was doing was publishing the product event. I removed that handler. The internal event still gets fired so other subscribers still use the event.

There is one potential issue that I don't think will be a problem but it's something to be aware of: the product event used to be published before the user deletion happened. I changed it so it now happens after. It shouldn't be an issue since product events handling is already "out-of-band".

## Testing

I deployed this branch to `load-test` and made sure the event is still published and that it flows through the outbox.

author: samordonez
body:
## Summary

Adopts the Salesforce Business Unit name change for the Premium tier (PRODPLAT-809).

- Bumps `StackExchange.Zuora` from `1.0.44` → `1.0.50`. `1.0.50` is a backport of PRODPLAT-809 onto the 1.0.x maintenance line. See [StackEng/StackExchange.Zuora#71](https://github.com/StackEng/StackExchange.Zuora/pull/71) for the backport itself.
- `ZuoraHelper.ToZuoraBusinessUnit()` returns `StackBusinessUnit.Business` for `TeamsTier.Premium` (was `SOForBusiness`).
- The three `UpdateLicensedSeats_PremiumDoesNotUpdateZuora_*` tests mock subscriptions with `FulfillmentType.Business`.

## Why 1.0.x and not 2.x?

The original version of this PR bumped to `StackExchange.Zuora` 2.1.2, which transitively requires `StackExchange.Utils.Http` 1.0 and `CsvHelper` 33. Together those force consumers into the in-progress JIL → STJ migration ([#25350](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/25350)), because Utils.Http 1.0 dropped Jil in favour of `System.Text.Json` for `SendJson`/`ExpectJson` — and STJ silently ignores `[DataMember(Name = "...")]` attributes that production models depend on. 

The 1.0.x backport is a tiny, isolated addition (just the new `StackBusinessUnit.Business` and `FulfillmentType.Business` enum values plus a couple of switch cases) that doesn't touch the HTTP/serialization stack at all, so this PR can ship now and the JIL → STJ work can proceed at its own pace in #25350.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build StackOverflow.sln` — passes with 0 errors
- [x] Unit tests pass locally
- [x] Three previously-failing `PremiumDoesNotUpdateZuora_*` tests now match the new enum value
- [ ] CI integration tests — pending current run

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: PRODPLAT-816: Upgrade StackExchange.Zuora to 1.0.50 and update ToZuoraBusinessUnit()

author: jtoom4SO
body:
## Summary

Jira: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/ZAMB-86

Searches from MS Teams containing `@` (e.g. `azure@Shell`, `DevOps@Shell`) were returning no results. The upstream `ExtractTagsAndTermsAsync` strips `@` and concatenates the surrounding tokens into one (`azureshell`), but Elasticsearch tokenizes on `@` at index time, so the resulting single token never matches. Replacing `@` with a space before passing the query to the search client tokenizes it the same way as the indexed content.

## How to Test

1. From MS Teams, run a search like `search azure@Shell` or `search DevOps@Shell`
2. Confirm relevant questions are returned (previously: no results)
3. Confirm plain searches without `@` still work as before
title: ZAMB-86: Fix MS Teams search failing when query contains '@'

author: sandermvanvliet-stack
body:
## Summary

- Folds the standalone `.github/workflows/trigger-analysis.yaml` workflow into the tail of the `build` job in `build_test_package.yml`, then deletes the original file.
- Preserves the `**.cs` / `**.cshtml` / `**.razor` path filtering by comparing changed files via `gh api repos/.../compare/<before>...<sha>` instead of GitHub's workflow-level `paths:` trigger.
- Dispatch is gated to `matrix.configuration == 'Release' && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` so it fires once per push to main, matching the original scope.

## Behavior change worth flagging

The analysis trigger previously fired regardless of whether the main build succeeded — it was its own workflow listening for the same push. After this change it only fires if the `Release` matrix entry of the `build` job succeeds. Reasonable trade-off (no point analyzing a broken build), but flagging in case anyone was relying on the old behavior.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on this PR: confirm the two new steps appear in the `build` job and are **skipped** on every matrix entry (PR runs are excluded by the `if:` condition).
- [ ] After merge to `main`: confirm the steps run on the `Release` matrix entry and skip on the other three. If the merge touched a `.cs`/`.cshtml`/`.razor` file, confirm a workflow run shows up at https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.Analyzers/actions/workflows/analyze-stackoverflow.yml for the merge SHA.
- [ ] Sanity-check a docs-only commit on main afterwards — the trigger step should be skipped (output `trigger=false`).

author: daleksiuk
body:
https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-15990

When displaying logs on the `/ingestion` page, because we were relying on the IngestionSourcePostMetadata table, we are unable to display page names for failed confluence cloud page ingestions as there will be a record in IngestionConfluenceCloudPages but not in IngestionSourcePostMetadata.

We already flipped the Sql query around so `IngestionConfluenceCloudPages ` is the source of truth and we left join `IngestionSourcePostMetadata` instead. So we need to additionally add a PageName column to the `IngestionConfluenceCloudPages` table and populate it at time of creation. That PageName is a guess due to the logic in https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow.KnowledgeIngestion/pull/469. So we still fallback to the `IngestionSourcePostMetadata` table when we can to get the true correct page name.

## How to Test

1. Apply migration `1358` (adds `PageName` to `IngestionConfluenceCloudPages` and backfills from `PageId`).
2. As a Teams admin, ingest a Confluence Cloud space and let at least one page fail (e.g. trip the connector or force `IngestionStatus.ExternalIngestionFailure`).
3. Open the ingestion log / dashboard and find the failed row. Confirm the displayed name is the Confluence page's title (e.g. "Onboarding Guide"), not the raw page ID.
4. Re-ingest the same page after renaming it in Confluence and confirm the log row updates to the new title (covers the `ResetPageForReingestion` path).
title: TEAMS-15990: Re elevate PageName to IngestionConfluenceCloudPages table level instead of from the document level in IngestionSourcePostMetadata

author: daleksiuk
body:
TEAMS-15979

## Summary

In production, intermittently, a published review queue item is remaining in the review queue. The reason for this is that there are two review tasks for the post, verified by querying the production stackint instance. This is probably from a race condition in the scheduled sync job that creates the tasks.

This fix, generated by Codex, does a query to fetch duplicate items and uses the review queue engine's existing invalidation logic. I tested that the query works using an Octopus runbook. What I like about this fix is that it is fairly basic, and cleans up the problem in environments where it has already happened.

There is a second new guardrail that makes sure the post is in the right state for its related ReviewTask to be shown.

An alternative fix to the root-cause might be to put a unique index in the DB like this and then catch the exception, but I like the invalidation fix for the reasons above:
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX UX_ReviewTasks_Ingestion_Active_PostId
ON ReviewTasks(PostId)
WHERE ReviewTaskTypeId = 15
  AND DeletionDate IS NULL
  AND IsAudit = 0;
```

## How to Test

This query will duplicate a ReviewTask row in the same way we see it in production. In `main`, you are able to hit the duplicate task. In this branch, it won't be shown to you and it will be cleaned up.

```sql
DECLARE @OriginalReviewTaskId int = <a local active review task id>;
DECLARE @DuplicateReviewTaskId int;

INSERT INTO ReviewTasks (
    ReviewTaskTypeId,
    CreationDate,
    DeletionDate,
    ReviewTaskState,
    IsAudit,
    PostId,
    SuggestedEditId,
    AuditPositivity,
    AuditTitle,
    AuditBody,
    AuditComment,
    ValidResultCount,
    CreationReason
)
SELECT
    ReviewTaskTypeId,
    CreationDate,
    NULL,
    1, -- Active
    IsAudit,
    PostId,
    SuggestedEditId,
    AuditPositivity,
    AuditTitle,
    AuditBody,
    AuditComment,
    0,
    CreationReason
FROM ReviewTasks
WHERE Id = @OriginalReviewTaskId
  AND ReviewTaskTypeId = 15 -- Ingestion
  AND DeletionDate IS NULL;

SET @DuplicateReviewTaskId = CONVERT(int, SCOPE_IDENTITY());

SELECT @DuplicateReviewTaskId AS DuplicateReviewTaskId;
```

If you run this SQL, you will see that there is an available duplicate:
```sql
WITH ActiveIngestionReviewTasks AS (
    SELECT rt.Id,
           IsReviewable =
               CASE WHEN p.Id IS NOT NULL
                         AND p.PostTypeId = 1
                         AND p.PostState = 50
                         AND p.DeletionDate IS NULL
                         AND p.ClosedDate IS NULL
                         AND p.LockedDate IS NULL
                    THEN 1
                    ELSE 0
               END,
           DuplicateRank = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY rt.PostId ORDER BY rt.CreationDate, rt.Id)
    FROM ReviewTasks rt
    LEFT JOIN Posts p ON p.Id = rt.PostId
    WHERE rt.ReviewTaskTypeId = 15
        AND rt.DeletionDate IS NULL
        AND rt.IsAudit = 0
)
SELECT Id
FROM ActiveIngestionReviewTasks
WHERE IsReviewable = 0
    OR DuplicateRank > 1;
```


Then publish the original review task through the UI. After that, you should have the published post plus the duplicate active task still in ReviewTasks, which simulates the bug. One indication that you're replicating it is that when you navigate to the newly created duplicate review task, you see vote buttons since it is linked to a published post.

You can tell that this fix worked in the PR branch because it says that the task is no longer reviewable, and you won't hit it randomly in the review queue.

If you run the dupe check SQL above, it won't come back with anything because this fix also invalidates all of the duplicates.

SELECT TOP 1 @PostId = P.Id FROM Posts AS P WHERE P.Id NOT IN (SELECT PostId FROM IngestionSourcePostMetadata) INSERT INTO IngestionSourcePostMetadata(IngestionSourceTypeId, PostId, CreationDate, SourceUrl, ConfidenceScore, ExternalId, ExternalName, ExternalDocumentId) VALUES (1, @PostId, GETUTCDATE(), 'http://google.com', 12, 'confluence-page-id-1', 'confluence space 1', 12345) INSERT INTO ReviewTasks (ReviewTaskTypeId, CreationDate, ReviewTaskState, PostId) VALUES(15, GETUTCDATE(), 1, @PostId) ``` * Go to https://stackenterprise.local/ingestion?sourceType=ConfluenceCloud&page=1 and click `Delete all posts` on the new test row * Confirm the page reloads and the item is shown as `Deleting` status: * The documents row on the python side needs to be deleted too, if testing with a real process, either by turning on the service or manually deleting the row. * Run the scheduled job to transition it into the `Deleted` status: https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/sync-confluence-cloud-pages * You should see the message: `Syncing statuses completed. Total updated: 1.` * Next run the scheduled job to complete the deletion: https://stackenterprise.local/scheduled/ingestion-confluence-delete * Confirm the record in `IngestionConfluenceCloudPages` is fully deleted now: DeletionDate is set and ProcessingStateId is 99.

author: marradoss
body:
## Summary

This PR looks at the integration tests we have for votes and restructures them.

### What's the goal

The goal is to have a living doc of all requirements. Ultimately, having a reasonably full and readable test coverage/living doc will enable us to use claude more efficiently. Much less stress about introducing regression errors cause the critical functionality is covered, and if something break, we exactly know what.

### Why the naming

Each test should describe what requirement(s) it tests and what functionality is broken when the test is red. Naming connected to requirements allows us for faster assessment of the criticality of the bug. Grouping by functionality rather than for class tested allows us to easier look for related problems and edge cases.

### Why integration tests

The first reason is that those tests are overarching the db, modules and the monolith code, so they can be very helpful when we decide to modularize stuff with Claude's help.
The other reason is that they are easier to connect to requirements than unit tests - smaller chance that claude gets it wrong.
Is it ideal? No. Is it fast and robust to errors? I think so.

### What's included

I focused on the voting and all of its types. The tests themselves were not changed. No new tests were introduced. I only moved the tests around, regrouped them and made sure that the names make sense.

### Tradeoffs

The naming was generated by Claude. It may be wrong. But, when reviewing the test names and comparing them to the old ones, I often caught myself realizing why a test was introduced in the first place. That's a huge win for me. If you agree and also find this helpful, let's merge it and I'll move on to a next domain.
title: Refactor votes tests

3. Approve and merge if everything looks good. If not, follow up with the team that added the problematic strings to correct any issues and (optionally) wait for the fixes to be merged and the workflow to re-run to pick up any changes.

Questions, comments, concerns? Give the Ascension team a shout.

body:
## Summary

Fixes [A11Y-156](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/A11Y-156) — four BofA audit defects where focus or input events triggered automatic context changes (navigation, page refresh, search) without an explicit user gesture, violating WCAG 3.2.1, 3.2.2, and 3.2.4.

- **SO_55** — Articles and Collections list pages: replaced the auto-navigating Permissions and Sort `<select>` controls with Stacks button groups backed by normal links, so focus and keyboard exploration do not change context; updated the labels to fit the compact layout, added `bg-black-050`, removed “for this filter” count copy, and refined the responsive filter layout across desktop, narrow desktop, and mobile widths
- **SO_142** — Moderator analytics: replaced `change` event listener on report selectors, which auto-submitted the form, with an Apply button click handler
- **SO_234** — Dashboard > Comments: removed 300ms debounced `keyup` auto-search; wired form `submit` event to the AJAX filter so search only runs on Enter or button click; added a visible Search button
- **SO_117** — Tag popup on Tools > Stats: rewrote `showingPopup()` in `07_TagMenu.js` to use `offset()` (absolute document coordinates) instead of `position()` (relative to offset parent), so the popup renders in the correct position when tags are inside a table layout rather than a standard post container

## Test plan

- [ ] Articles > Permissions/Sort: tab through the filter links — no navigation on focus; activate each option — navigates correctly with title/author filters preserved
- [ ] Collections > Permissions/Sort: tab through the filter links — no navigation on focus; activate each option — navigates correctly with title/creator filters preserved
- [ ] Articles and Collections responsive layout: check desktop, 981-1006px, <=980px, and narrow mobile widths; filter controls stay inside content padding and do not awkwardly wrap or truncate labels
- [ ] Articles and Collections empty-state counts: filtered zero-result copy omits “for this filter”
- [ ] Moderator inbox > Dashboard > Analytics: change report selector — no page refresh; click Apply — refreshes chart
- [ ] User > Dashboard > Comments: type in search field — no auto-search; press Enter or click Search — filters results
- [ ] Tools > Stats > New Tags: hover or tab to a tag — popup appears adjacent to the tag, consistent with tag popups on Q&A pages
- [ ] Tag popups on standard Q&A pages still position correctly

author: troygould-stack
body:
[TEAMS-15941]

## Summary

*Removing the check of SiteSetting or Statsig to check if an Enterprise has the Ingestion feature*

Every customer gets the free Ingestion tier called "foundation". This PR removes the SiteSetting and check from Statsig which previously only included users with paid tiers. 

Most places that previously checked `IsIngestionEnabled` now need to check `IsIngestionActivatedByAdmin` instead. 

**Note:** I also added the infra to pull statsig SDK key inot this PR. It was in another PR, but each really need each other to test properly. This PR fixes a previous bug that made the other PR difficult to test.

## How to Test

1. Do an `az login` to ensure your personal SO account is authenticated to Azure, and not one of our `stackenterprise.local` test accounts.
2. Build app - sometimes you have to do a clean to get it to rebuild the .json.secret and .json files once they are deleted. I use this powershell script to ensure they are all deleted. 
```
Get-ChildItem -Path . -Recurse -Directory -Filter "bin" |
    ForEach-Object {
        Get-ChildItem -Path $_.FullName -Recurse -File |
            Where-Object { $_.Name -match '^environmentsettings\..+\.json(\.secret)?$' }
    } |
    ForEach-Object {
        Write-Host "Deleting: $($_.FullName)"
        Remove-Item $_.FullName -Force
    }

Write-Host "Done."
exit
```
3. Verify that the `environmentsettings.Local.Enterprise.json` file under `C:\code\StackOverflow\StackOverflow\bin\Enterprise` and `C:\code\StackOverflow\StackOverflow.Api.V3\bin\Enterprise` have a section at the bottom called "Statsig" with a server secret that does not start with "ref+azurekeyvault" (these should get replaced during the build with the correct values from azure key vault.
4. Ensure that the api calls all work correctly.
    - specifically, the diagnostic endpoint in V3 (`ingest/available-diagnostics`) should return that the feature is enabled, the admin has enabled it, and api is enabled.
    - toggle UseStatsig site setting to false and run the api endpoints again. They should return defaults like 100 instead.
5. Ensure that you can still publish and ingest based on not being over the monthly limit.
6. Go the the admin settings for Ingestion and disable the Ingestion toggle. When you go back to the Swagger API, you should no longer see the Ingestion API endpoints for testing. As well, under Integration and Apps -> API you should not see Ingestion
7. Re-enable Ingestion toggle. The swagger endpoints for ingestion should show up again. As well, the Ingestion application should show under Integration and Apps -> API again.


[TEAMS-15941]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/TEAMS-15941?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: juanrodriguezcen
body:
Yesterday, I merged [a PR](https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/pull/25361) to update the versions of Scheduler and Tagserver so they are pulled from ACR instead of Cloudsmith. These are SOE's "external dependencies" (outside of the monolith). 

While doing so, I missed the fact that we include the Helm chart of those external dependencies in SOE's CNAB invocation image. In order to do so, the dockerfile runs a script (`cnab\soe\build\download-external-helm-charts.ps1`) that does the following for each external dependency: 
- Connects to the image registry (**Cloudsmith**) and queries the image's manifest
- From the manifest, it gets the `helm.chart` label which contains the helm chart version that should be used with the version pinned for that external dependency. 
- With the helm chart version, it download it from the helm charts repository (**Cloudsmith**)

This script works with both the image registry and the Helm charts repository in Cloudsmith. So, when I changed the registry to be ACR, this script broke, breaking SOE release creation. 

This PR reapplies the changes from the PR that I merged yesterday (and reverted), and fixes the script to download the Helm charts. It also fixes it so that we can build the SOE CNAB invocation locally so that `cnab-invoke.ps1` keeps working. 

Testing:
- The create releases workflow should work in this PR (does)
- Local deployments through `cnab-invoke.ps1` still work (I tested this)
title: PRODPLAT-463 Update scheduler version in SOE to run with .net 10 & pull images from ACR

body:
Reverts StackEng/StackOverflow#25361

The commit that is being reverted introduces a build problem on SOE's CNAB image. 

TL;DR;: In order to match a docker image with it's helm chart, we add a label on the docker image. When we build SOE's CNAB image, we download the helm chart using a script that reads the image's manifest via Cloudsmith's API. When changing that to ACR, we'll need to update the script to work with ACR. This work is needed to move away from Cloudsmith in SOE, I'm going to look into that tomorrow, but for now we should revert to unblock the pipeline.
