author: qheaden-stack
body:
## Summary

**Bug**: The weekly `RevokeDupeBadges()` task was incorrectly deleting multiple awards of the same community badge to the same user. Community badges that are configured to allow multiple awards (with `Single = 0`) were being treated as duplicates and only the first grant was preserved.

**Root Cause**: The deduplication query partitions badge grants by `(BadgeId, UserId, ReasonId)` and deletes all but the first row. When the same admin grants the same multi-award community badge to the same user multiple times, all rows have identical `(BadgeId, UserId, ReasonId)` values, causing them to be incorrectly deduplicated.

**Fix**: Modified the `RevokeDupeBadges()` query to exclude community badges from deduplication:
- Added filter: `AND u2b.BadgeId NOT IN (SELECT Id FROM Badges WHERE BadgeReasonTypeId = {=CommunityBadge})`
- This preserves the original intent (removing true duplicates from scheduler race conditions) while respecting that community badges are explicitly allowed to be awarded multiple times
- Changed `RevokeDupeBadges()` from `private` to `internal` to allow direct testing

## How to Test

1. Run the integration tests:
   ```bash
   dotnet test tests/StackOverflow.Tests.Integration --filter "ScheduledControllerWeeklyBadgeDedupTests"
   ```

2. All 4 tests should pass:
   - `RevokeDupeBadges_ShouldPreserveMultipleCommunityBadgeAwards` - Verifies grants from different admins are preserved
   - `RevokeDupeBadges_ShouldPreserveDuplicateGrantsFromSameAdminForMultiAwardBadge` - **Main bug fix test** - Verifies multiple grants from same admin are preserved
   - `RevokeDupeBadges_StillDedupsNonCommunityBadges` - Verifies the fix doesn't break original dedup for non-community badges
   - `RevokeDupeBadges_ShouldPreserveSingleAwardCommunityBadges` - Verifies single-award community badges are also protected

3. Manual verification (if needed):
   - Create a community badge with `Single = 0` (allows multiple awards)
   - Grant it multiple times to the same user as the same admin
   - Run the weekly scheduled task
   - Verify all badge grants are preserved (count in Users2Badges table)
title: [MOD-520] - Prevent community badge deduplication in weekly cleanup job

body: ## Summary Fixes a WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard accessibility issue on the close reasons admin page (`/admin/flags/site-specific-close-reasons`) where the "Edit question" link inside the post notice preview was reachable via JAWS arrow keys but not via Tab. ## Related Issue [ZAMB-27](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/ZAMB-27) ## Changes - `StackOverflow/Views/Shared/PostDisplayNotice.cshtml` — When `GetEditUrl()` returns `null` (e.g. preview contexts where `PostId = -1`), the `` tag was rendered without an `href`. An `` without `href` is not a focusable element and is skipped by Tab, but JAWS's virtual cursor can still navigate to it via arrow keys. Added `tabindex="0"` in this case to explicitly place the element in the tab order, making it reachable consistently via both Tab and arrow keys. ## WCAG Criteria **2.1.1 — Keyboard Only (Level A)** All functionality must be operable through a keyboard interface. The fix ensures the edit link is either a standard focusable link (when a valid `href` exists) or explicitly keyboard-focusable via `tabindex="0"` (when no `href` is available), eliminating the inconsistency between Tab and arrow key navigation. ## Verification Steps 1. Navigate to `/admin/flags/site-specific-close-reasons` 2. Tab through the page to a close reason row and press Enter/Space on **"Show post notices"** to expand it 3. Continue tabbing — confirm the **"Edit question"** link is now reachable via Tab 4. With JAWS: use arrow keys when the section is collapsed — confirm behaviour is consistent with Tab 5. On a live post notice (non-preview), confirm the edit link still behaves as a normal link with `href` ## Screenshots / Before & After **Before:** `Edit question` — no `href`, not Tab-focusable, but reachable via JAWS arrow keys. **After:** `Edit question` — explicitly in the tab order, consistent keyboard behaviour. --- > This PR was generated by a developer using an AI agent with the > [a11y-fix](https://github.com/StackEngLabs/stackskill/tree/main/skills/workflows/a11y-fix) skill [ZAMB-27]: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/ZAMB-27?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: so-tooling
body:
## Summary

The Teams/Enterprise Metrics Dashboard time series charts (built with Chart.js canvas elements) were not accessible to screen readers. Chart data was only available via visual hover tooltips, which screen readers cannot interact with. This fix adds visually-hidden HTML data tables as accessible alternatives for every dashboard chart, satisfying WCAG 2.1 Level A criterion 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).

**Jira**: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/A11Y-105

## What changed

- **`SingleValueChart.mod.ts`** — Added `accessibilityConfig` and `getAccessibilityDatapoints()` so the Interaction Rate, Answers, and Edits widgets now populate their screen-reader-only `<table>` with formatted data (date range, current value, previous value, benchmark).
- **`IntegrationChart.mod.ts`** — Added `accessibilityConfig` and `getAccessibilityDatapoints()` so the Questions and Searches widgets expose totals in their accessible tables.
- **`AcceptedAnswerRatioChart.mod.ts`** — Added `accessibilityConfig` and `getAccessibilityDatapoints()` so the Answer Ratio widget exposes accepted/unaccepted percentages in its accessible table.
- **`DailyVisitorsChart.mod.ts`** — Added `accessibilityConfig` and `getAccessibilityDatapoints()` so the Daily Active Users widget exposes total, contributor, and consumer counts in its accessible table.
- **`MedianTimeToAnswerChart.mod.ts`** — Updated table selector from `.js-interaction-rate-chart-accessible` to `[data-widget-role="table"]` for consistency with the template's existing semantic markup.
- **`TimeSeriesChart.mod.ts`** — Updated `renderAccessibilityChart()` to scope the table selector to the nearest `.s-card` container, preventing cross-widget contamination when using attribute selectors.
- **`TimeSeriesWidgets.mod.ts`** — Removed the manual `js-interaction-rate-chart-accessible` class addition (no longer needed).

## How to verify

1. Navigate to the metrics dashboard at `/metrics-dashboard` on a Teams or Enterprise instance.
2. Enable a screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA, or JAWS).
3. Navigate through the page — each widget's chart data should now be announced via an HTML table with:
   - A `<caption>` describing the metric (e.g., "Interaction rate over time")
   - Column headers for date range, current value, and (when trendlines are active) previous/benchmark values
   - Row headers with date ranges and corresponding metric values
4. Toggle trendlines (Off / Compare dates / Benchmarks) — the accessible tables should update to include the appropriate comparison columns.
5. Verify with an axe or Lighthouse audit that no 1.1.1 violations are reported for the chart widgets.

## Conformance

- **WCAG 2.1 Level A** — [1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content)
- **Severity**: Serious
- **Affected products**: Teams, Enterprise
title: A11Y-105: add screen reader accessible data tables to all dashboard time series charts

author: ycantu
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces AEH sign up events for SHINE. Both of these events exist in PRIZM and this is a "lift and shift" from PRIZM to AEH:
- `signup.start` - Client and server-side event
- `signup.complete` - Server-side event

#### Why not use the existing `user.signup` event?
The existing `user.signup` sign up event appears to have been created for Braze and includes `Account` as a property. `Account` in turn includes user e-mail which is "first-class" PII. 

https://github.com/StackEng/StackOverflow/blob/0e85792ff82b53adef34c7c6f22b5cdc827fd0e2/StackOverflow.Common/Models/User.Events.cs#L130-L137

I have created new events that do not contain "first-class" PII because we DO NOT want to store this data in Data Bricks. Even though the new Event Registry provides a mechanism to obfuscate this data on SELECT, I really don't think it should be stored in the first place. 

#### Implementation Notes
Sign up pages and modals in the monolith use either legacy JavaScript or Svelte islands for client-side interactivity.

For those using legacy JavaScript, I found it easiest to export the site setting to JS and use that. (`StackExchange.options.setting.signup.enableSignupProductEvents`). 

For the newer Svelte islands, the site setting is passed as a parameter. This 1) Removes dependencies on `StackExchange` namespace and, 2) makes writing tests easier since we can avoid having to mock the `StackExchange` namespace to prevent namespace not defined errors.

##### Feature Flagging
 I decided to place all this code behind a feature flag because:
 - Allows me to turn it off in the event things go sideways  
 - Prevents these events from going out to SOT/I and SOE AEH instances
 - Helps me complete testing on `main-test`

## How to Test
**IMPORTANT:** I cannot get a sign up completion on my local so I'm going to YOLO some parts of this. My plan is to enable this site setting on `main-test` and complete a few sign ups before enabling this in prod. The code is relatively straightforward. 

#### Legacy  JS
I had trouble getting breakpoints on these files in DevTools so I placed a breakpoint in `stack-events.mod.ts` and inspected the call stack to see which file was being called.

The steps below only verify we can successfully submit the event from each file rather than from each place it occurs.
We have three legacy files on JS with the new `signup.start` event:

`auth.js`
1. Visit https://localhost:7205/users/signup?ssrc=homepage_wizard&returnurl=https%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A7205 and select any of the auth options
2. It should send a `signup.start` event

`inline_auth.js`
1. I couldn't find where this is triggered so YOLO?

`21_OpenID.js`
1. Visit https://literature.stackexchange.local/questions/23448/what-aspects-of-roman-ingardens-theory-of-literature-does-stanis%c5%82aw-lem-critici and select one of the OAuth options
2. It should send a `signup.start`event

#### Svelte Islands
Beta Homepage Wizard - Only accessible via the new beta homepage
1. On the beta site https://localhost:7205 go through the beta homepage wizard and click on an OAuth option OR submit a valid e-mail and password 
2. Verify a `signup.start` event is sent to `/stackevent` 

Homepage Wizard - The original homepage wizard accessible in the classic homepage
1. Go to the classic questions page https://meta.stackexchange.local/questions and click "Home" on the left sidebar to bring up the original homepage wizard
2. Go through the beta homepage wizard and click on an OAuth option OR submit a valid e-mail and password
3. Verify a `signup.start` event is sent to `/stackevent` 

Sign up modal - Appears in both the beta site and classic homepage
1. On the beta site go to https://localhost:7205/beta/challenges and click "Start discussion" to bring up the sign up modal
2. On the sign up modal, click on an OAuth option OR submit a valid e-mail and password
3. Verify a `signup.start` event is sent to `/stackevent` 

#### Site Setting
To test the feature flag, turn off the following site setting.
https://meta.stackexchange.local/developer/site-settings/edit?name=Signup.EnableSignupProductEvents

1. Refresh the page and retry one of the tests above for the legacy JS files and verify that no call to `/stackevent` is made 
2. Refresh the page and retry on the tests above for a Svelte island and verify that no call to `/stackevent` is made
title: YETI2-900 - SHINE Signup Events `signup.start` and `signup.complete`

author: gcasar
body:

author: so-tooling
body:
## Summary

The date picker inputs (`#from` and `#to`) on the **Site Analytics** page (`/site-analytics`) use jQuery UI Datepicker, which renders a calendar popup that is completely inaccessible via keyboard. Arrow keys, Enter, and Escape have no effect on date cells, trapping focus in the text input and preventing keyboard-only users from selecting dates. This violates **WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A)**.

This PR replaces the jQuery UI Datepicker with native `<input type="date">` elements, which provide full keyboard accessibility out of the box.

**Jira**: https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/A11Y-142

## What changed

- **`Views/siteanalytics/History.cshtml`**:
  - Changed `<input type="text">` to `<input type="date">` for both `#from` and `#to` date fields
  - Updated date format from `yyyy-MMM-dd` (e.g., `2026-Mar-01`) to `yyyy-MM-dd` (e.g., `2026-03-01`), which is the format required by native date inputs
  - Removed `@HtmlUtil.IncludeJQueryUI()` since jQuery UI is no longer needed on this page
  - Updated the `init` call to pass min/max dates in `yyyy-MM-dd` format

- **`_Scripts/legacy/global/LegacyJS/site-analytics.js`**:
  - Removed jQuery UI Datepicker initialization (`$('#from').datepicker(...)`)
  - Set `min` and `max` attributes on native date inputs to enforce date range constraints
  - Replaced `$.datepicker.formatDate()` in CSV export with plain JS date formatting (no dependency on jQuery UI)
  - Simplified the `phaseDate` click handler to set values directly (dates are now already in `yyyy-MM-dd` format)

## How to verify

1. Navigate to `/site-analytics` (requires View Site Analytics privilege)
2. **Tab** to the "From" date field — should receive focus with visible focus indicator
3. The browser's native date picker should appear (varies by browser)
4. Use **Arrow keys** to navigate between date parts (month, day, year)
5. The date picker calendar (if shown) should be navigable with **Arrow keys**
6. **Enter/Space** should confirm a date selection
7. **Escape** should close any picker popup
8. **Tab** to the "To" date field and repeat verification
9. Click a phase date link (Private beta, Public beta, Graduation if shown) — should update the From field and refresh graphs
10. Test CSV download — dates should be formatted as `yyyy-MM-dd`

## Conformance

- **WCAG 2.1.1** — [Keyboard (Level A)](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html)
- **Severity**: Serious
- **Affected product**: Enterprise

**Agent run**: https://github.com/StackEng/Accessibility/actions/runs/22578188865
title: A11Y-142: replace jQuery UI datepicker with native date inputs for keyboard accessibility

body:
## Summary

Caps search and question list pagination to Elasticsearch's max_result_window (default 10,000) to prevent HTTP 400 errors when from + size exceeds the limit. Clamps page counts and total results so the pager doesn't render unreachable pages, silently redirects users requesting pages beyond the cap, and shows an info banner when results are truncated.

## How to Test

1. High page number doesn't error: Go to /search?q=javascript&page=700 and /questions/tagged/javascript?page=700 while logged in.  Both should return results on a valid page, not a 400 or 404.
2. Pager links are all reachable: Search for a broad term or browse a popular tag, navigate to the last page in the pager. It should return results, not an error.
3. No phantom last page: On /questions/tagged/javascript, verify the last pager page number is floor (10000 / pageSize) (e.g., 777 for pageSize=15), not one higher.
4. Info banner appears: When results are capped, verify "Showing the first 10,000 results. Refine your search for more specific results." appears above the pager on search, questions list, and tagged questions pages.
5. No banner for small result sets: Browse a tag with fewer than 10,000 results. No banner, normal pagination.
6. Anon cap still works: Log out, go to /search?q=javascript&page=40 should redirect per the existing 500-result anonymous cap.

body:
## Summary

The IP address links on the admin "all IPs" page (`/admin/show-user-ips/{userId}`) were rendered as `<a>` elements without `href` attributes, making them completely unreachable via keyboard. This replaces them with semantically correct `<button>` elements that are natively keyboard-focusable and properly indicate they trigger a popup.

## Related Issue

[A11Y-147](https://stackoverflow.atlassian.net/browse/A11Y-147)

## Changes

- **`StackOverflow/_Scripts/legacy/scoped/moderator/moderator.ts`** — Changed `initIpAddressLookups` to wrap IP addresses in `<button type="button" class="s-btn s-btn__link" aria-haspopup="true">` instead of `<a/>`. Updated filter guard and event binding selectors from `a` to `button`.
- **`StackOverflow/Views/Developer/AccountQueue.cshtml`** — Updated jQuery selector from `.ip-address-lookup a` to `.ip-address-lookup button` to match the new element.

## WCAG Criteria

**2.1.1 — Keyboard (Level A)**
The `<button>` element is natively keyboard-focusable and operable (Enter/Space). The `aria-haspopup="true"` attribute informs assistive technologies that activating the button opens a popup. This satisfies the requirement that all functionality be operable through a keyboard interface.

## Verification Steps

1. Navigate to `/admin/show-user-ips/<userId>` (the "all IPs" page)
2. Press Tab from the "all / week / month" filter links
3. Verify focus moves to the first IP address button in the table
4. Continue tabbing — each IP button should receive focus with a visible focus indicator
5. Press Enter or Space on a focused IP button — the info popup should appear
6. Press Escape to close the popup

author: WouterDeKort
body:
This PR upgrades `System.Data.SqlClient` to `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`.

This comes down to:
- Changing all the package references from `System.Data.SqlClient` to `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient`.
- Updating all connection strings to have `TrustServerCertificate=true`. This is a [breaking change](https://github.com/dotnet/SqlClient/blob/main/porting-cheat-sheet.md#functionality-changes) where the default value changed from true to false and since we don't have trusted certificates in production we now need this.
- Update dependencies for `StackMail`, `TagEngine`, `StackExchange.Events`, `StackExchange.Exceptional`, `AdServer.Sdk` , `StackExchange.SqlMigrator` and `StackExchange.Compliance` and some framework packages that had a transitive dependency on System.Data.SqlClient.
- Update the reflection code for the SQL timers to use the new namespaces

# How to test

## PubPlat

I deployed this PR all the way to main-prod and let it run for over an hour. I also ran various heavy scheduled routes. I found no issues.

## SOE

I deployed this PR to SEM1 and SEM2 and ran the Playwright test suite from the QA team. No issues where found.

## FBB

I deployed this PR to FBB production and let it run overnight to make sure we didn't see the issues from last time. I found no issues.
title: Upgrade System.Data.SqlClient to Microsoft.Data.SqlClient

## Summary
This PR adds several client-side events for the watched tags and homepage wizard modals. It also sends an event when an item on the interesting post list is clicked. About half of the code are tests to verify tracking.

Event samples can be found in: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RpxKDORncdq7NymJC18oUHm97rClpahpzebKjvXeQ-U/edit?tab=t.0

Notable changes include:
- The beta search popover can consume objects of any type so that we can pass additional properties that may be needed on selection (in this case `id` so we can enrich events). `getDisplayString` is added to customize the display. 
- `WatchedTagsModal.cs` has a new property `initialTagLookup` with the IDs of the user's watched and ignored tags. This dictionary is modified during add/remove actions.
- Not a fan of this but the popular tags for the homepage wizard are hard-coded. They are meant for production so not every tag has an ID locally. I have moved the hard-coded tags from the frontend to the backend so we can pass in a dictionary with the tag and it's ID to the modal.

While working on this, I figured most of these modals will not be opened on most homepage views and that we should load the data for the modals on demand so as not to perform unnecessary database calls. That is a bit of refactor and not included in this PR. 

## How to Test
You will need to setup a way to view dev AEH events. There are a few listed in this article:  https://stackoverflowteams.com/c/stack-overflow/articles/25015

To send events from your local to dev AEH set `ProductEvents.UseInMemoryStore` to `false` in `environmentsettings.Local.Public.json`.

**Homepage Wizard (Anonymous only)**
1. Opening the wizard should trigger the `homepage_wizard.open` event
2. Closing the wizard should trigger the `homepage_wizard.close` event
3. Click a popular tag and search additional tags then click next, this should trigger the `homepage_wizard.tag_step.ext` event
4. Select a theme and click next, this should trigger the `homepage_wizad.theme_step.next` event

**Watched/Ignored Tags (Logged-in only)**
1. Open the modal to trigger the `watched_tags_modal.open` event
2. Close the modal to trigger the `watched_tags_modal.close` event
3. Add or remove a watched tag to trigger the `watched_tags_modal.watched` event
4. Add or remove an ignored tag to trigger the `watched_tags_modal.ignored` event

**Interesting Post Click**
1. Click on an interesting post to trigger the `homepage.question_title_link` event
title: YETI2-900 - Events for beta homepage modals (excluding sign up)

## Summary
 When users entered a + character in the search input field on the Users and permissions page, it was being displayed as a blank space after form submission. For ' character it was convert to encoded character on the input

- Modified the finished() JavaScript function to encode + characters as %2B before sending the SearchQuery parameter to the server
- Updated the partialHref() function to properly decode URL components when processing navigation links

## How to Test
1. Go to SO Enterprise and log in with an Admin user
2. Go to "users and permissions" on Admi settings “~/users-permissions”
3. Test a search/filter by user:
   3.1 Test with an apostrophe - Search by user name
    3.2 Test with a + sign - Search by email
4. It should display correct results and show the correct character in input
